body.en: The Continental Divide runs through Montana, separating the mountains and glaciers on the west from rolling plains to the east. Much of the state is built on a bed of rock that dates back more than a billion years, to the Precambrian, or the earliest era in Earth’s history. The geology of Montana has shaped the state, from the mountain ranges to that draw hikers to Glacier and Yellowstone National Parks to mineral deposits that drew prospectors during the Gold Rush to the vast plains that have long supported hunting and agriculture.
body.zh: 大陸分水嶺穿過蒙大拿州，將西部的山脈和冰川與東部起伏的平原分開。該州的大部分地區都建在岩床上，其歷史可以追溯到十億多年前的前寒武紀，即地球歷史上最早的時代。蒙大拿州的地質塑造了這個州，從吸引徒步旅行者前往冰川和黃石國家公園的山脈，到淘金熱期間吸引探礦者的礦藏，再到長期支持狩獵和農業的廣闊平原。

body.en: Along with the rest of the Pacific Northwest, Oregon has been shaped by volcanic activity. Active volcanoes, Mount Hood among them, dominate the skyline, and the city of Portland was built atop an extinct volcano. Over tens of thousands of years, these geological hotspots have left many holes in their wakes, including deep craters, narrow canyons, and subterranean lava tubes. Here are a few of the most intriguing voids that Oregon has to offer.
body.zh: 與太平洋西北地區的其他地區一樣，俄勒岡州也受到火山活動的影響。包括胡德山在內的活火山佔據了天際線，波特蘭市建在一座死火山之上。數萬年來，這些地質熱點留下了許多洞，包括深坑、狹窄峽谷和地下熔岩管。以下是俄勒岡州提供的一些最有趣的空白。

body.en: Sure, Kitty Hawk, North Carolina, got headlines, but the Wright Brothers were Ohioans through and through. That's where they had their print and cycle shop, and established the world's first airplane factory. From Dayton's Aviation Heritage National Historical Park, to NASA's Glenn Research Center, to Congress officially declaring Ohio the “birthplace of aviation,” and much more, no other state takes to the skies and beyond like the home of the Buckeyes. Here are some of our favorite places to feel the wind beneath your wings.
body.zh: 當然，北卡羅來納州的基蒂霍克成了頭條新聞，但萊特兄弟是徹頭徹尾的俄亥俄州人。他們在那裡開設了印刷和自行車店，並建立了世界上第一家飛機工廠。從代頓的航空遺產國家歷史公園，到美國宇航局的格倫研究中心，再到國會正式宣布俄亥俄州為“航空的誕生地”，等等，沒有哪個州像七葉樹的故鄉那樣擁有天空和更廣闊的天地。這裡有一些我們最喜歡的地方，可以感受翅膀下的風。

body.en: The deep, moody forests of Washington state are filled with secrets and stories. From springy mosses to towering Douglas firs, rocky outcrops, and glacial deposits, it’s easy to see how the landscape helped set the tone for stories like David Lynch’s trippy TV series Twin Peaks and the teen vampire romance that is Twilight. Across the Evergreen State, human- and nature-made oddities are rarely far from reach.
body.zh: 華盛頓州幽深、喜怒無常的森林充滿了秘密和故事。從富有彈性的苔蘚到高聳的道格拉斯冷杉、岩石露頭和冰川沉積物，很容易看出這些景觀如何為大衛林奇的迷幻電視連續劇《雙峰》和青少年吸血鬼浪漫故事《暮光之城》等故事定下基調。在整個長青州，人為和自然造成的怪異現像很少是遙不可及的。

body.en: Yes, we know, Hawaiʻi is surrounded by water—the state is a watery wonder in and of itself. But the ocean is only the beginning. The volcanic islands' dramatic topography, unpredictable coastlines, and high rainfall mean that water in and around the Paradise of the Pacific cavorts in all sorts of stunning ways: waterfalls, blowholes, pools, and more. (Plus rainbows. Lots and lots of rainbows.) And you can enjoy all of these natural showstoppers without having to get your feet wet.
body.zh: 是的，我們知道，夏威夷四面環水——這個州本身就是一個水上奇蹟。但海洋只是一個開始。火山島奇特的地形、不可預測的海岸線和高降雨量意味著太平洋天堂及其周圍的水以各種令人驚嘆的方式湧動：瀑布、氣孔、水池等等。 （還有彩虹。很多很多的彩虹。）您無需弄濕腳即可欣賞所有這些自然美景。

body.en: For superb pizza, most people look to New York. Excellent burgers are available in every one of the 50 states. But where can you find hamburger recipes caught in the early 20th-century, cooked in steamers or served on toast with absolutely no ketchup allowed? Or, for that matter, fancy cheese made by trailblazing nuns who launched their dairying business at a time when Velveeta was still the norm? Connecticut may be an odd place to designate as a culinary cradle, but the state contains everything from the last of a generation of feminist vegetarian restaurants to what the Library of Congress dubs the very first place to have served up a hamburger. Unique culinary institutions cropped up in every corner of the state. Some have survived, while others have fallen by the wayside (R.I.P. to the Frisbie Pie Company). Here are six remarkable gastronomic institutions in a place that has proved to be fertile ground for unusual eats.
body.zh: 對於美味的披薩，大多數人都會去紐約。美國 50 個州中的每一個州都提供優質漢堡。但是，您可以在哪裡找到 20 世紀早期的漢堡食譜，用蒸籠烹煮或放在吐司上，絕對不允許使用番茄醬呢？或者，就此而言，由開創性的修女們製作的精美奶酪，她們在 Velveeta 仍然是常態的時候就開展了乳製品業務？康乃狄克州被稱為烹飪搖籃可能是一個奇怪的地方，但該州擁有從一代女權主義素食餐廳的最後一家到美國國會圖書館稱為第一個提供漢堡包的地方的一切。獨特的烹飪機構出現在該州的每個角落。有些倖存下來，而有些則半途而廢（願福里斯比餡餅公司安息）。這裡有六個非凡的美食機構，事實證明，這裡是孕育不尋常美食的沃土。

body.en: In the arid and remote expanses of New Mexico's landscape, booms and zooms abound. From the volatile effects of the Manhattan Project to the otherworldly possibilities of Roswell's UFO, the Land of Enchantment has never shied away from the controversial or far-reaching. Here are several places to encounter those legacies across this southwestern state.
body.zh: 在新墨西哥州乾旱而偏遠的土地上，轟鳴聲和爆炸聲比比皆是。從曼哈頓計畫的不穩定性影響到羅斯威爾不明飛行物的超凡脫俗的可能性，魔法之地從不迴避有爭議或影響深遠的事情。在這個西南部的州，有幾個地方可以欣賞這些遺產。

body.en: The Sunflower State has a reputation for being flat—in fact, scientists have shown that it is objectively way flatter than a pancake. Far from being featureless, though, Kansas can be mind-bending in its own weird way. Maybe it all started with The Wizard of Oz. From a missile silo that once dominated the world's LSD supply to rock formations shaped like mushrooms, roadside art that will make you think you've been whisked away by a tornado, and a giant pile of sock monkeys, Kansas is full of treasures that are sure to make you do a double take.
body.zh: 向日葵州素以平坦而聞名，事實上，科學家已經證明，它客觀上比煎餅還要平坦。然而，堪薩斯州遠非平淡無奇，它也以其獨特的方式令人費解。也許這一切都始於《綠野仙蹤》。從曾經主宰世界LSD供應的飛彈發射井，到蘑菇形狀的岩層，讓你以為自己被龍捲風捲走的路邊藝術，還有一大堆襪子猴，堪薩斯充滿了一定會讓你回味無窮的寶藏。

body.en: New York has been described as a playground for the rich and powerful, but the state's history is full of ordinary people who have overcome extraordinary struggles. What if Seneca Falls, the village that launched the fight for women's suffrage, were as famous as Niagara Falls? What if Weeksville, the historic free Black community in Brooklyn, were as well-known as Williamsburg? From immigrant sanctuaries to the Survivor Tree, here are sites where New York has shown its resilience.
body.zh: 紐約被描述為富人和權貴的遊樂場，但該州的歷史充滿了克服非凡鬥爭的普通人。如果塞內卡瀑布這個發起婦女選舉權鬥爭的村莊和尼加拉瀑布一樣出名怎麼辦？如果布魯克林歷史悠久的自由黑人社區威克斯維爾和威廉斯堡一樣出名怎麼辦？從移民庇護所到倖存者樹，紐約在這些地方展現了其韌性。

body.en: North Dakota is not quite the flattest state in the U.S., but it's pretty close. (In one analysis, it placed third, after Illinois and Florida.) During the last Ice Age, glaciers moving across the terrain had a planing effect on the land, dropping sediment that filled in any valleys, creating sprawling prairies and open, big skies. These large expanses are home to more than a few sky-high structures, both natural and human-made. From rocky peaks and multi-ton animal statues to one of the tallest buildings in the world, these are some of the most impressive structures that North Dakota has to offer.
body.zh: 北達科他州並不是美國最平坦的州，但也非常接近了。 （在一項分析中，它排名第三，僅次於伊利諾伊州和佛羅裡達州。）在上一個冰河時代，冰川在地形上移動對土地產生了刨平效應，沉積物沉積在山谷中，形成了廣闊的草原和開闊的天空。這些大片土地上有不少天然和人造的高空建築。從岩石山峰和重達數噸的動物雕像到世界上最高的建築之一，這些都是北達科他州最令人印象深刻的建築。

body.en: For about half of any given year, much of Arizona is too hot to handle. But even in peak summer, the state is home to a stunning spread of geographic diversity and a mysterious magic that emanates from the landscape—and we don’t just mean the mirages. Locals and visitors alike flock to higher altitudes, recreation-friendly bodies of water, and indoor spaces that are so heavily air-conditioned they practically require a jacket. Here are eight sheltered spots to retreat from the heat, from natural formations to an immersive art exhibit that invites lingering. We've even added a couple cool places (220 feet underground or a mile above sea level) to dream about spending the night.
body.zh: 每年大約有一半的時間，亞利桑那州的大部分地區都太熱了。但即使在夏季高峰期，該州也擁有令人驚嘆的地理多樣性和從景觀中散發出的神秘魔力——我們指的不僅僅是海市蜃樓。當地人和遊客都湧向海拔更高、適合休閒的水域和空調嚴重的室內空間，幾乎需要一件夾克。這裡有八個避暑勝地，從自然景觀到令人流連忘返的沉浸式藝術展覽。我們甚至添加了幾個涼爽的地方（地下 220 英尺或海拔 1 英里），供您夢想過夜。

body.en: A run through New York City demands a delicate balance: Zoning out versus keeping your eyes peeled. On the one hand, there’s the clear-headed, in-the-zone mental state that any good sneaker-to-pavement exercise requires. At the same time, well, it is New York City. You can hardly walk two blocks without uncovering a hidden gem or noticing some new detail that’s actually been lurking in plain sight for decades. This 5.3-mile run takes you along a scenic route to discover some of these hidden gems. You can run the entire route, break it up into multiple runs, or do it in reverse. With the right running shoes, you’re bound to pick up on one of the million tiny, fascinating details along the way.
body.zh: 穿越紐約市需要一種微妙的平衡：分心與保持警覺。一方面，任何良好的從運動鞋到路面的運動都需要頭腦清醒、專注的精神狀態。同時，嗯，這是紐約市。你幾乎不可能走兩個街區而不發現隱藏的寶石或註意到一些實際上潛伏在視線中數十年的新細節。這條 5.3 英里的跑步路線將帶您沿著風景優美的路線去發現一些隱藏的寶藏。您可以跑整條路線，將其分成多條路線，或以相反的方式進行。有了合適的跑鞋，你一定會發現一路上數以百萬計的微小而迷人的細節。

body.en: Originally named “Venice of America,” Venice, California, owes its existence to a wealthy developer’s dream of a canal-laden resort town west of Los Angeles. The dream didn’t last long: After opening in 1905, the city went broke before joining Los Angeles in 1926. The decades of neglect that followed earned Venice the nickname “the slum by the sea,” but its affordability also attracted artists, beginning with the Beats in the late ’50s. Venice’s identity as a rough-around-the-edges artist haven endures more than 60 years later, though its affordability less so. If you’re looking to plot a trek across Los Angeles pavement and beaches, zero in on Venice with a run that oscillates between fast-and-furious and slow-and-curious. Take on this 5.2-mile run in one go, break it up into multiple runs, or do it in reverse. With the right running shoes, you’ll be ready to navigate Venice’s storied past and its eternally eccentric personality.
body.zh: 加州威尼斯最初被稱為“美國威尼斯”，它的存在歸功於一位富有的開發商夢想在洛杉磯西部建立一個運河縱橫的度假小鎮。這個夢想並沒有持續太久：1905 年開放後，這座城市在 1926 年加入洛杉磯之前就破產了。隨後幾十年的忽視為威尼斯贏得了“海邊貧民窟”的綽號，但它的負擔能力也吸引了藝術家，從 20 世紀 50 年代末的垮掉派開始。威尼斯作為一個邊緣藝術家天堂的身份在 60 多年後仍持續存在，儘管它的經濟承受能力有所下降。如果您想在洛杉磯的人行道和海灘上徒步旅行，不妨以威尼斯為零，體驗一下在快速與激烈和緩慢與好奇之間搖擺的跑步。一次完成 5.2 英里的跑步，將其分成多次跑步，或反向進行。穿上合適的跑鞋，您將準備好探索威尼斯傳奇的過去及其永遠古怪的個性。

body.en: Long before California was home to tech campuses, freeways, and palm trees, Native inhabitants etched huge designs into the landscape. Even before that, at roughly the same time that the Pyramids of Giza were under construction, a tree that still survives today began taking root. And even farther into the past, glaciers and mammoths created enduring monuments to antiquity. Across the state, the distant past is still within easy reach.
body.zh: 早在加州成為科技園區、高速公路和棕櫚樹之前，原住民就已經在這片土地上刻下了巨大的設計。甚至在此之前，大約在吉薩金字塔開工的同時，一棵至今仍存活的樹開始生根發芽。即使在更遙遠的過去，冰川和猛獁像也創造了不朽的古代紀念碑。在整個州，遙遠的過去仍然觸手可及。

body.en: There’s a time-tested saying about things being large in Texas—and it certainly holds true for the state’s artworks, many of which are so huge or sprawling they could only reasonably live outdoors. Across the vast expanse of the Lone Star State are artistic testaments to some of the area’s oddest characters and stories.
body.zh: 有一句經過時間考驗的說法是，德克薩斯州的東西都是大的，這對於該州的藝術品來說當然是正確的，其中許多藝術品是如此巨大或龐大，以至於只能在戶外合理地生存。孤星州廣闊的土地上遍布著該地區一些最奇怪的人物和故事的藝術見證。

body.en: The smallest state in America is often the butt of jokes. Rhode Island is neither a road nor an island, and it was once famously parodied in the now-defunct website “How Many Rhode Islands”—a simple tool that allowed you to see just how many Rhode Islands could squeeze inside a given country. The United States could contain 3,066 Rhode Islands, and Russia could hold 5,445. But the tiny state has a rather grand history. Rhode Island was founded on the principle of religious freedom, was the first of the Thirteen Colonies to renounce its allegiance to the British Crown, and was one of only two states not to ratify the 18th Amendment, which prohibited the manufacture and sale of alcohol. Many of the state’s attractions still loom large, including a 58-foot-long blue fiberglass termite and an improbably large blue bear slumped under a lampshade.
body.zh: 美國最小的州常常成為笑柄。羅德島既不是一條路，也不是一個島嶼，它曾經在現已不復存在的網站“多少個羅德島”中被惡搞——這是一個簡單的工具，可以讓你看到一個特定的國家可以擠進多少個羅德島。美國可以控制 3,066 個羅德島，俄羅斯可以控制 5,445 個。但這個小國卻有著相當悠久的歷史。羅德島州以宗教自由原則為基礎，是十三個殖民地中第一個放棄效忠英國王室的州，也是僅有的兩個不批准禁止製造和銷售酒精的第十八修正案的州之一。該州的許多景點仍然引人注目，包括一隻 58 英尺長的藍色玻璃纖維白蟻和一隻躺在燈罩下的大得不可思議的藍熊。

body.en: Famous for country music and hot chicken, Tennessee is also filled with natural wonders. Across the state, caverns beckon. Venturing into some of Tennessee's strangest subterranean haunts is a great way to experience the depths of the state's spell-binding charm.
body.zh: 田納西州以鄉村音樂和辣雞而聞名，也充滿了自然奇觀。在全州各地，洞穴都在向您招手。冒險進入田納西州一些最奇怪的地下場所是體驗該州迷人魅力深處的好方法。

body.en: Louisiana has long had a complex relationship with the wet world. Chitimacha, Choctaw, and Atakapa peoples built communities among the knobby knees of bald cypress trees; French fur traders and pirates eventually made their own marks. Later still, modern engineers attempted to corral waters with levees and dams, or to reclaim land where there had been none. Across the 50,000-odd square miles that make up the state, troves of special places are becoming concealed by rising water. Here are seven places water has revealed or covered up.
body.zh: 路易斯安那州長期以來與潮濕的世界有著複雜的關係。奇蒂馬查人、喬克託人和阿塔卡帕人在禿柏樹的多節樹叢中建立了社區；法國毛皮商人和海盜最終留下了自己的印記。再後來，現代工程師試圖用堤防和水壩圍住水域，或是開墾原本沒有土地的土地。在該州 5 萬多平方英里的土地上，許多特殊的地方正被不斷上漲的水位所掩蓋。以下是水暴露或掩蓋的七個地方。

body.en: Michigan is famous for its steep, sweeping sand dunes, freckling of lakes, and unique fossils—but across the state, you'll find slews of automated wonders, past and present. From old animatronic toys to the ruins of early assembly lines, here are seven places to be dazzled by industry.
body.zh: 密西根州以其陡峭、廣闊的沙丘、斑點狀的湖泊和獨特的化石而聞名，但在全州各地，您會發現過去和現在的大量自動化奇蹟。從舊的電子動畫玩具到早期裝配線的廢墟，這裡有七個令人眼花繚亂的工業場所。

body.en: Here at Atlas Obscura, we have a fondness for the forbidden, a hunger for the hidden, a gusto for the grim. (You get the point.) But it wouldn’t be so intrepid to simply highlight Nevada’s underbelly, would it? There’s more to the state than extraterrestrial-themed brothels and nuclear bomb test sites. Kids and grandparents might enjoy enormous Ferris wheels, unusual geysers, or pristine parklands. Even Nevada—home to Sin City—has a family-friendly side.
body.zh: 在Atlas Obscura，我們熱愛禁忌，渴望隱藏的事物，熱愛嚴峻的事物。 （你明白了。）但是僅僅強調內華達州的軟肋也不會那麼勇敢，不是嗎？該州除了外星主題妓院和核彈試驗場之外還有更多其他東西。孩子和祖父母可能會喜歡巨大的摩天輪、不尋常的間歇泉或原始的公園綠地。即使是罪惡之城的所在地內華達州也有適合家庭的一面。

body.en: Maine is widely known for its mottled red crustaceans and stony-faced lighthouses, as well as bucolic towns and the top-notch hiking outside of them. But before all that, Maine was all about one thing: trains. As America industrialized in the 19th century, there was an insatiable demand to build and a hunger for lumber. Maine had plenty of it, and the state’s rivers became swollen with the fallen bodies of pine and spruce, much of which was hauled by rail. Trains did the heavy lifting to coastal hubs including Bangor and Ellsworth, and by 1924, there was enough railroad mileage in Maine to get from London’s King's Cross station to Mosul, Iraq. Over the years, some of the old cars were fashioned into eateries, but many were simply abandoned in the woods. Now, relics of Maine’s railroad history are scattered in museums, restaurants, and more.
body.zh: 緬因州以其斑駁的紅色甲殼類動物和石面燈塔以及田園風光小鎮和小鎮外一流的徒步旅行而聞名。但在此之前，緬因州只關心一件事：火車。隨著美國在 19 世紀工業化，對建築的需求不斷增加，對木材的需求也越來越大。緬因州有許多這樣的水，該州的河流因松樹和雲杉倒下的屍體而水位上漲，其中大部分是通過鐵路運輸的。火車承擔了前往班戈和埃爾斯沃思等沿海樞紐的重任，到 1924 年，緬因州已有足夠的鐵路里程從倫敦國王十字車站前往伊拉克摩蘇爾。多年來，一些舊汽車被改造成餐館，但許多都被遺棄在樹林裡。現在，緬因州鐵路歷史的遺跡散佈在博物館、餐廳等地方。

body.en: Picture Alaska. You might see in your mind's eye the granite and stark white snowcaps of Denali National Park, or the dark seas that surround 6,000-plus miles of coastline, or the muted olive of its tundra in the summer. But as anyone who's been there knows, the country's largest, most sparsely populated state can absolutely burst with color, from the luminous green of the Northern Lights, to the deep aqua of its glaciers, to the flourish of wildflowers fed by its long summer days. Here are some places to see the full spectrum of The Last Frontier.
body.zh: 想像一下阿拉斯加。您可能會在腦海中看到德納利國家公園的花崗岩和純白色的雪蓋，或者環繞 6,000 多英里海岸線的黑暗海洋，或者夏季苔原上柔和的橄欖色。但去過那裡的人都知道，這個國家面積最大、人口最稀少的州絕對充滿色彩，從北極光的明亮綠色，到冰川的深綠色，再到漫長夏日培育的繁茂野花。這裡有一些地方可以觀賞《最後的邊疆》的全貌。

body.en: The District of Columbia is home to a number of places that you need to flash the right ID to access. From restricted rooftops to government storage facilities and underground tunnels, the city is filled with places that are off-limits to the average visitor. What’s more, many of them are hidden within popular tourist destinations and densely populated neighborhoods—so you might catch a glimpse of them, but never get any closer. These are a few of our favorite restricted spots in D.C., and the stories behind them.
body.zh: 哥倫比亞特區有許多地方，您需要出示正確的身份證件才能進入。從受限制的屋頂到政府倉儲設施和地下隧道，這座城市充滿了普通遊客禁止進入的地方。更重要的是，它們中的許多都隱藏在熱門旅遊目的地和人口稠密的社區內，因此您可能會瞥見它們，但永遠無法靠近。以下是我們在華盛頓特區最喜歡的一些限制景點，以及它們背後的故事。

body.en: If you thought Pensacola, Florida—with its powder-white sand beaches, near-perfect weather, and fresh seafood—was just a place to soak up the sun, think again. In fact, the city and beach of the same name is the site of the first European settlement in the continental United States. Established by Spanish explorer Tristán de Luna in 1559, it was christened Panzacola, a name of Native American origin and the precursor to the city’s modern name. The destination is also the birthplace of U.S. naval aviation and is still home to a naval air station and the thousands of service members stationed there, as well as the Blue Angels, the flight squadron famous for their death-defying fighter plane stunts. This delightful coastal city is an ideal, if somewhat quirky, blend of historical sites (on land and underwater) and activities to get your adrenaline flowing.
body.zh: 如果你認為佛羅裡達州彭薩科拉擁有白色的沙灘、近乎完美的天氣和新鮮的海鮮，那麼你可能認為這裡只是一個沐浴在陽光下的地方，那麼請再想一想。事實上，同名的城市和海灘是美國大陸第一個歐洲定居點的所在地。它由西班牙探險家 Tristán de Luna 於 1559 年建立，被命名為 Panzacola，這是一個起源於美洲原住民的名字，也是這座城市現代名稱的前身。該目的地也是美國海軍航空的發源地，仍然是海軍航空站和駐紮在那裡的數千名軍人以及以玩命戰鬥機特技而聞名的藍天使飛行中隊的所在地。這座令人愉悅的沿海城市是一個理想的城市，雖然有些古怪，但它融合了歷史遺跡（陸地和水下）和讓您腎上腺素激增的活動。

body.en: A deep blanket of snow often covers New England in the winter. But there’s adventure to be found in the frozen landscape, with its steep mountains and frozen ponds—and not just for skiers and snowboarders. This route blazes a unique path through Massachusetts and New Hampshire that is filled with bright colors, bold flavors, and the legacies of pioneering thinkers.
body.zh: 冬天，新英格蘭經常被厚厚的積雪覆蓋。但在冰凍的土地上，有陡峭的山脈和冰凍的池塘，可以找到冒險的樂趣，而且不僅僅是滑雪者和單板滑雪者。這條路線開闢了一條穿越馬薩諸塞州和新罕布什爾州的獨特道路，充滿了鮮豔的色彩、大膽的風味和先驅思想家的遺產。

body.en: The people of Tucson have been eating off the land for 4,100 years. From grains to livestock to produce introduced by missionaries in the 1600s, this UNESCO City of Gastronomy is home to some of the oldest farmland in North America. What once was old is new again in The Old Pueblo where ancient flavors are found in nearly every dish — trendy to traditional.
body.zh: 圖森人民以土地為食已有 4,100 年歷史。從穀物到牲畜，再到 1600 年代傳教士引進的農產品，這座聯合國教科文組織美食之城擁有北美一些最古老的農田。在老普韋布洛，曾經古老的東西再次煥然一新，幾乎每道菜都充滿了古老的風味——從時尚到傳統。

body.en: Any travel enthusiast would be hard-pressed to open any social media channel and not see photos of Iceland, with its jaw-dropping peaks, natural hot springs, pure glaciers, northern lights and snow-covered landscapes. But the island nation’s appeal goes well beyond the well-worn paths of Reykjavik, the Golden Circle and the southern region's countryside. Travel to the untamed north along the Arctic Coast Way to discover otherworldly beauty—sans crowds—around every bend.
body.zh: 任何旅遊愛好者在打開任何社交媒體頻道時都會很難不看到冰島的照片，那裡有令人驚嘆的山峰、天然溫泉、純淨的冰川、北極光和冰雪覆蓋的景觀。但這個島國的吸引力遠遠超出了雷克雅維克、黃金圈和南部地區鄉村的陳舊道路。沿著北極海岸之路前往未開化的北部，在每個拐角處發現超凡脫俗的美景，沒有人群。

body.en: Crowds clog Edinburgh's Royal Mile, the main artery between Edinburgh Castle and Holyrood Palace. The road is dotted with stores selling Nessie trinkets and lined with bagpipers and street performers pulling off dazzling tricks. But look beyond the tartan tourist traps, and you’ll discover tucked-away gardens, remnants of the city’s medieval past, and much more.
body.zh: 人群堵塞了愛丁堡皇家大道，這是愛丁堡城堡和荷里路德宮之間的主要道路。這條路上散佈著販售尼斯湖水怪小飾品的商店，兩旁都是風笛手和街頭藝人表演令人眼花撩亂的戲法。但拋開格子呢旅遊陷阱，您會發現隱藏的花園、這座城市中世紀歷史的遺跡等等。

body.en: In 1967, 100,000 artists, activists, and hippies gathered in San Francisco’s Haight-Ashbury neighborhood for the Summer of Love. Janis Joplin and Jimi Hendrix played free concerts for fields of college dropouts, and San Francisco established itself as a countercultural capital. More than 50 years later, in a city increasingly known for Twitter and tech rather than art and activism, travelers who come on a pilgrimage are often disappointed to find expensive, skin-deep psychedelia. But if you know where to look, you’ll find a walk down Haight Street to be wonderfully weird, full of historic links to hippiedom and modern takes on the vibe.
body.zh: 1967 年，10 萬名藝術家、活動家和嬉皮士聚集在舊金山的海特-阿什伯里社區，慶祝「愛之夏」。賈尼斯·喬普林 (Janis Joplin) 和吉米·亨德里克斯 (Jimi Hendrix) 為大學輟學者舉辦了免費音樂會，舊金山也成為了反文化之都。 50 多年後，在這個越來越以 Twitter 和科技而非藝術和激進主義聞名的城市，前來朝聖的旅客往往會失望地發現昂貴的、膚淺的迷幻藥。但如果您知道去哪裡尋找，您會發現沿著海特街散步非常奇怪，充滿了嬉皮士的歷史聯繫和現代氛圍。

body.en: More than eight million diverse individuals call New York City home, and many of them share their heritage through food. Whether it’s a billiards hall that serves stellar Bhutanese fare or a mosque where Malian vendors sell snacks for just a few hours each Friday, the city offers a vast culinary landscape for those willing to explore it. Venture beyond the flashy hotspots with months-long waiting lists and you’ll find New York’s true flavor lies within the small restaurants and stands rooted in its thriving immigrant communities.
body.zh: 超過 800 萬多元化人士以紐約市為家，其中許多人透過美食分享自己的傳統。無論是提供不丹美食的撞球廳，還是馬利小販每週五隻營業幾個小時的清真寺，這座城市為願意探索的人提供了廣闊的美食景觀。走出那些等待名單長達數月的浮華熱點，您會發現紐約真正的風味在於小餐館和紮根於蓬勃發展的移民社區的小攤。

body.en: It may be famous for Mardi Gras, but New Orleans has subtle, surprising wonders on tap all year long—even in the touristy French Quarter. Around every cobblestoned corner, you’ll find historic ephemera, bits of Creole culture, environmentalism, and no shortage of spooky stories, whenever you happen to visit.
body.zh: 新奧爾良可能因狂歡節而聞名，但新奧爾良全年都有微妙、令人驚訝的奇觀——即使在旅遊勝地法國區也是如此。在每個鵝卵石鋪成的角落，只要您碰巧造訪，您都會發現歷史短暫、克里奧爾文化、環保主義，而且不乏恐怖故事。

body.en: From the street, the Metropolitan Museum of Art is hard to miss: The institution’s two-million-square-foot main building, at 1000 Fifth Avenue, spans four New York City blocks and stretches into Central Park. Inside the galleries, you’ll find thousands of objects spanning 5,000 years of world history. With so many treasures under one roof, it's inevitable that some fascinating pieces are tucked into the museum's lonelier nooks and crannies, hiding in plain sight. The next time you spend a day at the museum, keep an eye out for these overlooked wonders.
body.zh: 從街上看，大都會藝術博物館很難錯過：該機構主樓佔地 200 萬平方英尺，位於第五大道 1000 號，橫跨紐約市的四個街區，一直延伸到中央公園。在畫廊內，您會發現數千件跨越 5,000 年世界歷史的物品。由於同一個屋簷下藏有如此多的寶藏，一些迷人的收藏不可避免地被藏在博物館更偏僻的角落和縫隙中，隱藏在人們的視線中。下次在博物館度過一天時，請留意這些被忽視的奇觀。

body.en: Detroit and Nashville are synonymous with two all-American music genres. It’s no surprise that visitors flock to these cities each year to get a feel for the places where artists such as Marvin Gaye, Diana Ross & the Supremes, Johnny Cash, and Dolly Parton began their careers. A (relatively) straight, north to south route connects the two cities, as does musical heritage. Load up the RV, make sure your speaker system is in tip-top shape, and create a playlist filled with old-school Motown and Country hits. If you're not driving on the trip down south, you should be dancing.
body.zh: 底特律和納許維爾是兩個全美音樂流派的代名詞。毫不奇怪，每年遊客都會湧入這些城市，感受馬文·蓋伊、戴安娜·羅斯與至尊樂隊、約翰尼·卡什和多莉·帕頓等藝術家開始職業生涯的地方。一條（相對）筆直的從北到南的路線連接兩個城市，音樂遺產也是如此。裝載房車，確保您的揚聲器系統處於最佳狀態，並建立一個充滿老派摩城和鄉村歌曲的播放清單。如果你不開車去南方旅行，你應該跳舞。

body.en: The terrain along the Gulf of Mexico is sometimes called the “Third Coast,” but for an offbeat road trip, it’s second to none. Starting in Houston and ending in Pensacola Bay, this journey takes you through some of America’s most diverse landscapes. You’ll cross Cajun swamps, drive along sparkling white sand beaches, and even spend some time in the Big Easy. Take an RV and camp along the way to truly immerse yourself in this wondrous region. The world’s largest gulf, it turns out, holds some of America’s best-kept secrets.
body.zh: 墨西哥灣沿岸的地形有時被稱為“第三海岸”，但對於另類公路旅行來說，它是首屈一指的。從休士頓開始，到彭薩科拉灣結束，這段旅程將帶您穿越美國一些最多樣化的景觀。您將穿越卡津沼澤，沿著閃閃發光的白色沙灘行駛，甚至在 Big Easy 度過一段時間。乘坐房車沿途營地，真正沉浸在這個奇妙的地區。事實證明，世界上最大的海灣蘊藏著美國一些最保守的秘密。

body.en: The Coachella Valley and its environs boom in the spring, when tens of thousands of music lovers flock to catch their favorite artists perform in front of a dramatic, mountainous backdrop. But this region stays wonderfully weird all year long. If the festival drew you to the area and you only have a day to explore, choose a direction: Either head north, toward Joshua Tree and Landers, or southeast to the Salton Sea and nearby oases for a blissful respite. If you can spare a couple of days, lucky you—go forth and see it all.
body.zh: 在春季，科切拉山谷及其周邊地區蓬勃發展，數以萬計的音樂愛好者蜂擁而至，觀看他們最喜歡的藝術家在戲劇性的山地背景前表演。但這個地區一年四季都異常怪異。如果節日吸引您來到該地區，而您只有一天的時間來探索，請選擇一個方向：要么向北前往約書亞樹和蘭德斯，要么向東南前往索爾頓海和附近的綠洲，享受幸福的休息。如果你能抽出幾天的時間，那麼你很幸運——出去看看這一切。

body.en: Los Angeles’ Highland Park is a diverse, eclectic neighborhood that Native Americans and Latinx communities have inhabited for centuries. Celebrated for its history, art scene, ethnic diversity, and cuisine, Highland Park is filled with surprising delights that more and more people are discovering every day. Exploring the neighborhood's nooks and crannies is one of the most rewarding ways to spend a day in L.A.
body.zh: 洛杉磯的高地公園是一個多元化、不拘一格的社區，幾個世紀以來，美洲原住民和拉丁裔社區一直居住於此。高地公園以其歷史、藝術景觀、種族多樣性和美食而聞名，每天都有越來越多的人發現令人驚奇的樂趣。探索附近的角落和縫隙是在洛杉磯度過一天最有價值的方式之一。

body.en: Once referred to as “The Coney Island of the Pacific,” L.A.’s beachfront neighborhood of Venice has long been a popular tourist destination. Its colorful characters, quirky architecture, and carnivalesque atmosphere are well-known the world over. But take a moment to look past the kitsch, and you’ll discover a place where artistic ingenuity thrives more than a century after Abbot Kinney endeavored to bring a grandiose version of Venice to America. The bohemian beehive has always attracted artists and performers, and everyone is welcome to enjoy the show.
body.zh: 洛杉磯的威尼斯海濱社區曾被稱為“太平洋上的康尼島”，長期以來一直是熱門的旅遊目的地。其豐富多彩的人物、奇特的建築和狂歡節的氛圍聞名於世。但花點時間拋開庸俗，你會發現在阿博特·金尼 (Abbot Kinney) 努力將宏偉的威尼斯帶到美國一個多世紀後，這裡的藝術創造力蓬勃發展。波西米亞蜂巢一直吸引著藝術家和表演者，歡迎大家前來欣賞表演。

body.en: The 1970s brought a wave of artists into this former industrial area in Downtown Los Angeles. They sparked a fuse of creative imagination that burned for years. Up-and-coming creators took advantage of the then-low rents and built a foundation for the creative mecca that exists here today. In its infancy, L.A.’s Downtown Arts District came to life behind-the-scenes, with artists mostly working in closed studios. Today, the art has spilled onto the streets in the form of colorful murals, attractive gallery spaces, and stylish storefronts. But the curious explorer can still find literal and figurative traces of the ‘70s. In addition to the more historic spots that remain, a creative, entrepreneurial spirit abounds.
body.zh: 20 世紀 70 年代，大批藝術家湧入洛杉磯市中心這個前工業區。他們點燃了多年來燃燒的創造性想像力的導火線。嶄露頭角的創作者利用當時低廉的租金，為今天的創意聖地奠定了基礎。在其起步階段，洛杉磯市中心藝術區在幕後開始活躍起來，藝術家大多在封閉的工作室工作。如今，藝術以色彩繽紛的壁畫、迷人的畫廊空間和時尚的店面的形式蔓延到街道上。但好奇的探險家仍然可以找到 70 年代的字面和比喻痕跡。除了保留下來的歷史景點外，這裡還充滿了創造力和創業精神。

body.en: Wedged between Charing Cross and Leicester Square, Trafalgar Square is known for the throngs of people flocking to its famous attractions. Weave around the tourists on the National Gallery stairs and dodge the crowds clogging the street corners. Instead, duck down dreamy alleys and pop into unique, overlooked museums and shops. There, a secret side of this busy area waits to reveal itself.
body.zh: 特拉法加廣場位於查林十字街和萊斯特廣場之間，以其著名景點蜂擁而至的人群而聞名。在國家美術館樓梯上繞過遊客，躲避堵塞街角的人群。相反，你可以躲進夢幻般的小巷，走進獨特的、被忽視的博物館和商店。在那裡，這個繁忙地區的秘密一面正在等待揭曉。

body.en: Few cities on Earth are as well-trodden as New York–but as any intrepid traveler knows, the more you explore a place, the more wonders you find. You may not be able to discover all of these spots in a single trip, but that could be a good thing. No matter how many times you return, the city that never sleeps never ceases to surprise. Visit NYCGo to uncover more of the city’s secret spots.
body.zh: 地球上很少有城市像紐約一樣被人們所熟知，但正如任何勇敢的旅行者都知道的那樣，您對一個地方探索得越多，就會發現越多的奇蹟。您可能無法在一次旅行中發現所有這些景點，但這可能是一件好事。無論您返回多少次，這座不夜城永遠會給您帶來驚喜。造訪 NYCGo，發現更多這座城市的秘密景點。

body.en: Anchored by the Zócalo plaza and the architectural splendor of the Palacio de Bellas Artes, Mexico City's historic center rightfully draws scores of visitors from around the world. If you look, smell, and taste carefully, you’ll also find a universe of culinary offerings that tells stories of immigration, adaptation, and imagination. With the help of Culinary Backstreets, we assembled a primer on eating and drinking your way through the district.
body.zh: 墨西哥城的歷史中心以索卡洛廣場和宏偉的美術宮為中心，理所當然地吸引了來自世界各地的遊客。如果您仔細觀察、聞聞和品嚐，您還會發現一個充滿美食的世界，講述移民、適應和想像的故事。在烹飪後街的幫助下，我們編寫了一本關於在該地區飲食的入門讀物。

body.en: Hollywood Boulevard is world-famous—for the Oscars and the Walk of Fame, for schlocky souvenir shops and crowded tour buses. But beyond the terrazzo stars and the occasional celebrity sighting, there’s plenty left to discover. Here’s how to make Hollywood’s acquaintance, whether you’re a visitor or a local who keeps a practiced distance from these busy, saturated blocks. Look closer and you'll find a neighborhood full of nature, history, and wonder.
body.zh: 好萊塢大道因奧斯卡頒獎典禮和星光大道、粗劣的紀念品商店和擁擠的旅遊巴士而聞名於世。但除了水磨石星星和偶爾出現的名人之外，還有很多值得探索的地方。以下是結識好萊塢的方法，無論您是遊客還是當地人，都與這些繁忙、飽和的街區保持著一定的距離。仔細觀察，您會發現一個充滿自然、歷史和奇蹟的社區。

body.en: There's the Times Square you know, full of blazing billboards, selfie sticks, and costumed characters. Then there's the less familiar one, beyond the lights—the nooks and crannies that most visitors to Midtown Manhattan overlook. They're not obvious, but surprises can still be found along this world-famous stretch of real estate.
body.zh: 你知道，那是時代廣場，到處都是閃亮的廣告看板、自拍棒和盛裝的人物。還有一個不太熟悉的地方，那就是燈光之外的地方——大多數到曼哈頓中城的遊客都會忽略的角落和縫隙。它們並不明顯，但在這片舉世聞名的房地產中仍然可以發現驚喜。

body.en: Follow along on our 2,200-mile adventure with NPR's 'All Things Considered.'
body.zh: 跟隨 NPR 的“All Things Thought”節目一起踏上 2,200 英里的冒險之旅。

body.en: Forge your own path in this tourist magnet, toward places that are less crowded but no less wondrous.
body.zh: 在這個旅遊勝地開闢自己的道路，前往人煙稀少但同樣精彩的地方。

body.en: Find faded grandeur and vibrant street life in Argentina's largest city.
body.zh: 在阿根廷最大的城市尋找褪色的宏偉和充滿活力的街頭生活。

body.en: Just when you thought you knew the Windy City, it finds new ways to surprise you.
body.zh: 就在您以為您了解風城時，它卻以新的方式帶給您驚喜。

body.en: Find secret vistas, labyrinthine bookstores, and eclectic public art.
body.zh: 尋找秘密景觀、迷宮般的書店和不拘一格的公共藝術。

body.en: In the homeland of explorers, your best bet is to keep looking.
body.zh: 在探險家的故鄉，最好的選擇就是繼續尋找。

body.en: Go beyond the beaches in the continental United States’ only truly tropical city.
body.zh: 超越美國大陸唯一真正的熱帶城市的海灘。

body.en: New York City's most diverse borough is also its most rewarding.
body.zh: 紐約市最多元化的行政區也是最有價值的行政區。

body.en: Southern California's second city holds plenty of sparkling secrets.
body.zh: 南加州第二大城市擁有許多閃閃發光的秘密。

body.en: Find surprises around every corner in a U.S. city that embraces history like no other.
body.zh: 在這座擁有獨特歷史的美國城市的每個角落都能找到驚喜。

excerpt.en: Rippling sand dunes frozen in the Arizona rock.
excerpt.zh: 亞利桑那州岩石中凍結的沙丘起伏不定。

body.en: 190 million years ago, one of the greatest geological formations in the world began to take shape.
body.zh: 1.9億年前，世界上最偉大的地質構造之一開始形成。

body.en: In the Coyote Buttes ravine, some 5,225 feet above sea level, stands Arizona's the Wave. The Wave has a remarkable undulating appearance, with massive sandstone structures stretched like taffy and cinnamon color strata domes. It is, in a way, a geological snapshot in time, a still shot of the effect natural forces have on the environment.
body.zh: 在 Coyote Buttes 峽谷中，海拔約 5,225 英尺，矗立著亞利桑那州的 Wave。波浪具有引人注目的起伏外觀，巨大的砂岩結構像太妃糖色和肉桂色的地層圓頂一樣伸展。在某種程度上，它是一張地質快照，是自然力量對環境影響的靜態照片。

body.en: The Wave is comprised of Navajo Sandstone dunes that have calcified vertically and horizontally, turning into hardened, compacted rocks over time. The peculiar and unique fluctuating stratum was created by slow wind and rain erosion. The Wave remained basically unknown until the 1990s when it was largely advertised in German travel brochures and shown in the 1996 movie Faszination Natur. Small groups of Europeans visited the area, and its popularity grew; tour guides confide that it is still largely a European population that visits, though Americans have definitely begun to take notice of the landscape.
body.zh: 波浪由納瓦霍砂岩沙丘組成，這些沙丘已經垂直和水平鈣化，隨著時間的推移變成硬化、壓實的岩石。奇特而獨特的起伏地層是由風雨緩慢侵蝕而形成的。直到 20 世紀 90 年代，波浪基本上還是不為人所知，當時它在德國旅遊手冊中大量宣傳，並在 1996 年的電影《Faszination Natur》中放映。一小群歐洲人參觀了該地區，該地區的知名度也隨之提高。導遊坦言，儘管美國人肯定已經開始注意到這裡的風景，但遊客仍然主要是歐洲人。

body.en: Many describe walking through the dunes as an intensely strange experience, surreal and vertigo inducing, or in several cases, described as being like a drug induced walking dream. The rock is certainly a photographer's delight, where professionals and amateurs strive to take the perfect mid-day shot when not a single shadow eclipses the Wave, or they go for the more dramatic effect of morning or near-twilight that comes with the high domes casting stark shadows on the land.
body.zh: 許多人將穿越沙丘描述為一種極其奇怪的體驗，超現實且令人眩暈，或者在某些情況下，被描述為就像藥物引起的行走夢。這塊岩石無疑是攝影師的最愛，專業人士和業餘愛好者都努力在沒有任何陰影遮蓋波浪的情況下拍攝完美的中午照片，或者他們追求早晨或接近黃昏時高聳的圓頂在陸地上投下鮮明陰影的更戲劇性的效果。

body.en: While the rocks have been hardened, they are still susceptible to damage. Only 64 visitors a day are allowed to walk through the ravine, and permits are required. The permits are issued through online and in person lotteries, and tour guides are available for hire.
body.zh: 雖然岩石已經硬化，但它們仍然容易受到損壞。每天只允許 64 名遊客穿過峽谷，並且需要許可證。許可證透過網路和現場抽籤的方式發放，並且可以租用導遊。

body.en: Get more unusual and extraordinary places each week with the Atlas Obscura Places newsletter.
body.zh: 每週透過 Atlas Obscura Places 通訊了解更多不尋常和非凡的地方。

address: House Rock Road, Marble Canyon, Arizona, 86036

excerpt.en: Most-visited and most-photographed slot canyon in the American Southwest.
excerpt.zh: 美國西南部遊客最多、拍照最多的狹縫峽谷。

body.en: Frequently subject to flash floods, Antelope Canyon can only be visited through guided tours because of the extreme danger. Still, it has managed to become the most photographed and most-visited slot canyon in all of the American Southwest due to its beauty and a peculiar phenomenon of natural light beams.
body.zh: 羚羊峽谷經常遭受山洪爆發，由於極度危險，只能透過導遊遊覽。儘管如此，由於它的美麗和自然光束的奇特現象，它仍然成為美國西南部最受拍照和訪問量最大的狹縫峽谷。

body.en: Formed by millions of years of wind and water erosion, Antelope Canyon’s magnificent smooth and flowing shaped sandstone has made it one of the most famous slot canyons in the world.
body.zh: 羚羊峽谷經過數百萬年的風雨侵蝕而形成，其宏偉光滑、流動的異形砂岩使其成為世界上最著名的狹縫型峽谷之一。

body.en: Located within the LeChee Chapter of the Navajo Nation in Arizona, Antelope Canyon is actually two separate canyons, the upper canyon and lower canyon. The upper canyon, which the Navajo call Tsé bighánílíní ("the place where water runs through rocks"), is a narrow passage through 120-foot-high canyon walls. The lower canyon is known as Hazdistazí ("spiral rock arches") and is a shallower V-shaped canyon that is a more difficult trek for visitors.
body.zh: 羚羊峽谷位於亞利桑那州納瓦荷族的勒奇部落內，實際上是兩個獨立的峽谷，上峽谷和下峽谷。上峽谷被納瓦霍人稱為 Tsé bighánílíní（「水流過岩石的地方」），是一條穿過 120 英尺高的峽谷壁的狹窄通道。較低的峽谷被稱為 Hazdistazí（“螺旋岩拱門”），是一個較淺的 V 形峽谷，對遊客來說徒步難度更大。

body.en: Get more unusual and extraordinary places each week with the Atlas Obscura Places newsletter.
body.zh: 每週透過 Atlas Obscura Places 通訊了解更多不尋常和非凡的地方。

body.en: Your newsletter subscriptions with us are subject to Atlas Obscura's Privacy Policy and Terms of Use .
body.zh: 您向我們訂閱的電子報須遵守 Atlas Obscura 的隱私權政策和使用條款。

body.en: Both upper and lower canyons are only accessible by guided tour which are pretty expensive. Also, pets are not allowed anywhere in the park, including service animals! Tripods are not allowed, unless on a photography tour, which comes with a surcharge. To properly film the light beams, a sturdy tripod and a wide-angle lens are highly recommended.
body.zh: 上峽谷和下峽谷都只能透過導遊遊覽，價格相當昂貴。此外，園區內任何地方都不允許攜帶寵物，包括服務性動物！不允許使用三腳架，除非是參加額外收費的攝影之旅。為了正確拍攝光束，強烈建議使用堅固的三腳架和廣角鏡頭。

excerpt.en: This secluded aqua waterfall in the Grand Canyon is the perfect swimming hole, and the Havasupai tribe's fiercely protected natural wonder.
excerpt.zh: 大峽谷中這個僻靜的水瀑布是完美的游泳洞，也是哈瓦蘇派部落嚴密保護的自然奇觀。

body.en: The Grand Canyon draws in over five million tourists each year and is hailed as one of the Seven Natural Wonders of the World. But hidden deep within a side canyon, on the reservation of the local Havasupai tribe, completely surrounded by Grand Canyon National Park and so not really in a National Park, lies something lesser-known to tourists yet unparalleled in beauty: Havasupai Falls.
body.zh: 大峽谷每年吸引超過 500 萬遊客，被譽為世界七大自然奇觀之一。但隱藏在側峽谷深處，在當地哈瓦蘇派部落的保留地，完全被大峽谷國家公園包圍，因此並不是真正的國家公園，隱藏著一些鮮為遊客所知但美麗無與倫比的東西：哈瓦蘇派瀑布。

body.en: The Havasupai people, which literally translates to “people of the blue-green water,” are native to a region of northern Arizona that’s home to Havasupai Falls, a group of aquamarine waterfalls tucked within the Havasu Canyon. The most famous is Havasu Falls, a stunning cascade that almost looks like it flows with liquid turquoise. Yet despite the inescapable crowds of the Grand Canyon, these beautiful falls are relatively secluded, a long-guarded secret of the Havasupai tribe and a small handful of outsiders.
body.zh: 哈瓦蘇派人的字面意思是“藍綠色水域的人”，原產於亞利桑那州北部的一個地區，該地區是哈瓦蘇派瀑布的所在地，哈瓦蘇峽谷內有一組碧綠色的瀑布。最著名的是哈瓦蘇瀑布，這是一個令人驚嘆的瀑布，看起來幾乎流淌著液態綠松石。然而，儘管大峽谷的人群不可避免，這些美麗的瀑布卻相對僻靜，是哈瓦蘇派部落和少數外來者長期保守的秘密。

body.en: This secrecy is largely a result of the tribe’s understandable reluctance to fully open the gates of their homeland to tourists. Of the tribal nations affiliated with the Grand Canyon area, the Havasupai are the only ones who continue to live deep within the canyon. The Havasupai consider themselves the keepers and guardians of the Grand Canyon.
body.zh: 這種保密很大程度上是由於該部落不願意向遊客完全開放家園的大門，這是可以理解的。在隸屬於大峽谷地區的部落民族中，哈瓦蘇派是唯一繼續生活在峽谷深處的民族。哈瓦蘇派人認為自己是大峽谷的守護者和守護者。

body.en: They’ve set up a system of camping permits that only lets a small portion of applicants into the village of Supai, where the falls are located. Even if you’re lucky enough to get the permit, you have to be able to shell out for the helicopter ride, horse ride, or mule ride to assist you in getting there. Otherwise, you’ll have to hike 10 miles there and 10 miles back. It’s a hot, dry, strenuous although beautiful hike, passing red rocks, cacti, and ancient pictograms along the way.
body.zh: 他們建立了一個露營許可證系統，只允許一小部分申請者進入瀑布所在的蘇派村。即使您有幸獲得許可證，您也必須能夠支付乘坐直升機、騎馬或騎騾子的費用來幫助您到達那裡。否則，您將不得不徒步 10 英里到那裡並返回 10 英里。這是一次炎熱、乾燥、艱苦但美麗的徒步旅行，沿途經過紅色的岩石、仙人掌和古老的象形文字。

body.en: Once there, the views from the 100-foot Havasu Falls are priceless. It’s also a daredevil’s dream; visitors have the opportunity to attempt high cliff jumps and swim to a rocky shelter behind the falls, both of which are extremely risky. And as if one aquamarine waterfall wasn’t enough, there are four more in the area. Near Havasu Falls lie Mooney, Navajo, Supai, and Beaver Falls, each beautiful and awe-inspiring in its own way.
body.zh: 到達那裡後，100 英尺高的哈瓦蘇瀑布的景色是無價的。這也是勇敢者的夢想；遊客有機會嘗試懸崖跳高和游到瀑布後面的岩石庇護所，這兩者都非常危險。好像一個海藍寶石瀑布還不夠，該地區還有四個。哈瓦蘇瀑布附近有穆尼瀑布、納瓦霍瀑布、蘇派瀑布和海狸瀑布，每個瀑布都以自己的方式美麗而令人驚嘆。

body.en: The reason for the picturesque turquoise color is the high levels of calcium carbonate in the spring-fed waters of Havasu Creek, the source of the five waterfalls. These high levels also create 70-degree travertine pools at the base of some of the falls, making them the perfect swimming holes.
body.zh: 之所以呈現如畫的綠松石色，是因為哈瓦蘇溪的泉水中碳酸鈣含量很高，哈瓦蘇溪是五個瀑布的源頭。這些高水位還在一些瀑布的底部形成了 70 度的石灰華水池，使其成為完美的游泳洞。

title.en: Yayoi Kusama Firefly Infinity Mirror Room
title.zh: 草間彌生螢火蟲無限鏡房

excerpt.en: The installation’s official name, “You Who Are Getting Obliterated in the Dancing Swarm of Fireflies,” says it all.
excerpt.zh: 裝置的官方名稱「在螢火蟲跳舞的群體中被抹殺的你」就說明了一切。

body.en: The 89-year-old Japanese avant-garde artist Yayoi Kusama is finally getting her due as one of the greatest living artists in the world.
body.zh: 89 歲的日本前衛藝術家草間彌生 (Yayoi Kusama) 終於成為世界上最偉大的在世藝術家之一。

body.en: Having moved to New York just in time for the exploding avant-garde art movement of the 1960s, Kusama was known for her wild “happenings.” She staged large events featuring nude people covered in polka dots, opened a nude painting studio and social club, and once wrote a letter to Richard Nixon offering to have vigorous sex with him if he stopped the Vietnam War.
body.zh: 草間彌生搬到紐約，恰逢 20 世紀 60 年代前衛藝術運動的爆發，她以其狂野的「事件」而聞名。她舉辦了大型活動，以全身覆蓋圓點的裸體為主題，開設了裸體繪畫工作室和社交俱樂部，並曾寫信給理查德·尼克松，提出如果他停止越南戰爭，就與他發生激烈的性行為。

body.en: Yet despite being a darling of New York’s counterculture art scene, Kusama was largely forgotten after moving back to Japan in 1973 for health issues, where she voluntarily took up residence in a hospital for the mentally ill.
body.zh: 然而，儘管草間彌生是紐約反主流文化藝術界的寵兒，但在 1973 年因健康問題回到日本後，她自願住在精神病院，之後基本上被遺忘了。

body.en: Kusama never stopped making art, but it wasn’t until the early 1990s that her work began to gain international recognition once again. It has been on a steady upward climb since. Working from the hospital, she sold a piece of artwork in 2008 for $5.1 million, setting a record for the highest price paid to a living female artist.
body.zh: 草間彌生從未停止藝術創作，但直到 20 世紀 90 年代初，她的作品才開始再次獲得國際認可。此後，它一直在穩步上升。 2008年，她在醫院工作時以510萬美元的價格出售了一件藝術品，創下了在世女藝術家的最高售價記錄。

body.en: Fans can now once again experience Kusama’s wild and wonderful work in person, at an installation appropriately entitled “You Who Are Getting Obliterated in the Dancing Swarm of Fireflies.” Installed permanently at the Phoenix Art Museum, the piece uses a 25-foot square space with mirror-lined walls, flooring of polished black granite, a black plexiglass ceiling, and 250 dangling LED lights programmed with alternating color. The effect is ethereal and expansive. Like much of Kusama’s work, your sense of self, space, and time are overwhelmed and nearly obliterated by visual force.
body.zh: 粉絲們現在可以再次親身體驗草間彌生狂野而精彩的作品，在一個名為“在螢火蟲群舞中被抹殺的你”的裝置中。作品永久安裝在鳳凰城藝術博物館，使用 25 英尺見方的空間，牆壁為鏡面，地板為拋光黑色花崗岩，天花板為黑色有機玻璃，還有 250 個顏色交替的懸掛 LED 燈。效果空靈廣闊。就像草間彌生的大部分作品一樣，你的自我感、空間感和時間感被視覺力量壓倒，幾乎被抹殺。

excerpt.en: A sharp bend in a dramatic river canyon cut through red rocks.
excerpt.zh: 戲劇性的河流峽谷中的急轉彎切穿了紅色的岩石。

body.en: After a short hike from U.S. Route 89 just south of Page, Arizona, one can safely peer from a high ledge down into one of America's great natural wonders: a sharp bend in the Colorado River cut 1000 feet deep into the red-rock plateau over millions of years. This is a world-class example of what geologists call an entrenched meander, eroded by the river on its way downstream to Grand Canyon.
body.zh: 從亞利桑那州佩吉以南的美國 89 號公路出發，徒步一小段距離後，人們可以安全地從高處俯瞰美國最偉大的自然奇觀之一：科羅拉多河的一個急轉彎，在數百萬年的時間裡切入了 1000 英尺深的紅岩高原。這是一個世界級的例子，地質學家稱之為根深蒂固的河曲，在河流下游到大峽谷的過程中受到侵蝕。

body.en: An accessible path leads about three-quarters of a mile from the parking area ($10 per vehicle; National Park Passes not accepted) to a viewing platform with sturdy railings. Beyond the viewing platform, the rim remains open to the sheer drop, and visitors should tread with caution. Be sure to dress for desert conditions and carry water. Pets are permitted if on leash, and toilet facilities are available at the parking area but not on the trail.
body.zh: 一條無障礙道路從停車場（每輛車 10 美元；不接受國家公園通行證）延伸約四分之三英里，到達帶有堅固欄桿的觀景台。在觀景台之外，邊緣仍然對陡峭的落差開放，遊客應小心行走。一定要穿適合沙漠條件的衣服並攜帶水。允許攜帶寵物，但需拴著皮帶，停車場設有廁所設施，但步道上不提供廁所設施。

body.en: Located along U.S. Route 89, just a short drive south of Page, AZ. The city of Page charges $10 per vehicle to park in the lot next to the trailhead. National Park Passes are not valid for access to the parking area.
body.zh: 位於美國 89 號公路沿線，距離亞利桑那州佩奇以南僅一小段車程。佩吉市將每輛車停放在步道起點旁的停車場收費 10 美元。國家公園通票不適用於進入停車場。

body.en: Facebook590576781

excerpt.en: Situated 90 feet off the valley floor is one of the first monuments protected by the Antiquities Act.
excerpt.zh: 距離谷底 90 英尺，是第一批受《古物法》保護的古蹟之一。

body.en: Thanks to Theodore Roosevelt, the United States Congress passed the Antiquities Act of 1906, giving the office of the president the power to create National Monuments. Although that ability has changed by legislation over time, Teddy bullishly took on the task and picked the first monuments that same year, including Montezuma Castle in Camp Verde, Arizona.
body.zh: 感謝西奧多·羅斯福，美國國會通過了 1906 年《古物法》，賦予總統辦公室創建國家紀念碑的權力。儘管隨著時間的推移，立法改變了這種能力，但泰迪樂觀地接受了這項任務，並在同年挑選了第一批紀念碑，包括亞利桑那州坎普維德的蒙特蘇馬城堡。

body.en: This cliff dwelling is remarkably intact for a structure nearly a thousand years old, and naming the site for Montezuma reveals an error in the early archeology of the site: It wasn’t built by Aztecs, but by the indigenous Sinagua, the pre-Columbian people who lived in the Verde Valley of central Arizona.
body.zh: 這座懸崖住宅對於擁有近一千年歷史的建築來說非常完好，將遺址命名為「蒙特祖瑪」揭示了該遺址早期考古學中的一個錯誤：它不是由阿茲特克人建造的，而是由土著西納瓜人建造的，他們是居住在亞利桑那州中部維德山谷的前哥倫布時期的人。

body.en: Like an early apartment building, the structure is comprised of five stories and 20 rooms, built in a natural cave in the nearly vertical limestone cliff face. Rising 90 feet from the valley floor, it could only be accessed by ladders, which, when pulled away, provided safety for the tribe from any intruder—man or beast—with unsavory motives.
body.zh: 與早期的公寓大樓一樣，該建築由五層樓和 20 個房間組成，建在近乎垂直的石灰岩懸崖面的天然洞穴中。它距離谷底 90 英尺高，只能通過梯子進入，拉開梯子後，可以為部落提供安全，使其免受任何懷有不良動機的入侵者（人或獸）的侵害。

body.en: There was a time when visitors were permitted inside to have a look around, but limestone is soft, and thousands of stomping feet are destructive, so within a few years of its protected status as a National Monument, the public was kept out, in order to preserve it. But even from down below, it’s an extraordinary site.
body.zh: 曾經有一段時間，遊客被允許進去參觀一下，但石灰岩很軟，數千次的跺腳會造成破壞，所以在其成為國家紀念碑的保護地位的幾年內，為了保護它，公眾被禁止進入。但即使從下面看，它也是一個非凡的地方。

address: Montezuma Castle Road, Yavapai County, Arizona

excerpt.en: A self-built castle made by a mysterious man.
excerpt.zh: 由神秘人建造的自建城堡。

body.en: Mystery Castle was built by Boyce Luther Gulley over a 15-year period. The mystery in Mystery Castle, is what compelled Gulley to abandon his job, wife, and his one-year-old daughter and set off to build the castle.
body.zh: 神秘城堡由博伊斯·路德·古利 (Boyce Luther Gulley) 歷時 15 年建造。神秘城堡中的謎團迫使格利放棄工作、妻子和一歲的女兒，開始建造這座城堡。

body.en: Gully disappeared altogether for three years before turning up in Phoenix and beginning work on the castle. The Castle is said to be held together by a combination of mortar, cement, and goat milk, and built from a wide range of materials including stone, adobe, automobile parts, salvaged rail tracks, and telephone poles. Despite having 18 rooms, 13 fireplaces, and numerous parapets, until recently, the castle had no running water or electricity.
body.zh: 格利完全消失了三年，然後才出現在鳳凰城並開始建造城堡。據說這座城堡是由砂漿、水泥和羊奶組合而成，並由多種材料建造而成，包括石頭、土坯、汽車零件、回收的鐵軌和電線桿。儘管擁有 18 個房間、13 個壁爐和眾多護牆，但直到最近，城堡還沒有自來水或電力。

body.en: In 1945, Gulley's abandoned wife and daughter received a call from a lawyer. They learned of Gulley's recent death, the first they had heard of Gulley since his disappearance, and of the castle he had built, which was now rightfully theirs.
body.zh: 1945年，格利被遺棄的妻子和女兒接到了律師的電話。他們得知格利最近去世了，這是他們自他失踪以來第一次聽說格利，以及他建造的城堡，現在它理所當然地屬於他們了。

body.en: Gulley's daughter, who died in 2010, lived in the castle and gave tours with her granddaughter for many years.
body.zh: 格利的女兒於 2010 年去世，多年來她一直住在城堡裡，並與孫女一起遊覽。

body.en: Update January 2025: According to Mystery Castle's website , tours have been suspended until further notice.
body.zh: 2025 年 1 月更新：根據神秘城堡網站，遊覽已暫停，直至另行通知。

excerpt.en: In a 345-million-year-old cave that's 200 feet underground, dinner awaits.
excerpt.zh: 在地下 200 英尺的一個擁有 3.45 億年歷史的洞穴中，晚餐正在等待著。

body.en: To get to this restaurant, you'll need to take an elevator. You'll be taking it down—21 stories down—into a 345-million-year-old cave network that stretches 60 miles to the Grand Canyon.
body.zh: 要到達這家餐廳，您需要搭乘電梯。您將深入 21 層樓，進入一個擁有 3.45 億年歷史的洞穴網絡，該網絡綿延 60 英里直至大峽谷。

body.en: Walter Peck first stumbled upon the cave in 1927 on his way to a poker game. He mistook the iron oxide and selenite crystals for gold and diamonds, and bought the surrounding 800 acres, though he may have been better served just playing poker. “What it all adds up to is we have one of the largest quantities of the most worthless material in Arizona,” tour guide Ron Pritchard told Arizona Highways TV , "but it's fun to look at."
body.zh: 1927 年，沃爾特·佩克 (Walter Peck) 在去打撲克的路上第一次偶然發現了這個洞穴。他將氧化鐵和亞硒酸鹽晶體誤認為黃金和鑽石，並購買了周圍的 800 英畝土地，儘管他可能只玩撲克會得到更好的服務。導遊 Ron Pritchard 告訴亞利桑那高速公路電視台：“這一切加起來就是我們擁有亞利桑那州數量最多、最無價值的材料之一，但看起來很有趣。”

body.en: The space is now known as Grand Canyon Caverns, where visitors can explore the cave's sprawling innards and, as of recently, stop for a bite while they're at it. Known as the Caverns Grotto, the four-table eatery offers simple American comfort food that makes a not-so simple voyage to your table. Cooked at ground level, the food takes the elevator back down to the cave before it's hoisted on a pulley 25 feet in the air to the raised wooden platform that is the dining room. With unobstructed, 360-degree views of the largest known chamber in the cave network and zero sound interference aside from other diners, it's an incomparable auditory and visual dining experience.
body.zh: 這個空間現在被稱為大峽谷洞穴，遊客可以在那裡探索洞穴廣闊的內部結構，最近還可以停下來吃點東西。這家四桌餐廳被稱為 Caverns Grotto，提供簡單的美式休閒食品，讓您的餐桌之旅變得不那麼簡單。食物在地面煮熟，然後乘電梯返回洞穴，然後用滑輪吊到 25 英尺高的空中，到達升高的木製平台，即餐廳。可以暢通無阻地 360 度欣賞洞穴網絡中已知最大的房間，並且除了其他食客之外零聲音幹擾，這是一種無與倫比的聽覺和視覺用餐體驗。

body.en: A decades-old mummified bobcat speaks to the fact that it is a "dead cave." Without running water or sunlight, no bacteria (or any living organisms for that matter) can subsist in these depths, which means no creepy crawlies to worry about while you wine and dine. It's cave eating at its finest.
body.zh: 一隻幾十年前的木乃伊山貓講述了一個事實：這是一個「死亡洞穴」。如果沒有自來水或陽光，細菌（或任何與此相關的生物體）就無法在這些深處生存，這意味著您在喝酒吃飯時無需擔心令人毛骨悚然的爬蟲。這是最好的洞穴飲食。

body.en: lukefater
body.zh: 路克法特

address: Grand Canyon Caverns, AZ-66, Peach Springs, Arizona, 86434

excerpt.en: This 4,000-foot-diameter hole is touted as "the most well known, best preserved meteorite crater on Earth."
excerpt.zh: 這個直徑 4,000 英尺的洞被譽為「地球上最著名、保存最完好的隕石坑」。

body.en: About 50,000 years ago, a meteorite came screaming from the sky and slammed into the Earth. The scar it left across the Arizona landscape is now a popular tourist attraction, complete with wreckage from daredevil pilots that flew too low.
body.zh: 大約五萬年前，一顆隕石呼嘯著從天而降，砸向地球。它在亞利桑那州留下的傷痕現在已成為一個受歡迎的旅遊景點，其中充滿了飛得太低的大膽飛行員的殘骸。

body.en: While it's known simply as "Meteor Crater" to most, scientists refer to it as "Barringer Crater" after Daniel Barringer, the man who first suggested that the giant hole was made by a flying space rock. Barringer was a mining engineer, and his business, Standard Iron Company, staked claim on the property. In 1903, along with his partner, mathematician and physicist Benjamin Chew Tilghman, Barringer conducted land surveys and collected documentation supporting his meteor theory. Despite his efforts, he was met with skepticism and disbelief from the scientific community.
body.zh: 雖然大多數人簡稱為“流星隕石坑”，但科學家將其稱為“巴林傑隕石坑”，以丹尼爾·巴林傑（Daniel Barringer）的名字命名，丹尼爾·巴林傑是第一個提出這個巨大的洞是由飛行的太空岩石形成的人。巴林格是一名採礦工程師，他的公司標準鋼鐵公司對這片土地擁有所有權。 1903 年，巴林格與他的搭檔、數學家和物理學家本傑明·週·蒂爾曼 (Benjamin Chew Tilghman) 一起進行了土地調查並收集了支持他的流星理論的文件。儘管他做出了努力，但他還是遭到了科學界的懷疑和不信任。

body.en: Planetary science didn't mature enough for geologists to swallow Barringer's impact theory until the '50s and '60s. A discovery of the minerals coesite and stishovite, which only occur when quartz-bearing rocks are severely shocked by an instantaneous overpressure, supported all of Barringer's findings. Unfortunately, Barringer died in 1929 and was never vindicated in life. Eugene M. Shoemaker, who discovered the minerals, was given credit as the man who uncovered the first unarguable proof of extraterrestrial impact.
body.zh: 直到 1950 年代和 1960 年代，行星科學還沒有成熟到足以讓地質學家接受巴林格的撞擊理論。柯石英和石英礦物的發現支持了巴林格的所有發現，這種礦物只有在含石英岩石受到瞬間超壓嚴重衝擊時才會出現。不幸的是，巴林傑於 1929 年去世，生前從未得到平反。這些礦物的發現者尤金·M·舒梅克 (Eugene M. Shoemaker) 被譽為第一個發現外星撞擊的無可爭議證據的人。

body.en: Those visiting the Meteor Crater should keep their eyes out for the plane wreckage said to still be visible after an ill-fated attempt in 1964 to buzz the crater's rim, ending in a fiery crash that seriously injured a pair of commercial pilots. Both men survived, and the wreckage of the Cessna 150 was left in the crater, perhaps as a cautionary visual aid to other daredevils that found the geological oddity hard to resist.
body.zh: 那些參觀流星隕石坑的人應該留意飛機殘骸，據說在 1964 年一次不幸的撞擊隕石坑邊緣的嘗試之後，飛機殘骸仍然清晰可見，最終導致一場激烈的墜機事故，導致兩名商業飛行員嚴重受傷。兩人都倖存下來，塞斯納 150 的殘骸被留在火山口中，也許是為了向其他發現難以抗拒地質怪異現象的冒險者提供警示性的視覺輔助。

excerpt.en: See massive fossils that are over 200 million years old in northeastern Arizona.
excerpt.zh: 在亞利桑那州東北部觀賞距今超過 2 億年的巨大化石。

body.en: Straddling the border between Navajo County and Apache County in the far northeastern corner of Arizona, the Petrified Forest National Park is about 146 square miles in size. The northern part of this site extends into the Painted Desert; the entire thing was declared a National Park in 1962, more than five decades after it was first named a National Monument in 1906.
body.zh: 石化森林國家公園橫跨亞利桑那州東北角的納瓦霍縣和阿帕奇縣之間的邊界，面積約 146 平方英里。該遺址的北部延伸至彩繪沙漠；整個公園於 1962 年被宣佈為國家公園，距離 1906 年首次被命名為國家紀念碑已經過去了 50 年多。

body.en: Known for its fossils, especially those of fallen trees that first grew during the Late Triassic period of the Mesozoic Era more than 225 million years ago, the Petrified Forest is in a region that was once near the equator on the southwestern edge of the supercontinent Pangaea. Back then, its climate was humid and sub-tropical. The sediments that contain the fossilized logs are park of the colorful and widespread Chinle Formation, from which the Painted Desert first got its name.
body.zh: 石化林以其化石而聞名，尤其是那些最早生長於 2.25 億多年前中生代晚三疊紀時期的倒下樹木化石，石化林位於盤古大陸西南邊緣曾經靠近赤道的地區。當時，氣候濕潤，屬於亞熱帶氣候。含有化石原木的沉積物是色彩繽紛、分佈廣泛的欽利地層的公園，彩繪沙漠最初由此得名。

body.en: There are no overnight spots or campgrounds available in the park, but nearby communities offer motels and other accommodations that visitors use. Overnight parking is not allowed, either, unless you have a wilderness hiking permit and are backpacking through the park.
body.zh: 園區內沒有過夜地點或露營地，但附近的社區提供汽車旅館和其他住宿供遊客使用。也不允許過夜停車，除非您有荒野健行許可證並且在公園裡背包旅行。

body.en: Sightseeing options are offered for private motorcycles, automobiles, and hikers. The park road, turn-outs, and parking lots are big enough to accommodate large recreational vehicles such as tour buses and traditional RVs.
body.zh: 為私人摩托車、汽車和健行者提供觀光選擇。公園道路、岔路和停車場足夠大，可以容納旅遊巴士和傳統房車等大型休閒車輛。

excerpt.en: Eons ago, a rushing lava river formed this pristine passage through solid rock.
excerpt.zh: 億萬年前，一條湍急的熔岩河穿過堅固的岩石形成了這條原始通道。

body.en: Lava does weird things. When it flows from a volcano or some other fiery leak in the Earth's crust, its surface cools and hardens in the open air, but a viscous molten core continues to flow beneath and through that outer shell. This leads to the formation of fascinating geological phenomena like rippling lava fields, artistic lava spirals and decorative lava ropes.
body.zh: 熔岩會做一些奇怪的事情。當它從火山或地殼中的其他火熱洩漏流出時，其表面在露天冷卻並硬化，但黏性熔融核心繼續在外殼下方流動並穿過外殼。這導致了迷人的地質現象的形成，如波紋熔岩場、藝術熔岩螺旋和裝飾性熔岩繩。

body.en: Of all these intriguing curiosities, most interesting for adventurers is surely the lava tube — long, cave like passages underground, arching in a near-perfect circle so ideal for traveling through, one might think they were man-made. These caves were formed millennia ago as the outside of a giant lava flow hardened, but a still-liquid center traveled through it like an underground river. Until the river stopped, leaving behind a circular tube unlike any other naturally-formed subterranean cave.
body.zh: 在所有這些令人著迷的好奇心中，對冒險家來說最有趣的肯定是熔岩管——長長的、像洞穴一樣的地下通道，呈近乎完美的圓形拱形，非常適合穿越，人們可能會認為它們是人造的。這些洞穴是幾千年前形成的，當時巨大的熔岩流的外部變硬了，但仍然液態的中心像地下河一樣穿過它。直到河流停止，留下了一個與其他自然形成的地下洞穴不同的圓形管道。

body.en: One such tube is the Coconino Lava River Cave in the Coconino National Forest, near Flagstaff, Arizona. The cave is massive – big enough for a person to walk through with dozens of feet overhead – and features the striking, telltale circumference of a lava tube. Spelunkers won't find stalactites or stalagmites decorating this hall of echoes – just the smooth arch formed by liquid-hot rock as it traveled through.
body.zh: 其中之一就是位於亞利桑那州弗拉格斯塔夫附近的可可尼諾國家森林的可可尼諾熔岩河洞。這個洞穴很大，足夠一個人在幾十英尺高的地方穿過，並且具有引人注目的熔岩管週長。洞穴探險者不會發現裝飾這個迴聲大廳的鐘乳石或石筍——只有液態熱岩石在穿過時形成的光滑拱門。

body.en: The unexpectedly smooth surface area can actually be hazardous, as the difference in temperature between the cool subterranean cave and the hot desert above ground is so great, condensation often forms and makes the walls and floors of the Lava River Cave very slick.
body.zh: 出乎意料的光滑表面區域實際上可能是危險的，因為涼爽的地下洞穴和炎熱的地面沙漠之間的溫差如此之大，經常形成凝結並使熔岩河洞穴的牆壁和地板非常光滑。

body.en: Coconino's Lava River Cave isn't the only lava river cave in the world, nor is it the largest even though it stretches for more than a mile through solid rock. But one extremely notable feature that continues to fascinate visitors and geologists alike is the unique "Y-intersection" deep within the tunnel, at which two massive tubes combine into one, creating a unique Y-shape out of three identical tubes. This leads to a dizzying mirror effect that can sometimes be disorienting to inexperienced explorers.
body.zh: 科科尼諾的熔岩河洞穴不是世界上唯一的熔岩河洞穴，也不是最大的，儘管它在堅硬的岩石中綿延一英里多。但一個極其顯著的特徵仍然讓遊客和地質學家著迷，那就是隧道深處獨特的“Y 形交叉點”，兩根巨大的管道合二為一，用三個相同的管道形成了獨特的 Y 形。這會導致令人眼花撩亂的鏡子效應，有時會讓沒有經驗的探險者迷失方向。

body.en: "The cave has also historically been referred to as "Government Cave" due to its location on the eastern edge of Government Prairie and southeast of Government Peak. Today, Lava River Cave is freely accessible to the general public." (Wiki) Many people in the area still use the historic name.
body.zh: “該洞穴歷史上也被稱為“政府洞穴”，因為它位於政府草原的東部邊緣和政府峰的東南部。如今，熔岩河洞穴向公眾免費開放。” （維基）該地區的許多人仍然使用這個歷史名稱。

excerpt.en: A reproduction of earth's many biomes.
excerpt.zh: 地球上許多生物群落的再現。

body.en: With dreams of colonizing Mars, Ed Bass, a multi-millionaire Texas oilman, funded the building of Biosphere 2 in the middle of the Arizona desert. (Planet Earth is Biosphere 1.) The 3.15-acre sealed glass house is a dazzling attempt to completely recreate the conditions and environment of Earth including a rain forest, desert, marsh, and a mini-ocean.
body.zh: 德州億萬富翁石油商艾德巴斯 (Ed Bass) 懷抱著殖民火星的夢想，資助在亞利桑那州沙漠中部建造生物圈 2 號。 （地球是生物圈 1。）這座佔地 3.15 英畝的密封玻璃屋是一次令人眼花繚亂的嘗試，旨在完全重現地球的條件和環境，包括雨林、沙漠、沼澤和迷你海洋。

body.en: In September 1991, seven crew members walked into Biosphere 2, which was sealed behind them. They were charged with the task of growing their own food and conducting environmental experiments while sealed for two years inside the complex.
body.zh: 1991年9月，7名船員走進生物圈2號，生物圈2號在他們身後被封印。他們的任務是自己種植食物並進行環境實驗，同時將其封閉在建築群內兩年。

body.en: What started as a science experiment turned into a psychological experiment. The body masses of the scientists fell over time, as did the biosphere's oxygen levels. "Confined environment psychology" set in. Crew members grew to despise each other and found conflict in even the smallest decisions. The media and scientific community criticized the two-year, $150-million-dollar experiment, calling it "tamper-prone" and a "stunt."
body.zh: 一開始的科學實驗變成了心理實驗。隨著時間的推移，科學家的體重不斷下降，生物圈中的氧氣水平也隨之下降。 「密閉環境心理學」開始出現。船員們逐漸互相鄙視，甚至在最小的決定中也發現了衝突。媒體和科學界批評了這項為期兩年、耗資 1.5 億美元的實驗，稱其「容易被篡改」和「噱頭」。

body.en: The crew stayed in Biosphere 2 for the full two years, but when they emerged, their experiment was largely dismissed as a scientific failure. It was, from a monetary perspective, a total disaster. Despite this discouraging news, a second crew entered in April of 1994 and exited prematurely in September of the same year as the management of Biosphere 2 dissolved. Both the high idealism of its founding and the ignominy of its abandonment call to mind the Garden of Eden.
body.zh: 船員們在生物圈二號待了整整兩年，但當他們出現時，他們的實驗在很大程度上被認為是科學失敗。從貨幣角度來看，這完全是一場災難。儘管有這個令人沮喪的消息，第二批工作人員還是於 1994 年 4 月進入，並於同年 9 月隨著生物圈 2 號管理解散而提前退出。它成立時的崇高理想主義和廢棄它的恥辱都讓人想起伊甸園。

body.en: Unused for many years, the facility was bought by the University of Arizona in 2007 and is now the home of many university experiments and educational programs. Visitors can now take a tour of the now non-sealed biosphere and learn about the over 3,500 exotic species growing in the dome, as well as the experiments currently taking place in it - none of which involve living inside the dome.
body.zh: 該設施多年來未使用，於 2007 年被亞利桑那大學購買，現在是許多大學實驗和教育計畫的所在地。遊客現在可以遊覽現已非密封的生物圈，了解圓頂內生長的 3,500 多種外來物種，以及目前在其中進行的實驗 - 這些實驗均不涉及圓頂內的生活。

excerpt.en: An homage to everyone's favorite prehistoric cartoon family.
excerpt.zh: 向每個人最喜歡的史前卡通家庭致敬。

body.en: Update as of August 2020: The park is now known as Raptor Ranch and has maintained much of its original Bedrock decor.
body.zh: 截至 2020 年 8 月的更新：該公園現在被稱為猛禽牧場，並保留了大部分原始的基岩裝飾。

body.en: Bedrock City is a Flintstones-themed amusement park and campground that will have you screaming, “Yabba dabba doo!" if you were a fan of the cartoon.
body.zh: 基岩城是一個以摩登原始人為主題的遊樂園和露營地，會讓您尖叫“Yabba dabba doo！”如果你是這部漫畫的粉絲。

body.en: Since 1973, Bedrock City has made it possible for park-goers to see what life was like for everyone's favorite Stone Age family. For Flintstones rookies, there is a small rock movie theatre they can watch a Flintstone cartoon to catch up. Besides the homes of Fred & Wilma, Barney & Betty, there is also a small train, a schoolhouse, and the dinosaur slide that mimics the brontosaurus Fred slides off when it is quitting time at the quarry. In addition to Bedrock City's more standard amenities, such as the campground and park area, visitors can also eat at Fred's Diner, which serves up Flintstones-inspired Bronto Burgers and Chickasurus Dinners, and spend money at the gift shop, which sells stuffed dinosaurs, postcards, and T-shirts with Fred's face on them.
body.zh: 自 1973 年以來，基岩城讓公園遊客有機會了解大家最喜歡的石器時代家庭的生活。對於《摩登原始人》的新手來說，這裡有一個小型搖滾電影院，他們可以觀看《摩登原始人》卡通片來追趕。除了弗雷德和威爾瑪、巴尼和貝蒂的家外，還有小火車、校舍，以及模仿雷龍的恐龍滑梯，弗雷德在採石場下班時會滑下來。除了基岩城的露營地和公園區等更標準的設施外，遊客還可以在 Fred's Diner 用餐，那裡提供受摩登原始人啟發的 Bronto 漢堡和 Chickasurus 晚餐，還可以在禮品店花錢，那裡出售毛絨恐龍、明信片和印有 Fred 頭像的 T 卹 晚餐。

body.en: In 2015, longtime owner Linda Speckels put Bedrock City up for sale. After having owned and operated the park for more than 40 years, Speckels, now in her mid-70s, cited her desire to retire as her primary reason for selling. The 30-acre property is currently priced at $2 million.
body.zh: 2015 年，長期業主 Linda Speckels 將基岩城掛牌出售。在擁有並經營該公園 40 多年後，現年 70 多歲的斯佩克爾表示，自己想要退休是出售公園的主要原因。這處佔地 30 英畝的房產目前售價為 200 萬美元。

body.en: This place is a great stop after you have seen the Grand Canyon and are driving that long stretch of desolate highway back to civilization.
body.zh: 當您參觀完大峽谷並開車經過漫長的荒涼高速公路返回文明世界後，這個地方是一個很棒的停留地。

body.en: Update As of January 2019: This site is closed.
body.zh: 截至 2019 年 1 月更新：網站已關閉。

excerpt.en: Ancestral Puebloan ruins, natural arches, and box canyons abound in this seldom-visited corner of Monument Valley Navajo Tribal Park.
excerpt.zh: 紀念碑谷納瓦荷部落公園中這個人跡罕至的角落，遍布普韋布洛祖先遺址、天然拱門和箱型峽谷。

body.en: Relatively unknown, moderately physically demanding, and inaccessible to unaccompanied visitors, Mystery Valley is a lightly trafficked but a thoroughly intriguing stretch of desert.
body.zh: 神秘谷相對不為人所知，體力要求適中，無人陪伴的遊客無法進入，是一片人跡罕至但非常迷人的沙漠。

body.en: Featuring graceful geological formations, petroglyphs, scattered artifacts, and breathtaking views of wide open spaces and the spectacular buttes of neighboring (and more famous) Monument Valley Tribal Park, this hidden gem provides a unique opportunity for a guided tour among ancient Indigenous ruins.
body.zh: 這個隱藏的寶石擁有優美的地質結構、岩畫、散落的文物，以及廣闊的開放空間和鄰近（更著名的）紀念碑谷部落公園的壯觀山峰的壯麗景色，為您提供了一個獨特的機會，可以在導遊的帶領下遊覽古代土著遺址。

body.en: Geologists believe that the now sun-dried valley was once completely underwater. The remarkable formations are the work of millions of years of slow erosion by wind and water. Mystery Valley, along with much of the American southwest, was once home to the Ancestral Puebloan people (from roughly 100 B.C. to 1300 A.D.) Around 500 years ago — after the Ancestral Puebloans departed from the area, leaving empty settlements and everyday items behind — the Diné (Navajo) tribe descended from northwestern Canada and settled in Mystery Valley and much of the surrounding territory. To this day, Mystery Valley belongs to the Diné and is under their tribal law, and is accessible to visitors only when accompanied by a Diné guide.
body.zh: 地質學家認為，現在被陽光曬乾的山谷曾經完全被淹沒在水下。這些非凡的構造是數百萬年風和水的緩慢侵蝕的結果。神秘谷以及美國西南部的大部分地區曾經是普韋布洛人祖先的家園（大約從公元前 100 年到公元 1300 年）。大約 500 年前，普韋布洛祖先離開該地區，留下空蕩蕩的定居點和日常用品後，迪內（納瓦霍）部落從加拿大西北部下降，定居在神秘谷和周邊大部分地區。直到今天，神秘谷仍屬於迪內族並受他們的部落法管轄，遊客只有在迪內族導遊的陪同下才能進入。

body.en: While exploring Mystery Valley, one cannot help but feel the immense amount of time that has shaped it. It is a cosmic place of strange red rock formations that, but for a scattering of desert plants, often resembles a Martian landscape. Exploring the ancient ruins of Ancestral Puebloan settlements, and gazing at petroglyphs that look like they could have been scratched into the sandstone yesterday, you can hear the echo of the ancient people who once called this valley home.
body.zh: 在探索神秘谷時，人們會情不自禁地感受到塑造它的巨大時光。這是一個充滿奇怪紅色岩層的宇宙地方，如果沒有零散的沙漠植物，通常類似於火星景觀。探索普韋布洛祖先定居點的古代遺址，凝視那些看起來像是昨天刻在砂岩上的岩畫，您可以聽到曾經以此山谷為家的古代人們的迴聲。

label.en: 'Once Upon a Time in the West' Filming Location

excerpt.en: Witnessing the might of this desert waterfall is a rare, powerful treat.
excerpt.zh: 目睹這個沙漠瀑布的威力是一種罕見而強大的享受。

body.en: At 185 feet tall, the Grand Falls is taller than many of its more well-known cousins, including the famous Niagara Falls. For much of the year, however, the river descends the falls at a rather underwhelming trickle. But if you time your visit right, you can witness the falls in their full thundering glory.
body.zh: 大瀑布高 185 英尺，比許多著名的瀑布還要高，包括著名的尼加拉瀑布。然而，在一年中的大部分時間裡，河流以相當平淡的細流從瀑布流下。但如果您的訪問時間正確，您可以親眼目睹瀑布的雷鳴般的輝煌。

body.en: The falls are a real natural wonder. Over 100,000 years ago, a volcanic eruption at Merriam Crater sent lava flowing toward the Little Colorado River. The molten rock cooled in the riverbed and created a natural dam, forcing the river to carve a new path. This created the tiers that formed the Grand Falls.
body.zh: 瀑布是真正的自然奇觀。十萬多年前，梅里亞姆火山口的火山爆發使熔岩流向小科羅拉多河。熔岩在河床冷卻並形成天然水壩，迫使河流開闢新的路徑。這就形成了形成大瀑布的層層。

body.en: Like many waterways in the deserts of the American southwest, the Little Colorado River's flow varies wildly based on the season and the weather, as the source of most of its water is snowmelt from the White Mountains.
body.zh: 與美國西南部沙漠中的許多水道一樣，小科羅拉多河的流量因季節和天氣而異，因為其大部分水源來自懷特山脈的融雪。

body.en: As the river flows from these mountains to the Grand Canyon, a farther 70 miles downstream from the falls, it collects brown and red sand and silt from the sandstone along its route, which gives the river its distinct color. As such, an apt nickname for the Grand Falls is "Chocolate Falls."
body.zh: 當河流從這些山脈流向距離瀑布下游 70 英里的大峽谷時，它從沿途的砂岩中收集了棕色和紅色的沙子和淤泥，使河流呈現出獨特的顏色。因此，大瀑布的一個恰當的暱稱是「巧克力瀑布」。

body.en: Most of the year, by the time the river gets to the Grand Falls, it barely even looks like a stream. But for a few weeks in the spring after snow in the mountains begins to melt, and after seasonal monsoons in the late-summer, the falls roar to life.
body.zh: 一年中的大部分時間，當河流到達大瀑佈時，它看起來幾乎不像一條溪流。但在春季的幾週內，山上的積雪開始融化，夏末的季節性季風過後，瀑布又恢復了生機。

body.en: Update: The falls have been closed until further notice by tribal decree .
body.zh: 更新：瀑布已關閉，直至部落法令進一步通知。

excerpt.en: An arsenic-filled pool in the Grand Canyon takes on the appearance of a giant, overflowing pumpkin.
excerpt.zh: 大峽谷中的一個充滿砷的水池呈現出一個巨大的、溢出的南瓜的外觀。

body.en: The Grand Canyon's Pumpkin Spring almost looks like an inviting place for a soak, but in reality, contains the most poisonous water in the canyon.
body.zh: 大峽谷的南瓜泉看起來像是個誘人的泡澡場所，但實際上，裡面含有峽谷中最毒的水。

body.en: The unique limestone formation has taken the shape and color of a large, round, festive pumpkin, deposits creating a fibrous “vegetable” appearance, and the gourd's distinctive downward stripes. Water pours into the top of the pumpkin, turns a caustic, murky green, and then runs over the sides and into the river below.
body.zh: 獨特的石灰岩結構具有大而圓的喜慶南瓜的形狀和顏色，沉積物形成纖維狀“蔬菜”外觀，以及葫蘆獨特的向下條紋。水流入南瓜的頂部，變成腐蝕性的暗綠色，然後流過南瓜的側面，流入下面的河流。

body.en: While the pool may appear to be full of mineral-rich, hot springs goodness, and the pumpkin-shaped bowl seems hypnotically inviting, the warm waters are a witch's brew of lead, zinc, copper, and very high levels of arsenic . While limited exposure is not fatal, it's clearly not suggested. Testing has shown that one liter of water from Pumpkin Springs contains 1100 milligrams of the infamous toxin. Bathing in the water is not suggested, and drinking it is strictly prohibited, as well as extremely foolish.
body.zh: 雖然池子看起來充滿了富含礦物質的溫泉精華，南瓜形狀的碗似乎具有催眠般的吸引力，但溫暖的水是鉛、鋅、銅和砷含量非常高的女巫釀造的。雖然有限的接觸並不致命，但顯然不建議這樣做。測試表明，南瓜泉的一公升水含有 1100 毫克這種臭名昭著的毒素。不建議洗澡，更嚴禁飲用，也是極度愚蠢的行為。

body.en: While it's ill-advised to touch, the Pumpkin Spring is one of the many beautiful stops along the winding Colorado River that should definitely be observed, appreciated, and photographed.
body.zh: 雖然不建議觸摸，但南瓜泉是蜿蜒的科羅拉多河沿岸眾多美麗的景點之一，絕對值得觀察、欣賞和拍照。

excerpt.en: This diner has been slinging sodas and egg creams since the 1930s.
excerpt.zh: 這家餐廳自 20 世紀 30 年代以來一直供應蘇打水和蛋奶油。

body.en: There aren’t many shops as old as MacAlpine's that still stand in the desert city of Phoenix, Arizona. The diner's selection of classics includes malts, phosphates, egg creams , and more. With an array of syrups, diners can also choose from a menu of more than 99 soda flavors at the vintage soda fountain. Anything from pickle to bubblegum to red velvet is fair game.
body.zh: 在亞利桑那州的沙漠城市鳳凰城，像麥卡爾派恩一樣古老的商店並不多。用餐者的經典選擇包括麥芽、磷酸鹽、蛋奶油等等。老式冷飲櫃提供多種糖漿，食客還可以從超過 99 種蘇打水口味的菜單中進行選擇。從泡菜到泡泡糖到紅色天鵝絨，任何東西都可以。

body.en: The destination opened as Birch's 7th Street Pharmacy in the late 1920s, changing hands from various owners until it landed on Fred MacAlpine in 1938. MacAlpine's operated as a full-service pharmacy and soda fountain until 1991. While the drugs have been replaced by a food menu, the soda fountain, counter, and malt machine are original. The current owner even left a piece of history stuck beneath the counter: Bubblegum covers the underside, offering a sticky relic of the greasers and pink ladies who once shared malted milkshakes and egg creams at the same counter.
body.zh: 該目的地於 1920 年代末以 Birch's 7th Street Pharmacy 開業，幾經易主，直到 1938 年落腳 Fred MacAlpine。直到 1991 年，MacAlpine's 一直作為一家提供全方位服務的藥房和冷飲店運作。雖然藥物已被食品菜單取​​代，但冷飲櫃、櫃檯和麥芽機還是原來的。現任老闆甚至在櫃檯下面留下了一段歷史：泡泡糖覆蓋了櫃檯的底面，提供了曾經在同一個櫃檯共享麥芽奶昔和蛋奶油的加油工和粉紅女士的粘稠遺跡。

body.en: Today, waitresses offer meals to diners in wooden booths, guests select old tunes from a jukebox, and shoppers peruse vintage decor and a hodgepodge of antiques in the attached space next door. If it all sounds a bit overwhelming, just start tasting sodas with reckless abandon. You'll be jitterbugging with the best of ’em in no time.
body.zh: 如今，女服務員在木製包廂裡為食客提供餐點，客人從自動點唱機中選擇老曲子，而購物者則在隔壁的附屬空間中細細品味復古裝飾和各種古董。如果這一切聽起來有點難以承受，那就開始肆無忌憚地品嚐蘇打水吧。您很快就會與他們中最優秀的人一起玩吉特舞。

body.en: MacAlpine's is open for lunch on Friday, Saturday, and Sunday.
body.zh: MacAlpine's 每週五、週六和週日供應午餐。

body.en: rachelrummel
body.zh: 雷切爾魯梅爾

excerpt.en: A stealthy Apache hideaway that became the haunting site of a mass grave.
excerpt.zh: 一個阿帕契人的秘密藏身處，後來變成了一個令人難以忘懷的亂葬崗。

body.en: In 1878, a group of Apache raiders attacked a Navajo encampment near the Little Colorado river. Almost every Navajo man, woman, and child was killed in the raid. When the Apache finished looting the encampment, only three girls remained and they were swiftly taken prisoner by the Apache.
body.zh: 1878 年，一群阿帕契襲擊者襲擊了小科羅拉多河附近的納瓦霍營地。幾乎所有納瓦霍男人、女人和兒童都在襲擊中喪生。當阿帕契人洗劫完營地後，只剩下三個女孩，她們很快就被阿帕契人俘虜了。

body.en: When the Navajo leaders got word of this attack, they sent out a team of 25 men to avenge the fallen encampment. They tracked the Apache across the land and blocked the borders to the region. However their efforts failed and the trails went cold, disappearing into the river and volcanic cinder.
body.zh: 當納瓦霍領導人得知這次襲擊的消息後，他們派出一支由 25 人組成的小隊去為陷落的營地報仇。他們追蹤阿帕奇穿過這片土地並封鎖了該地區的邊界。然而他們的努力失敗了，小路變冷了，消失在河流和火山灰中。

body.en: News arrived that another nearby Navajo encampment had been raided, which meant that the Apache were still in the area. Scouts were deployed again, two of whom were sent to check the short arm of Canyon Diablo. The scouts had found nothing until they were startled by a blast of hot air from underground. Upon further investigation, the scouts discovered that the hot air was coming from an Apache campfire in an underground cavern beneath them, large enough to house both the Apache raiding party and their horses.
body.zh: 有消息稱附近的另一個納瓦霍營地遭到襲擊，這意味著阿帕奇人仍在該地區。偵察兵再次出動，其中兩人被派去檢查暗黑破壞神峽谷的短臂。偵察兵什麼也沒發現，直到他們被地下吹來的一股熱氣嚇了一跳。經過進一步調查，偵察兵發現熱空氣來自他們下方地下洞穴中的阿帕奇篝火，該洞穴大到足以容納阿帕奇襲擊隊和他們的馬匹。

body.en: The scouts returned with news of their discovery, and the Navajo came back with a vengeance. After killing two watchmen, they gathered up the dry sagebrush and driftwood on the canyon floor and started a fire at the entrance of the cave. Now aware of the attack as smoke billowed into their hideaway, the Apache slit the throats of their horses and used what was left of their water to put out the flames, doing their best to seal off the entrance with corpses of their former mounts.
body.zh: 偵察兵帶著他們的發現的消息回來了，納瓦荷人帶著復仇的心回來了。殺死兩名看守人後，他們收集了峽谷地面上的乾山艾樹和浮木，並在洞口生火。現在，當濃煙滾滾進入他們的藏身處時，阿帕奇人意識到了這次襲擊，他們割斷了馬匹的喉嚨，用剩下的水來撲滅火焰，並盡最大努力用以前坐騎的屍體封鎖了入口。

body.en: A lone Apache man escaped from the fiery barrier and begged for mercy. The Navajo proposed the customary payment of goods and stock in exchange for forgiveness, and the Apache man agreed. However, when the Navajo asked about the three girls who had been captured, the Apache spokesman hesitated, confirming the Navajos' worst fears: The girls had already met their end.
body.zh: 一名孤獨的阿帕奇人從火焰屏障中逃脫並乞求憐憫。納瓦荷人提議按照慣例支付貨物和庫存以換取寬恕，阿帕契人同意了。然而，當納瓦霍人詢問被俘虜的三名女孩時，阿帕奇發言人猶豫了，證實了納瓦霍人最擔心的事情：女孩們已經完蛋了。

body.en: Enraged, the Navajo shot into the cave and added more fuel to the fire. Smoke and the sound of the Apache singing death songs filled the air. When the songs faded and the smoke cleared, the Navajo broke through the charred barrier of horse corpses. They retrieved their goods, and stripped off the valuables of the 42 Apaches who had suffocated inside of the cave.
body.zh: 憤怒的納瓦荷人衝進洞穴，火上加油。空氣中瀰漫著煙霧和阿帕契人唱著死亡之歌的聲音。當歌聲漸漸消散，煙霧散去時，納瓦荷人衝破了馬屍體燒焦的屏障。他們取回了貨物，並搶走了在洞穴內窒息而死的 42 名阿帕奇人的貴重物品。

excerpt.en: This historic national park is covered in the stunning ruins of red rock pueblos.
excerpt.zh: 這座歷史悠久的國家公園遍布令人驚嘆的紅岩村遺址。

body.en: Surrounded by Arizona's scenic desert vistas, the Native American ruins at Wupatki National Monument are some of the most beautiful and well-preserved examples of pueblo architecture in the country.
body.zh: 烏帕特基國家紀念碑 (Wupatki National Monument) 的美洲原住民遺址周圍環繞著亞利桑那州風景如畫的沙漠景觀，是該國最美麗、保存最完好的普韋布洛建築典範之一。

body.en: Covering an area of about 40,000 acres (along with two other national monument areas), the grounds are home to a number of surprisingly preserved pueblo ruins. Dating back as far as 500 CE, the site probably saw the largest group of people living here, around 100 or so, soon after the nearby eruption of what is now Sunset Crater, around the late 11th century. Because of the volcanic ash and subsequent nutrients, agriculture boomed in the 12th century. The structures were likely abandoned by 1225.
body.zh: 該場地佔地約 40,000 英畝（連同另外兩個國家紀念碑區），擁有許多保存完好的普韋布洛遺址。早在西元 500 年，該遺址可能就見證了最大的人群居住在這裡，大約有 100 人左右，大約在 11 世紀末，附近現在的日落火山口噴發後不久。由於火山灰和隨後的養分，農業在 12 世紀蓬勃發展。這些建築很可能在 1225 年就被廢棄了。

body.en: While excavations and studies have been taking place since the 1800s, the remains of dozens of homes and buildings still stand on the site. While other examples of pueblos from the time can be found elsewhere, it is rare to find so many in one area, and so well preserved as well. Even if you aren't into the history of the site, the sheer beauty of the old ruins is shouldn't be missed. Especially if you are able to catch them around sunset. While they have not been inhabited for centuries, they still seem haunting.
body.zh: 儘管自 1800 年代以來一直在進行挖掘和研究，但該遺址上仍然矗立著數十座房屋和建築物的遺跡。雖然在其他地方也能找到當時的普韋布洛的其他例子，但在一個地區發現如此之多且保存如此完好的情況是很少見的。即使您不了解該地點的歷史，也不應該錯過古老遺址的純粹之美。特別是如果您能夠在日落時分捕捉到它們。雖然它們已經有幾個世紀無人居住了，但它們似乎仍然令人難以忘懷。

body.en: The Wupatki National Monument provides a bit more bang for your pueblo buck than most sites in the Southwest. Whether they are just passing through or they are there to check out the hundreds of years of history, visitors will find the site worthwhile.
body.zh: 烏帕特基國家紀念碑比西南部的大多數景點都更划算。無論他們只是路過還是為了了解數百年的歷史，遊客都會發現這裡值得一去。

excerpt.en: The Magical World of George Phar Legler.
excerpt.zh: 喬治法爾萊格勒的魔法世界。

body.en: In the 1920s, a man named George Legler began a massive project... to create a world of fantasy and imagination that sought to carry with it a message of kindness and peace to all visitors.
body.zh: 1920 年代，一位名叫喬治·萊格勒 (George Legler) 的人開始了一項龐大的計畫……創造一個充滿幻想和想像力的世界，力求向所有遊客傳遞友善與和平的信息。

body.en: Legler initially worked as a postal clerk, but soon found his life consumed by his desire to spread his message to all that would listen. He purchased the land for the Moon in 1917, and with the help of a couple of close friends, began the laborious endeavor of transforming the desert into a magical landscape of winding paths, stone towers and walls, and hidden grottoes. Throughout the following years, he expanded constantly on the construction while giving tours with the aid of friends and local children under the pseudonym of "The Mountain Gnome".
body.zh: 萊格勒原本是一名郵政職員，但很快就發現他的生活被他向所有願意傾聽的人傳播訊息的願望所消耗。 1917 年，他為月球購買了這片土地，並在幾個親密朋友的幫助下，開始了艱苦的努力，將沙漠變成了蜿蜒小路、石塔和牆壁以及隱藏石窟的神奇景觀。在接下來的幾年裡，他不斷擴大建設規模，同時在朋友和當地孩子的幫助下以「山地侏儒」的筆名進行遊覽。

body.en: Legler grew too ill to continue giving tours by 1967, and the Moon fell into disrepair. Fortunately, a group of Catalina high school students jumped the fence and befriended the ailing artist. Soon after, they took over maintenance and preservation of the site, and their organization (now known as the George Phar Legler Society) still maintains the Moon today.
body.zh: 到 1967 年，萊格勒病得太重，無法繼續進行遊覽，月球也年久失修。幸運的是，一群卡塔琳娜高中生跳出了柵欄，與這位生病的藝術家成為了朋友。不久之後，他們接管了該地點的維護和保護，他們的組織（現在稱為喬治法爾萊格勒協會）至今仍在維護月球。

body.en: Due largely to the fact that the Moon is run and maintained by a very small group of devoted volunteers, the events calendar at the site is often sporadic and variable, so it's best to check their calendar for chances to visit. Productions are scheduled in the spring, as well as a Halloween and Christmas show, and they are available to host private events.
body.zh: 很大程度上由於月球是由一小群忠誠的志願者運行和維護的，因此該地點的活動日曆通常是零星且可變的，因此最好檢查他們的日曆以獲取訪問機會。製作計劃於春季進行，還有萬聖節和聖誕節演出，並且可以舉辦私人活動。
