excerpt.en: Thousands of Mexican Free-Tailed Bats soar around an abandoned storm drain at sunset each summer.
excerpt.zh: 每年夏天日落時分，成千上萬的墨西哥無尾蝙蝠在廢棄的雨水渠周圍翱翔。

body.en: Who knew Batman's summer home was in the center of Phoenix ? Though the tall masked vigilante will remain elusive, this flood control tunnel offers an incredible (and free!) opportunity to view thousands of Mexican Free-Tailed bats.
body.zh: 誰知道蝙蝠俠的避暑別墅位於鳳凰城中心？儘管高大的蒙面治安維持者仍然難以捉摸，但這條防洪隧道提供了一個令人難以置信（而且免費！）的機會來觀看數千隻墨西哥無尾蝙蝠。

body.en: Every year from May to October approximately 10,000 to 20,000 bats flock to Phoenix on their migration south to Mexico . During the day, they gather within the “cave” to rest and sleep. But at night, they emerge and fill the sky.
body.zh: 每年五月至十月，約有 10,000 至 20,000 隻蝙蝠湧向菲尼克斯，向南遷徙至墨西哥。白天，他們聚集在「洞穴」內休息和睡覺。但到了晚上，它們就會出現並充滿天空。

body.en: The bats start to leave the storm drain just before dusk and continue into the night. It’s incredible to watch them whirl through the air, flapping around while they dive after insects. Stand quietly, and you can listen to them squeak and chirp as they embark upon their hunt. They don't seem to be afraid of people, so don't be surprised is they zoom right by you, mere inches away.
body.zh: 蝙蝠在黃昏前開始離開雨水渠，一直持續到夜晚。看著它們在空中旋轉、拍打翅膀、潛入水中追捕昆蟲，真是令人難以置信。靜靜地站著，你可以聽到它們開始狩獵時發出的吱吱聲和嘰嘰喳喳的聲音。它們似乎並不害怕人類，所以當它們從您身邊飛過，只有幾英寸遠時，請不要感到驚訝。

body.en: The bat cave is a hidden gem within Phoenix. It can be hard to find, making this chance to witness so many bats at once a special treat for those who are in the know. There are a few signs from the Arizona Game and Fish Department around the area to educate the public on these creatures and encourage quiet viewing behavior.
body.zh: 蝙蝠洞是鳳凰城內一顆隱藏的寶石。蝙蝠很難找到，對於那些了解情況的人來說，有機會同時目睹如此多的蝙蝠是一種特殊的享受。該地區周圍有亞利桑那州狩獵和魚類部門的一些標誌，以向公眾宣傳這些生物並鼓勵安靜的觀看行為。

excerpt.en: Founded by members of the Tohono O’odham Nation, this one-room joint's James Beard–winning fry bread is light as a cloud.
excerpt.zh: 這家單人餐廳由 Tohono O’odham Nation 的成員創立，其榮獲詹姆斯·比爾德 (James Beard) 大獎的炸麵包輕盈如雲。

body.en: In 1992, Cecelia Miller, a member of the Tohono O'odham Nation, opened a restaurant in Phoenix, Arizona. The shop was humble, a one-room eatery filled with the clatter of a lunchtime crowd, and it was run by an all–Native American staff. It served up straight comfort food: fry bread. Fluffy as a feather, crackly with bubbles from the fryer and slicked with grease, this Native American treat is made with white flour, baking powder, salt, and shortening . At The Fry Bread House, it's made into their signature Indian Tacos, folded and filled with chorizo, lettuce, and cheese, or sweetened with butter, sugar, and chocolate for dessert.
body.zh: 1992 年，Tohono O'odham 民族的成員塞西莉亞·米勒 (Cecelia Miller) 在亞利桑那州鳳凰城開設了一家餐廳。這家商店很簡陋，是一家只有一間房間的小餐館，午餐時擠滿了人群的喧鬧聲，經營者全是美國原住民。它提供直接舒適的食物：炸麵包。這種美洲原住民美食由白麵粉、泡打粉、鹽和起酥油製成，蓬鬆如羽毛，帶有油炸鍋中的氣泡和光滑的油脂。在 The Fry Bread House，它被製作成他們的招牌印度玉米餅，折疊起來並填入香腸、生菜和奶酪，或者用黃油、糖和巧克力加甜作為甜點。

body.en: Fry bread has a conflicted legacy in Native Nations of the American Southwest. People like the Tohono O'odham didn't traditionally eat white wheat flour and shortening, and there's an active debate over when and how fry bread entered their diet. One story traces the origins of the bread to the U.S. government's forced migration of Navajo people from Fort Defiance, in what is now Arizona, to Bosque Redondo, in what is now New Mexico. In this version, fry bread was a creative use of unhealthy government rations of flour and lard. Other Native historians, however, claim that fry bread wasn't a starvation food at all, but a 20th-century luxury food, developed when Native people in the Southwest transitioned from traditional foods to commercially available foods such as white flour .
body.zh: 油炸麵包在美國西南部的原住民族中有著矛盾的遺產。像 Tohono O'odham 這樣的人傳統上不吃白小麥粉和起酥油，關於油炸麵包何時以及如何進入他們的飲食存在著激烈的爭論。有一個故事將這種麵包的起源追溯到美國政府強迫納瓦霍人從迪法恩斯堡（現在的亞利桑那州）遷移到博斯克雷東多（現在的新墨西哥州）。在這個版本中，炸麵包是對不健康的政府配給的麵粉和豬油的創造性利用。然而，其他原住民歷史學家聲稱，炸麵包根本不是一種飢餓食品，而是一種 20 世紀的奢侈食品，是西南部原住民從傳統食品轉向白麵粉等商業食品時發展起來的。

body.en: Either way, fry bread is now commonly served at powwows and other Native cultural events and festivals, particularly in the Southwest. For some Native people, it symbolizes perseverance; for others, it represents the violence of forced assimilation and negative health outcomes. Like many foods consumed by colonized people, fry bread's legacy is complicated.
body.zh: 無論哪種方式，油炸麵包現在通常在儀式和其他原住民文化活動和節日中供應，特別是在西南部。對一些原住民來說，它像徵著毅力；對某些原住民來說，它像徵著毅力。對其他人來說，它代表著強迫同化的暴力和負面的健康後果。就像殖民地人民消費的許多食物一樣，炸麵包的遺產也很複雜。

body.en: What's not complicated, however, is the magic that Cecelia Miller and her crew make with the stuff. Warm, filling, and equal parts crispy and soft, Fry Bread House's version is like a hug on a plate. Try it in taco form, or with a side of hominy stew or red, spicy pozole . Twenty years after its opening, the restaurant was finally recognized for its work with a James Beard "America's Classics" designation, celebrating its menu, Native roots, and diverse clientele that includes Native regulars, "hipsters," and out-of-towners stopping in for a taste. While the award is an important recognition, lovers of the establishment know that its enduring legacy isn't on paper: The proof is in the fry bread.
body.zh: 然而，塞西莉亞·米勒和她的團隊用這些東西創造的魔法並不複雜。 Fry Bread House 的版本溫暖、飽滿、酥脆和柔軟，就像盤子上的擁抱。嘗試以炸玉米餅的形式，或配上燉玉米粥或紅辣波唑。開業二十年後，這家餐廳終於因其詹姆斯·比爾德 (James Beard) 的“美國經典”稱號而獲得認可，慶祝其菜單、原住民根源以及包括原住民常客、“潮人”和前來品嚐的外地人在內的多元化顧客。雖然該獎項是一項重要的認可，但該機構的愛好者都知道，其持久的遺產並不在紙上：證據就在炸麵包中。

body.en: The Fry Bread House is a great lunchtime stop—you'll be able to have a filling taco, side, and drink, for just about under $10—but be prepared for a rush, as it's a popular midday destination .
body.zh: Fry Bread House 是午餐時間的絕佳去處，您可以花不到 10 美元享用一份豐盛的炸玉米餅、配菜和飲料，但要做好趕路的準備，因為它是一個受歡迎的中午目的地。

excerpt.en: Its colorful features now fade in the hot Arizona sun.
excerpt.zh: 它多彩的特徵現在在亞利桑那州炎熱的陽光下褪色。

body.en: If you were alive in the ’80s or ’90s, you've likely encountered a Lisa Frank product. The brand won the hearts of many children and tweens with its adorable, sparkly products. Schools supplies such as folders and pencils depicting rainbow dolphins and colorful unicorns became a symbol of coolness.
body.zh: 如果你生活在 80 年代或 90 年代，你可能遇到過 Lisa Frank 產品。該品牌以其可愛、閃亮的產品贏得了許多兒童和青少年的心。描繪彩虹海豚和彩色獨角獸的文件夾和鉛筆等學校用品成為酷的象徵。

body.en: Lisa Frank Incorporated was founded in 1979 and named after its 24-year-old founder. Stickers were the first product with a popular line of school supplies following in 1987.
body.zh: Lisa Frank Incorporated 成立於 1979 年，以其 24 歲創辦人的名字命名。 1987 年，貼紙成為第一個受歡迎的學校用品系列產品。

body.en: Its popularity rose, and in 1996 this 320,000-square-foot factory opened in Tucson , Arizona and paid tribute to the company's line of cutesy, rainbow products. It even features a rainbow loading dock and pink glass entry. There are also more subtle details such as hearts and stars lining the fence. The cheerful features now fade in the desert sun, surrounded by dull brown tumbleweeds.
body.zh: 它的知名度不斷上升，1996 年，這家佔地 320,000 平方英尺的工廠在亞利桑那州圖森市開業，向該公司可愛的彩虹產品系列致敬。它甚至還有彩虹裝卸碼頭和粉紅色玻璃入口。還有更微妙的細節，例如柵欄上排列的心形和星星。歡快的面貌現在在沙漠的陽光下褪色，周圍是深褐色的風滾草。

body.en: The factory once offered tours, but now the interior is mostly empty. Behind the pink glass, a giant statue of the brand’s iconic yellow lab puppy guards the lobby. Journey deeper, and you’ll encounter a giant panda in overalls with a can of rainbow paint and a brush poised and ready to make the world brighter.
body.zh: 工廠曾經提供參觀服務，但現在內部大部分是空的。在粉紅色玻璃後面，一尊品牌標誌性黃色拉布拉多犬的巨型雕像守護著大廳。再往深處走，你會遇到一隻穿著工作服的大熊貓，手裡拿著一罐彩虹顏料和一把畫筆，準備讓世界變得更加光明。

body.en: Sales declined as the original fans grew up, and rumors of poorly treated employees showed that maybe it wasn’t all technicolor puppies and rainbows. In 2013, the factory was officially shut down.
body.zh: 隨著最初粉絲的成長，銷量下降，而關於員工待遇不佳的傳言表明，也許這並不全是彩色小狗和彩虹。 2013年，工廠正式關閉。

body.en: The brand saw a resurgence in popularity in 2021, however, when Lisa Frank’s son took over as Director of Business Development and began managing the brand’s Instagram. With nostalgia capitalism resurrecting demand for the brand, they started selling products online, and even gave the outside of the factory a fresh paint job.
body.zh: 然而，當 Lisa Frank 的兒子接任業務開發總監並開始管理該品牌的 Instagram 時，該品牌在 2021 年重新流行起來。隨著懷舊資本主義重新喚起了對品牌的需求，他們開始在網路上銷售產品，甚至為工廠的外部重新粉刷了一遍。

excerpt.en: This striking public art installation is suspended above a public park, designed to gently move in the breeze.
excerpt.zh: 這個引人注目的公共藝術裝置懸掛在公園上方，旨在在微風中輕輕移動。

body.en: A quote from Ralph Waldo Emerson, "adopt the pace of nature; her secret is patience," inspired the title of this massive public art installation created by Janet Echelman and located above Phoenix's Civic Space Park.
body.zh: 拉爾夫·沃爾多·愛默生（Ralph Waldo Emerson）的一句話“跟隨自然的步伐；她的秘密就是耐心”，珍妮特·埃切爾曼（Janet Echelman）創作的這個大型公共藝術裝置的標題受到了啟發，該裝置位於鳳凰城的公民太空公園上方。

body.en: The aerial structure is 145 feet tall, suspended 38 feet off the ground, and rising more than 100 feet in the air. The sculpture was made using galvanized steel, polyester twine netting, and colored lights. The creation was a combined effort between the artist and a team of engineers, architects, planners, lighting designers, and fabricators.
body.zh: 該空中結構高 145 英尺，距地面 38 英尺，高度超過 100 英尺。該雕塑由鍍鋅鋼、聚酯麻線網和彩色燈光製成。這項創作是藝術家和工程師、建築師、規劃師、照明設計師和製造商團隊的共同努力。

body.en: Echelman is known for her large-scale fiber sculptures. While in Hong Kong in the late 1990s, she was inspired to try a new approach to sculpture while watching fishermen bundling their nets. Many of Echelman's pieces use intricate net-like materials to create large forms that seem light as air.
body.zh: 埃克爾曼以其大型纖維雕塑而聞名。 1990 年代末在香港，當她觀看漁民收網時，受到啟發，嘗試了一種新的雕塑方法。埃克爾曼的許多作品都使用複雜的網狀材料來創造出看起來像空氣一樣輕的大型形狀。

body.en: Her Secret Is Patience was designed to create "shadow drawings," which the artist explains are inspired by Arizona's cloud shadows that enthralled her on her first visit. During the day the structure moves with the breeze. At night the structure is lit up with a kaleidoscope range of colors, which change with the seasons.
body.zh: 她的秘密是耐心旨在創作“陰影畫”，藝術家解釋說，其靈感來自於她第一次訪問時就著迷的亞利桑那州的雲影。白天，建築物隨著微風移動。到了晚上，這棟建築會被燈光照亮，呈現出萬花筒般的色彩，隨著季節的變化而改變。

excerpt.en: America's only nuclear missile silo open to the public.
excerpt.zh: 美國唯一向公眾開放的核子飛彈發射井。

body.en: The only megaton missile silo from the Cold War that is open to the public, the Titan Missile Museum offers a unique experience. It is located in the hot Arizona desert -- a bleak setting that feels appropriate for a nuclear missile silo -- and was the largest nuclear missile silo in the continental United States until it was decommissioned in 1982 by Ronald Reagan.
body.zh: 泰坦飛彈博物館是冷戰時期唯一向公眾開放的百萬噸級飛彈發射井，可為您帶來獨特的體驗。它位於炎熱的亞利桑那州沙漠中——荒涼的環境感覺適合建造核導彈發射井——並且是美國大陸最大的核導彈發射井，直到 1982 年被羅納德·裡根退役。

body.en: Inside the silo, you can see up close a missile that was used for training exercises (the original was moved when the silo became a museum), the control room, and the living quarters in a place that was built to survive a direct attack from a multi-megaton nuclear blast. The corridors look like they belong on the Death Star, but this is no science fiction. The culmination of the tour is a simulated launch, complete with secret codes and two-key ignition, a count down, and a blastoff. The nuclear winter, resulting fallout and post-apocalyptic aftermath is left to the imagination. Sitting deep within the chambers of one of the most destructive devices ever created by man is a much more frightening experience than any haunted house.
body.zh: 在發射井內，您可以近距離看到用於訓練演習的飛彈（當發射井成為博物館時，原來的飛彈被移動）、控制室和居住區，該居住區是為了在百萬噸級核爆的直接攻擊中倖存下來而建造的。這些走廊看起來就像是屬於死星，但這並不是科幻小說。參觀的高潮是模擬發射，包括密碼和兩鍵點火、倒數計時和發射。核子冬天、由此產生的後果和世界末日後的後果都留給人們想像。坐在人類有史以來最具破壞性的裝置之一的密室深處，是比任何鬼屋更可怕的經歷。

body.en: Attendants, for security reasons (and perhaps psychological ones too), were never told where the missiles they were ready to fire were aimed.
body.zh: 出於安全原因（也許還有心理原因），服務員永遠不會被告知他們準備發射的導彈瞄準了哪裡。

body.en: Henry
body.zh: 亨利

address: 1580 W. Duval Mine Rd., Green Valley, Arizona, 85614

excerpt.en: One of the largest, oldest, darkest, quietest motel rooms in the world.
excerpt.zh: 世界上最大、最古老、最黑暗、最安靜的汽車旅館房間之一。

body.en: During the Cuban Missile Crisis in 1961, then-President John F. Kennedy decided to create a safe place for evacuees should the bombs begin to rain down on American heads, and found the perfect spot in the Grand Canyon Caverns.
body.zh: 1961 年古巴飛彈危機期間，時任總統約翰·F·甘迺迪 (John F. Kennedy) 決定為撤離人員創建一個安全的地方，以防炸彈如雨般落在美國人的頭上，並在大峽谷洞穴中找到了完美的地點。

body.en: The POTUS moved enough food and supplies into the caves to support over 2,000 people for at least a month. While the bombs never dropped, in true American fashion, the site became a tourist spot. Visitors to the Grand Canyon can still take refuge in the caverns by staying in the Grand Canyon Caverns Underground Suite.
body.zh: 總統將足夠的食物和物資轉移到洞穴中，足以支持 2,000 多人至少一個月的生活。雖然炸彈從未落下，但按照真正的美國風格，該地點成為了一個旅遊景點。前往大峽谷的遊客仍可入住大峽谷洞穴地下套房，在洞穴中避難。

body.en: Maintained and operated by the above-ground Grand Canyon Caverns Motel, this single room is located 220 feet below ground, near the area where JFK's emergency rations are still stored, kept fresh and usable after 40 years by the cavern's naturally dry climate. The suite features many modern amenities including a television, double beds, a small library, a record player, and even running water supplied by hundreds of gallons, hand-carried down into the caves. Despite the seeming solitude of being deep in the Earth, the suite is actually not all that private--tours pass through during most daylight hours.
body.zh: 這間單人房由地上大峽谷洞穴汽車旅館 (Grand Canyon Caverns Motel) 維護和運營，位於地下 220 英尺處，靠近肯尼迪緊急口糧的存放區域，由於洞穴自然乾燥的氣候，40 年後仍然保持新鮮和可用。套房配備了許多現代化設施，包括電視、雙人床、小型圖書館、電唱機，甚至還有數百加侖的自來水，用手運送到洞穴中。儘管在地球深處看似孤獨，但套房實際上並不是那麼私密——旅遊團在大多數白天都會經過。

body.en: Due to the extreme depth, perpetual and complete darkness, and zero humidity, nothing lives in the caves. This lack of rodent, insect, or other animal coupled with the crushing insulation of stone makes the lodging possibly the quietest room in the world. The cavern that houses the room was created by over 65 million years of natural acidic erosion, a thing to keep in mind when staring down the $900/ a night rate.
body.zh: 由於極度深度、永久完全的黑暗以及零濕度，洞穴中沒有任何生命。由於沒有囓齒動物、昆蟲或其他動物，再加上石頭的隔熱效果，這使得該住宿可能是世界上最安靜的房間。房間所在的洞穴是由超過 6500 萬年的自然酸性侵蝕形成的，在考慮每晚 900 美元的房價時要記住這一點。

address: Grand Canyon Caverns, Route 66, Peach Springs, Arizona, 86434

excerpt.en: The artist James Turrell is repurposing an extinct volcano crater as an observatory to experience the cosmos.
excerpt.zh: 藝術家詹姆斯·特雷爾 (James Turrell) 正在將一座死火山口改造為體驗宇宙的天文台。

body.en: Roden Crater is 400,000 years old, the blackened, geological husk of what was once a fiery giant on the rim of Arizona's Painted Desert.
body.zh: 羅登隕石坑 (Roden Crater) 已有 40 萬年的歷史，它是亞利桑那州彩繪沙漠邊緣曾經熾熱的巨人的黑色地質外殼。

body.en: The 600-ft-tall cinder cone has been quiet for centuries, but artist James Turrell has given it a second life as naked-eye observatory and impressively grandiose visual art display. Its reincarnation as a land art project and celestial lookout began in 1975 and has been an ongoing endeavor ever since, the end game consisting of 20 underground rooms designed to alter your perception of the solar expanse.
body.zh: 這座 600 英尺高的煤渣錐已經沉寂了幾個世紀，但藝術家詹姆斯·特雷爾 (James Turrell) 賦予了它第二次生命，成為裸眼天文台和令人印象深刻的宏偉視覺藝術展示。它作為一個大地藝術項目和天體瞭望台的轉世始於 1975 年，自此一直是一項持續的努力，最終的遊戲由 20 個地下房間組成，旨在改變您對太陽廣闊的看法。

body.en: "At Roden Crater I was interested in taking the cultural artifice of art out into the natural surround. I did not want the work to be a mark upon nature, but I wanted the work to be enfolded in nature in such a way that light from the sun, moon and stars empowered the spaces … I wanted an area where you had a sense of standing on the planet. I wanted an area of exposed geology like the Grand Canyon or the Painted Desert, where you could feel geologic time. Then in this stage set of geologic time, I wanted to make spaces that engaged celestial events in light so that the spaces performed a “music of the spheres” in light. The sequence of spaces, leading up to the final large space at the top of the crater, magnifies events. The work I do intensifies the experience of light by isolating it and occluding light from events not looked at. I have selected different portions of the sky and a limited number of events for each of the spaces. This is a reason for the large number of spaces."
body.zh: 「在羅登火山口，我有興趣將藝術的文化技巧帶入自然環境中。我不希望作品成為自然的標記，但我希望作品能夠被自然包圍，讓來自太陽、月亮和星星的光賦予空間力量……我想要一個讓你有一種站在地球上的感覺的區域。我想要一個像大峽谷或彩繪沙漠這樣暴露的地質區域，在那裡你可以感受到地質時間。

body.en: -James Turrell
body.zh: ——詹姆斯‧特瑞爾

body.en: Turrell's magnum opus has so far entailed the redistribution of over 1.3 million cubic yards of dirt to shape the crater, and extensive engineering of tunnels and varying spaces from which to view the sky. Each space will offer a different perspective of the vastness above that we often take for granted. Celestial events as well as visual manipulation will be used to create a natural shift in the appearance of the desert sky, transforming Turrell's vision into a wondrous experience for the viewer.
body.zh: 到目前為止，特雷爾的鉅作包括重新分配超過 130 萬立方碼的泥土來塑造火山口形狀，以及對隧道和不同空間進行廣泛的工程設計，以供觀看天空。每個空間都會為我們通常認為理所當然的廣闊空間提供不同的視角。天體事件和視覺操縱將被用來創造沙漠天空外觀的自然變化，將特雷爾的視覺轉變為觀眾的奇妙體驗。

excerpt.en: In this small Phoenix taxidermy emporium, you can find everything from a squid in a jar to a freeze-dried toad.
excerpt.zh: 在這個小型的鳳凰城動物標本剝製商場裡，您可以找到從罐裝魷魚到冷凍乾燥蟾蜍的各種商品。

body.en: The arid, endlessly sunny environs of Phoenix, Arizona might not be the first place you would think to look for a fascinating natural history and taxidermy emporium, but thanks to Curious Nature, even those in the sunny Southwest need not go without some dead animals to display.
body.zh: 亞利桑那州鳳凰城乾旱、陽光燦爛的環境可能不是您尋找迷人的自然歷史和標本剝製商場的第一個地方，但由於好奇的大自然，即使是在陽光明媚的西南部，也不需要沒有一些死去的動物來展示。

body.en: Tucked away behind an unassuming storefront in Phoenix's art district, Curious Nature is a small shop filled with an ever-rotating selection of preserved natural objects. Visitors can find everything from preserved octopi in jars to tanned bison scrotum to owl pellets dissection kits to strangely adorable taxidermy ducklings. The deceased menagerie of Curious Nature has a a number of species that have never even been found close to a desert.
body.zh: Curious Nature 隱藏在鳳凰城藝術區一家不起眼的店面後面，是一家小商店，裡面擺滿了不斷輪換的精選保存完好的自然物品。遊客可以找到各種物品，從罐裝章魚到曬黑的野牛陰囊，到貓頭鷹顆粒解剖套件，再到奇特可愛的動物標本剝製小鴨。好奇大自然的已故動物園裡有許多從未在沙漠附近發現的物種。

body.en: In addition to the slimy and furry things around, there is a nearly floor-to-ceiling glass cabinet displaying animal skulls arranged from small to large, and trinkets like geodes, sea stars, and deer feet are sprinkled throughout the room. Curious Nature is also a reliable source for mounted and framed insects, unusual jewelry, anatomical art, and strange books. The shop also offers classes on taxidermy and preserving wet specimens.
body.zh: 除了周圍那些黏糊糊、毛茸茸的東西之外，還有一個幾乎從地板到天花板的玻璃櫃，裡面陳列著從小到大排列的動物頭骨，晶洞、海星、鹿腳等小飾品散佈在整個房間裡。好奇的自然也是鑲嵌和框架的昆蟲、不尋常的珠寶、解剖藝術和奇怪的書籍的可靠來源。該商店還提供動物標本剝製術和濕標本保存課程。

body.en: Similar stores such as Evolution in New York, offer a similar array of museum-like specimens, but Curious Nature is taxidermy oasis in the Southwest.
body.zh: 類似的商店，例如紐約的 Evolution，提供一系列類似博物館般的標本，但 Curious Nature 是西南部的動物標本剝制綠洲。

title.zh: 德爾加迪略的雪帽汽車劇院

excerpt.en: A classic Route 66 landmark that was built with scrap lumber and is held together with kitsch and puns.
excerpt.zh: 經典的 66 號公路地標，用廢木材建造而成，並用庸俗和雙關語組合在一起。

body.en: Built during the height of America's obsession with cruising the highways and byways, Delgadillo's Snow Cap Drive-In has been making drivers stop and laugh for over 50 years.
body.zh: 德爾加迪略 (Delgadillo) 的雪帽汽車影院 (Snow Cap Drive-In) 建於美國人熱衷於在高速公路和小徑上巡遊的鼎盛時期，50 多年來一直讓司機們駐足歡笑。

body.en: Located on the longest remaining stretch of Route 66, there is no better place to experience the genuine small town hospitality and quirky pride that once defined the Mother Road than Delgadillo's Snow Cap Drive-In. Originally constructed in 1953 by the now deceased Juan Delgadillo with mostly scrap lumber from a nearby railroad yard, the eatery first gained fame when Delgadillo sliced the top off of his car and began covering it in eye-catching flare such as stickers and a fake Christmas tree. The ramshackle greasy spoon soon became a favorite among locals and travelers down the famous highway.
body.zh: 德爾加迪略 (Delgadillo) 的雪帽汽車影院 (Snow Cap Drive-In) 位於 66 號公路僅存的最長路段上，是體驗真正的小鎮熱情好客和曾經定義的母親之路的奇特自豪感的最佳地點。這家餐廳最初由現已去世的胡安·德爾加迪略 (Juan Delgadillo) 於 1953 年建造，主要使用附近鐵路站的廢木材。當德爾加迪略 (Delgadillo) 將他的汽車頂部切下來並開始用貼紙和假聖誕樹等引人注目的耀斑覆蓋它時，這家餐廳首次聲名鵲起。搖搖欲墜的油勺很快就成為當地人和著名高速公路上旅行者的最愛。

body.en: The establishment's interior restaurant space and outdoor garden still evolves daily. The space is an organic cavern of kitsch, as visitors adorn the structure with foreign money, souvenirs, pictures, business cards, tour guide ID's, stickers, and a myriad of other pieces of travel ephemera. The walls and ceiling have become a shaggy roadmap of the diner's history of visitors.
body.zh: 酒店的內部餐廳空間和戶外花園仍然每天都在變化。這個空間是一個庸俗的有機洞穴，遊客用外國貨幣、紀念品、圖片、名片、導遊證、貼紙和無數其他旅行短暫物品來裝飾這個結構。牆壁和天花板已經成為餐廳訪客歷史的一張毛茸茸的路線圖。

body.en: The drive-in clearly does not take itself too seriously, but their devotion to jokes and whimsy seeps into every facets of the business. From the front door, which features two door knobs (one's a fake), to the jokingly redundant menu items (dead chicken, anyone?), the eatery gives every guest the funhouse treatment. Visitors may have to make a clear distinction between iced tea and iced tee and confirm that they want cheese on their cheeseburgers.
body.zh: 汽車餐廳顯然不太重視自己，但他們對笑話和奇思妙想的熱愛滲透到了生意的各個方面。從帶有兩個門把手（一個是假的）的前門，到可笑的多餘菜單項目（死雞，有人嗎？），這家餐廳為每位客人提供了歡樂的待遇。遊客可能必須明確區分冰茶和冰 T 卹，並確認他們想要在起司漢堡上加起司。

body.en: Despite dwindling numbers of passersby on Route 66, Delgadillo's Snow Cap Drive-In is still operated by Delgadillo's son who keeps the laughs and burgers coming.
body.zh: 儘管 66 號公路上的路人數量逐漸減少，德爾加迪略的 Snow Cap Drive-In 餐廳仍然由德爾加迪略的兒子經營，他的笑聲和漢堡包源源不斷。

excerpt.en: A spiritual vortex among the red rocks in Sedona.
excerpt.zh: 塞多納紅色岩石中的精神漩渦。

body.en: Although the 90-foot cross on its facade makes the Chapel of the Holy Cross a distinctly Christian monument, visitors without an interest in religion often describe their trek up the red rocks as a spiritual event.
body.zh: 雖然聖十字教堂正面 90 英尺高的十字架使之成為明顯的基督教紀念碑，但對宗教不感興趣的遊客經常將他們攀登紅色岩石的旅程描述為精神活動。

body.en: The Chapel is located in the heart of what many describe as a vortex bringing gratitude to those who flock there. Sedona itself is well known to many for its connection to new-age mysticism and the purported energy vortices on the outskirts of the city. Despite this connection, the Chapel itself was actually built by a devout student of Frank Lloyd Wright named Marguerite Brunswig Staude in 1956. Staude wanted to create a lasting tribute to her religious beliefs, and was so taken with the beauty of Sedona that she began work on the Chapel.
body.zh: 教堂位於許多人所描述的漩渦中心，為聚集在那裡的人們帶來感激之情。塞多納本身因其與新時代神秘主義和城郊所謂的能量漩渦的聯繫而為許多人所熟知。儘管有這種聯繫，教堂本身實際上是由弗蘭克·勞埃德·賴特 (Frank Lloyd Wright) 的一位虔誠的學生瑪格麗特·布倫斯維格·施陶德 (Marguerite Brunswig Staude) 於 1956 年建造的。施陶德希望為她的宗教信仰做出持久的致敬，並且被塞多納的美麗所吸引，因此她開始了教堂的工作。

body.en: Tucked between massive red boulders, the Chapel is more widely known as one of America's manmade wonders. The sunlight streaming through the windows is likely to make any visitor appreciate the glory of nature and man's ability to harness that power to create beauty in the desert. Even for those without a religious connection, the massive Chapel overlooking the arid horizon is picturesque enough to make the trip worthwhile.
body.zh: 這座教堂隱藏在巨大的紅色巨石之間，被譽為美國的人造奇觀之一。透過窗戶的陽光可能會讓任何遊客欣賞到大自然的輝煌，以及人類利用這種力量在沙漠中創造美麗的能力。即使對於那些沒有宗教信仰的人來說，俯瞰乾旱地平線的巨大教堂也風景如畫，值得一遊。

body.en: It's accessible by car from Uptown Sedona. There are no public restrooms. The chapel is closed on Christmas and Easter.
body.zh: 從塞多納住宅區開車即可抵達。沒有公共衛生間。教會在聖誕節和復活節關閉。

excerpt.en: Ancient pueblos built into the base of a natural canyon wall.
excerpt.zh: 古老的村莊建在天然峽谷壁的底部。

body.en: Ancient cliff dwelling ruins amidst geological beauty.
body.zh: 地質美景中的古代懸崖住宅遺址。

body.en: The Sinagua people of arid Arizona were a pre-Colombian people who lived in Walnut Canyon circa 1100 to 1250. The canyon was formed by Walnut Creek, and lies on the Colorado Plateau. Here, the Sinagua built around 80 dwellings beneath ledges of Kaibab limestone. Though they were adept at thriving in such a dry climate, and are even thought to have established a trading empire that extended towards Central America, why they abandoned their small community in Walnut Canyon remains a mystery.
body.zh: 生活在乾旱的亞利桑那州的西納瓜人是前哥倫比亞人，大約在 1100 年至 1250 年期間居住在核桃峽谷。該峽谷由核桃溪形成，位於科羅拉多高原上。在這裡，西納瓜人在凱巴布石灰岩的岩架下建造了大約 80 座住宅。儘管他們善於在如此乾燥的氣候下繁衍生息，甚至被認為已經建立了一個向中美洲延伸的貿易帝國，但他們為何放棄核桃峽谷的小社區仍然是個謎。

body.en: The picturesque site is now a protected national monument and visitors can walk through the ruins of the pueblos nestled beneath the cliffs.
body.zh: 這個風景如畫的地方現在是受保護的國家紀念碑，遊客可以步行穿過懸崖下的普韋布洛遺址。

body.en: Located about 7.5 miles east of FlTo reach Walnut Canyon from Flagstaff, travel east on Interstate 40 toward Albuquerque. Take Exit 204, and head south. The Walnut Canyon Visitor Center is located at the end of this three mile road. It complements the Grand Canyon National Park so well; green where the Grand Canyon is arid, small where the Grand Canyon is enormous, and completely manageable in one morning. Walnut Canyon is a National Monument and has frequent tours and stationed interpreters. The visitor center has a picnic area, bathroom, and water fountain.
body.zh: 位於佛羅裡達州以東約 7.5 英里處。從弗拉格斯塔夫到達核桃峽谷，請沿著 40 號州際公路向東前往阿爾伯克基。從204號出口向南行駛。核桃峽谷遊客中心位於這條三英里路的盡頭。它與大峽谷國家公園相得益彰；大峽谷乾旱的地方綠，大峽谷大的地方小，一上午完全可以搞定。核桃峽谷是國家紀念碑，有頻繁的遊覽活動並駐有翻譯人員。遊客中心設有野餐區、浴室和噴泉。

excerpt.en: The story of Two Guns, Arizona could easily be described as a Shakespearian tragedy on Route 66.
excerpt.zh: 《亞利桑那州兩把槍》的故事很容易被描述為 66 號公路上的莎士比亞悲劇。

body.en: It has all the workings of a modern-day Hamlet – murder, madness, and supernatural superstition dotting its colorful history.
body.zh: 它具有現代哈姆雷特的所有特徵——謀殺、瘋狂和超自然迷信點綴著它豐富多彩的歷史。

body.en: Two Guns, originally known as Canyon Lodge, started out as a modest trading post at the beginning of the 19th century, run by a couple of homesteaders by the names of Mr. and Mrs. Daniel B. Oldfield. A few more westward pioneers staked claim to the area over the years, and by the early 1920s the road through town, known as the National Trail Highway, became the preferred route across Diablo Canyon . When Earle and Louise Cundiff blew into town, they brought 320 acres of the land, making Canyon Lodge a busy stop for travelers. By the late '20s, what was once the National Trail Highway was blossoming into the famed Route 66, and the once-isolated trading post was evolving into a bustling stop for incoming drivers needing gas, food, and oil.
body.zh: 兩槍最初被稱為峽谷小屋 (Canyon Lodge)，最初是 19 世紀初的一個簡陋貿易站，由丹尼爾·B·奧德菲爾德 (Daniel B. Oldfield) 夫婦經營。多年來，更多的西進拓荒者聲稱擁有該地區的所有權，到 1920 年代初期，穿過城鎮的道路（稱為國家步道高速公路）成為穿越暗黑破壞神峽谷的首選路線。當 Earle 和 Louise Cundiff 進城時，他們帶來了 320 英畝的土地，使 Canyon Lodge 成為遊客繁忙的停留地。到了 1920 年代末，曾經的國道高速公路 (National Trail Highway) 逐漸發展成為著名的 66 號公路，曾經孤立的貿易站也逐漸發展成為需要汽油、食物和石油的入境司機的熙熙攘攘的停靠站。

body.en: This quickly escalating prosperity caught the attention of a man named Harry Miller. A well-educated veteran of the Spanish-American War and an ostentatious publicist, Miller was an eccentric man who claimed to be full-blooded Apache and was known for his garish and unpleasant demeanor. Wanting a piece of the action, Harry "Two Guns" Miller allegedly struck a deal with the Cundiffs to lease a business site for ten years.
body.zh: 這種快速增長的繁榮引起了一個名叫哈利·米勒的人的注意。米勒是一位受過良好教育的美西戰爭老兵，也是一位愛炫耀的公關人員，他性格古怪，自稱是純種阿帕奇人，以花哨和令人不快的舉止而聞名。據稱，哈利「雙槍」米勒想要分一杯羹，他與康迪夫兄弟達成協議，租用一處商業場地十年。

body.en: Under Miller's watch, the trading post was renamed Two Guns and turned into a full-blown tourist trap. He grew out his hair and braided it, taking on a persona by the name of Chief Crazy Thunder. He started a zoo with chicken-wire cages that held mountain lions and other native Arizona animals and started tours down into a canyon cave now called Apache Death Cave , where 42 Apache men met their death in battle.
body.zh: 在米勒的監督下，這個貿易站被更名為“兩槍”，並變成了一個全面的旅遊陷阱。他把頭髮留起來編成辮子，化身為狂雷酋長。他創辦了一個動物園，裡面有鐵絲網籠，裡面關著山獅和其他亞利桑那州本土動物，並開始深入一個峽谷洞穴（現在稱為阿帕奇死亡洞），42 名阿帕奇人在戰鬥中喪生。

body.en: The story of the cave was interesting in its own right, but Miller believed that the tale needed something more. He cleaned up the remaining bones he found in the cave, built fake ruins, and repurposed the tomb into a “cave dwelling.” In a macabre commercial stroke of genius, he saved the skulls of the ill-fated Apache and sold them as souvenirs. In order to make the cave a bit more tourist-friendly, he also strung up some electric lighting, threw in a soda stand, and renamed the death cave the “Mystery Cave.”
body.zh: 洞穴的故事本身就很有趣，但米勒認為這個故事還需要更多。他清理了在洞穴中發現的剩餘骨頭，建造了假廢墟，並將墳墓改造成「窯洞」。在一次令人毛骨悚然的商業天才中，他拯救了命運多舛的阿帕奇人的頭骨，並將它們作為紀念品出售。為了讓這個洞穴更適合遊客，他還安裝了一些電燈，擺設了一個汽水攤，並將死亡洞穴重新命名為「神秘洞穴」。

body.en: It was around this time that people say the curse of Two Guns began.
body.zh: 人們說，正是在這個時候，「兩槍」的詛咒開始了。

excerpt.en: Limestone caves with spectacular showcase chambers.
excerpt.zh: 石灰岩洞穴擁有壯觀的展示室。

body.en: After their discovery in 1974, these limestone caverns were kept secret for more than a decade as their discoverers sought a way to preserve their untrammeled beauty.
body.zh: 自 1974 年被發現以來，這些石灰岩洞穴的發現者一直在尋找一種方法來保存其不受約束的美麗，因此在十多年來一直保密。

body.en: Seeking undiscovered caves in the mid-70s, Gary Tenen and Randy Tufts discovered evidence of a secret cave: the two felt warm air emanating from a crack at the bottom of a sinkhole they found in the Whetstone Mountains of southern Arizona. The men slipped through the crack and discovered a network of pristine caverns with spectacular rock formations, including massive stalagmites and stalactites. The cavers would return on several occasions over four years, discovering 2.5 miles of passageways and chambers, all the while keeping their find secret, even from the owners of the property encompassing the cave, for fear of vandals.
body.zh: 在 70 年代中期尋找未被發現的洞穴時，加里·特南 (Gary Tenen) 和蘭迪·塔夫茨 (Randy Tufts) 發現了秘密洞穴的證據：兩人在亞利桑那州南部的磨石山發現的一個天坑底部的裂縫中感受到了溫暖的空氣。這些人從裂縫中鑽了出來，發現了一個由原始洞穴組成的網絡，裡面有壯觀的岩層，包括巨大的石筍和鐘乳石。四年來，探洞者多次返回，發現了 2.5 英里的通道和房間，同時，由於擔心遭到破壞，他們始終對自己的發現保密，甚至不告訴洞穴周圍財產的所有者。

body.en: In 1988, more than a decade after the discovery, the state of Arizona purchased the land from the Kartchner family and began developing the site into a state park, a process that took several years and millions of dollars.
body.zh: 1988 年，在這項發現十多年後，亞利桑那州從卡奇納家族手中購買了這片土地，並開始將該地開發成州立公園，這一過程花費了數年時間和數百萬美元。

body.en: Today parts of the cave are open to the public, including two large chambers. Throne Room holds the largest known soda-straw stalactite in the world, and Big Room features a large formation of Brushite moonmilk, a soft, creamy substance that's composed of mineral deposits but does not harden into rock.
body.zh: 如今，洞穴的部分區域向公眾開放，其中包括兩個大洞室。王座室 (Throne Room) 擁有世界上已知最大的蘇打秸稈鐘乳石，而大房間 (Big Room) 則擁有大量透鈣磷石月乳，這是一種柔軟的奶油狀物質，由礦物沉積物組成，但不會硬化成岩石。

body.en: Even though the cave has been partially developed to allow groups to visit, including paved paths and lights, there are still areas in the developed part of the cave that have been left relatively untouched. Tour guides will point out muddy footprints on the edge of a pool, which Tenens and Tufts left when they were exploring the cave.
body.zh: 儘管洞穴已經部分開發以允許團體參觀，包括鋪好的道路和燈光，但洞穴開發部分中仍然有一些區域相對不受影響。導遊會指出泳池邊緣的泥濘腳印，這是特南斯和塔夫茨在探索洞穴時留下的。

body.en: Big Room is also home to a colony of bats from spring through mid-autumn. The room is sealed off from humans to allow the bats to raise their young in the caves, as they have since time immemorial.
body.zh: 從春季到中秋，大房間還是一群蝙蝠的家。這個房間與人類隔離，以便蝙蝠在洞穴中撫養幼崽，就像它們自古以來的做法一樣。

title.en: Mini Time Machine Museum of Miniatures
title.zh: 迷你時光機微縮模型博物館

excerpt.en: Miniature art that tells an enormous story.
excerpt.zh: 微型藝術講述了一個巨大的故事。

body.en: The Mini Time Machine Museum of Miniatures transports visitors through space, time and imagination, through the observation of each unique little piece of art.
body.zh: 迷你時光機微縮模型博物館透過觀察每件獨特的小藝術品，帶領遊客穿越空間、時間和想像。

body.en: Each figurine and mini setting has its own special story to tell, and encourages visitors both young and old to use their imaginations. The museum creates a sensory, interactive experience, providing glimpses of history and culture and encounters with fantastical creatures.
body.zh: 每個雕像和迷你場景都有自己的特殊故事，鼓勵年輕和年長的遊客發揮他們的想像。博物館創造了一種感官、互動的體驗，讓人們一窺歷史和文化，並與奇幻生物相遇。

body.en: The museum is the permanent home of 275 miniature houses, room boxes, artifacts and figurines displayed in three captivating exhibits: the Enchanted Realm, History and Antique Gallery and Exploring the World. The Enchanted Realm shows the observer into an imaginary world, where woodland creatures, snow villages, fairy castles, witches and other mystical artifacts each tell a unique and magical story. The History Gallery represents various time periods and give observers tiny glimpses of history. It also displays how craftsmanship and technique have changed over time. This exhibit includes the oldest miniature house in the United States, crafted in 1775. The Exploring the World exhibit includes pieces from various countries including: the U.K., France, Germany, Holland, Italy, Japan, Thailand and Spain. Several times throughout each year, the museum assembles temporary displays featuring a specific point in history, notable miniature artists or miniatures in a particular context of society or culture.
body.zh: 博物館是 275 座微型房屋、房間盒子、文物和雕像的永久所在地，展示在三個迷人的展覽中：魔法王國、歷史和古董畫廊以及探索世界。魔法王國將觀察者帶入一個想像的世界，其中林地生物、雪村、童話城堡、女巫和其他神秘文物都講述著一個獨特而神奇的故事。歷史畫廊展示了不同的時期，讓觀察者可以一睹歷史。它還展示了工藝和技術如何隨著時間的推移而變化。展覽包括美國最古老的微型房屋，建於 1775 年。 「探索世界」展覽包括來自不同國家的作品，包括：英國、法國、德國、荷蘭、義大利、日本、泰國和西班牙。博物館每年都會多次舉辦臨時展覽，展示歷史上的特定時刻、著名的微型藝術家或特定社會或文化背景下的微型模型。

body.en: The founders of the museum, Patricia and Walter Arnell, became avid miniature collectors in 1979 when they moved to Tucson, Arizona. They became participating members of the National Association of Miniature Enthusiasts (NAME) and the International Guild of Miniature Artisans (IGMA). The Arnells envisioned a way to share their passion of miniature items in a creative, educational, and interactive environment. After two years of architectural planning, exhibit design, and construction, the vision of a mini time machine came to life.The Mini Time Machine Museum of Miniatures is a non-profit organization. All proceeds go to the maintinance and operation of the museum.
body.zh: 博物館的創始人帕特里夏·阿內爾 (Patricia Arnell) 和沃爾特·阿內爾 (Walter Arnell) 於 1979 年搬到亞利桑那州圖森市，成為狂熱的微型收藏家。他們成為全國微型愛好者協會 (NAME) 和國際微型工匠協會 (IGMA) 的參與成員。阿內爾夫婦設想了一種在創意、教育和互動環境中分享他們對微型物品的熱情的方法。經過兩年的建築規劃、展覽設計和施工，迷你時間機器的願景成為現實。迷你時間機器微縮模型博物館是一個非營利組織。所有收益均用於博物館的維護和運營。

address: 4455 East Camp Lowell Drive, Tucson, Arizona, 85712

excerpt.en: This golf ball–shaped former desert real estate office now houses a UFO museum.
excerpt.zh: 這座高爾夫球形狀的前沙漠房地產辦公室現在設有一個不明飛行物博物館。

body.en: Update as of May 2024: Closed indefinently.
body.zh: 截至 2024 年 5 月更新：無限期關閉。

body.en: This unusual 40-foot-diameter geodesic dome structure, known as Area 66, is a UFO museum dedicated to the alleged crash of a "flying saucer" outside of Kingman, Arizona, in 1953. The structure is impossible to miss from the highway and, as such, often draws in tourists and passersby who want to take a picture of the unusual orb, visit the museum, or shop in the convenience store on the grounds.
body.zh: 這座不尋常的直徑 40 英尺的測地圓頂結構被稱為 66 區，是一座 UFO 博物館，專門紀念 1953 年亞利桑那州金曼郊外所謂的「飛碟」墜毀事件。從高速公路上看，這座結構是不可能錯過的，因此，經常吸引想要為這個不尋常的球體拍照、參觀博物館或在地面便利商店購物的遊客和路人。

body.en: The structure has had many uses over the years and there are a few competing histories as to when and for what purpose it was originally built. It was used as a real estate office at one time to sell plots of land to "Lake Havasu Estates." The developers went so far as to send out promotional materials for the homes they hoped to construct showing happy would-be residents waterskiing and enjoying other amenities that were never to be built. The project was a classic scam and a couple of people served time in prison for it.
body.zh: 多年來，該建築有多種用途，關於其最初建造的時間和目的，存在一些相互矛盾的歷史。它曾一度被用作房地產辦公室，將土地出售給「哈瓦蘇湖莊園」。開發商甚至為他們希望建造的房屋發放了宣傳材料，展示了快樂的潛在居民滑水和享受其他從未建造的設施的情況。該項目是一個典型的騙局，有幾個人因此入獄。

body.en: After sitting empty for years, new owners eventually purchased the structure, spent significant money renovating it, built a store on the property, and named it Area 66. The structure once housed 3,400 square feet of living space but has been remodeled and opened as a UFO museum.
body.zh: 空置多年後，新業主最終購買了這座建築，斥巨資對其進行了翻新，並在該房產上建造了一家商店，並將其命名為「66 區」。該建築曾經擁有 3,400 平方英尺的居住空間，但現已改建為 UFO 博物館。

excerpt.en: A nature and cultural preserve named for its multitude of petroglyphs carved by the Northern Sinagua people.
excerpt.zh: 一個自然和文化保護區，因其眾多由北西納瓜人雕刻的岩畫而得名。

body.en: For many centuries, the Northern Sinagua people lived in the deserts of central and northern Arizona . Translating to “without water,” their name is derived from the name the Spanish Conquistadors gave the area when they arrived, shocked that people were able to survive in such an arid region.
body.zh: 許多世紀以來，北西納瓜人生活在亞利桑那州中部和北部的沙漠中。他們的名字被翻譯為“沒有水”，源自西班牙征服者到達時給該地區起的名字，他們對人們能夠在如此乾旱的地區生存感到震驚。

body.en: The Northern Sinagua people inhabited what is now Flagstaff , Arizona, from around 700 to 1300. Today, a large and scenic nature preserve within the city protects rare wetlands, birds and other wildlife, and the more than 150 Sinagua petroglyphs that gave Picture Canyon its name.
body.zh: 北西納瓜人在大約 700 年至 1300 年間居住在現在的亞利桑那州弗拉格斯塔夫。如今，該市內有一個風景優美的大型自然保護區，保護著稀有的濕地、鳥類和其他野生動物，以及 150 多處西納瓜岩畫，圖片峽谷由此得名。

body.en: The Sinagua people were primarily hunter-gatherers, but they did practice some limited agriculture after picking up irrigation techniques from their neighbors, the Hohokam tribe. Etched on rocks throughout the area, the petroglyphs in Picture Canyon depict scenes from this tribal life, such as hunters and animals like deer, elk, bighorn sheep, and water birds.
body.zh: 西納瓜人主要以狩獵採集為生，但在從鄰居霍霍卡姆部落學習灌溉技術後，他們確實從事了一些有限的農業活動。圖片峽谷中的岩畫刻在整個地區的岩石上，描繪了部落生活的場景，例如獵人和鹿、麋鹿、大角羊和水鳥等動物。

body.en: For reasons that are not totally understood—possibly drought, resource depletion, clashes with the neighboring Yavapai people, a changing climate, or some combination of these factors—the Northern Sinagua people left the region and resettled elsewhere, possibly becoming the early ancestors of the Hopi, Zuni, or Pima peoples.
body.zh: 由於尚未完全了解的原因——可能是乾旱、資源枯竭、與鄰近的亞瓦派人的衝突、氣候變遷或這些因素的某種組合——北西納瓜人離開了該地區並在其他地方定居，可能成為霍皮人、祖尼人或皮馬人的早期祖先。

body.en: For many centuries thereafter Picture Canyon was neglected and the growth of the city of Flagstaff began threatening the archaeological sites. Timber companies constructed railroads across the area in the early 20th century. The Arizona archaeologist Harold S. Colton took note of the area and studied it in 1928 but in the process unceremoniously looted the graves he uncovered there. Later, the El Paso company gas line was laid across the area and likely destroyed many historical sites in the process. The canyon also became a dumping ground by locals for cars, mattresses, and other garbage.
body.zh: 在此之後的許多世紀裡，圖畫峽谷一直被忽視，弗拉格斯塔夫市的發展開始威脅考古遺址。 20 世紀初，木材公司在該地區建造了鐵路。 1928 年，亞利桑那州考古學家哈羅德·S·科爾頓 (Harold S. Colton) 注意到了該地區並進行了研究，但在此過程中，他在那裡發現的墳墓被毫不客氣地洗劫一空。後來，埃爾帕索公司的天然氣管道鋪設在該地區，並可能在此過程中摧毀了許多歷史遺跡。該峽谷也成為當地人傾倒汽車、床墊和其他垃圾的場所。

body.en: For many years the petroglyphs and other archaeological sites in Picture Canyon were a little-known secret. As the city of Flagstaff kept growing, development encroached on the area. Citizens began advocating for the restoration and preservation of this picturesque landscape. They organized several cleanup efforts, including having cranes brought in to remove the abandoned and rusting cars.
body.zh: 多年來，圖畫峽谷的岩石和其他考古遺址都是一個鮮為人知的秘密。隨著弗拉格斯塔夫市的不斷發展，開發侵蝕了該地區。公民開始倡導恢復和保護這片風景如畫的景觀。他們組織了幾次清理工作，包括使用起重機來清除廢棄和生鏽的汽車。

address: 3920 N El Paso Flagstaff Rd, Flagstaff, Arizona

excerpt.en: On the outskirts of a reborn ghost town, a decaying post office remembers the bad old days.
excerpt.zh: 在一座重生的鬼城的郊區，一座破敗的郵局回憶著過去的糟糕時光。

body.en: Known at one time as "The Largest Ghost Town in America," Jerome, Arizona was once thought to have been lost to abandonment. The town has made a successful resurgence in recent years and is now home to a population of almost 500 people, a number of preserved historic sites, and an active artist community. However, its legacy of abandonment is far from forgotten.
body.zh: 亞利桑那州傑羅姆一度被稱為“美國最大的鬼城”，一度被認為已經被遺棄。近年來，該鎮成功復興，目前人口近 500 人，擁有許多保存完好的歷史遺跡和活躍的藝術家社區。然而，它被遺棄的遺產遠遠沒有被遺忘。

body.en: Sitting on the outskirts of the town, which has also been called "America's Most Vertical City" (it sits 5,200 feet above sea level), is a huge post office building that is slowly mouldering into oblivion, no matter how much the town might be bouncing back. Visitors to Jerome come to see the many historic houses and artsy community, but they often bypass the crumbling hulk hidden not far from the town's free parking lot. And it may be for the better considering that the aging building is probably super dangerous.
body.zh: 該鎮也被稱為「美國最垂直的城市」（海拔 5,200 英尺），坐落在該鎮郊區的一座巨大的郵局大樓，無論該鎮有多麼恢復活力，它都正在慢慢地被遺忘。來到傑羅姆的遊客來這裡是為了參觀許多歷史悠久的房屋和藝術社區，但他們經常繞過隱藏在距離小鎮免費停車場不遠的搖搖欲墜的廢墟。考慮到這座老化的建築可能非常危險，這可能會更好。

body.en: Nonetheless, some have dared venture to the rickety structure to observe the decay within. The lower floor of the post office is scattered with old lockers, broken ceiling pieces, and glass, providing access to a wobbly staircase that feels like it will collapse in from under your feet (which it might). The second story is equally, if not more, destroyed, with much of the ceiling fallen in.
body.zh: 儘管如此，還是有一些人敢於冒險進入這座搖搖欲墜的建築，觀察內部的腐爛情況。郵局的下層散落著舊置物櫃、破損的天花板和玻璃，通往搖搖欲墜的樓梯，感覺它會從你腳下塌陷（確實有可能）。第二層樓同樣被摧毀，甚至更嚴重，大部分天花板都塌陷了。

body.en: It may be wildly unsafe, and trespassing on the site is not recommended, but even from outside, the old Jerome post office is an impressive reminder of both how far a community can fall, and how resilient it can be.
body.zh: 它可能非常不安全，也不建議擅自進入該地點，但即使從外面看，舊傑羅姆郵局也令人印象深刻地提醒人們，一個社區可能會崩潰到什麼程度，以及它的恢復力有多大。

body.en: Update as of September 2019: The area is now in use by a mining company and only accessible if you disregard the "No Trespassing" signs. However, the building is visible from the road above that takes you to the Mine Museum.
body.zh: 截至 2019 年 9 月的更新：該區域目前由一家礦業公司使用，只有在無視「禁止侵入」標誌的情況下才能進入。然而，從上面通往礦山博物館的道路上可以看到這座建築。

body.zh: 每週透過 Atlas Obscura Places 通訊了解更多不尋常和非凡的地方。

excerpt.en: The world's largest rose bush has literally outgrown the pioneer museum it was planted behind.
excerpt.zh: 世界上最大的玫瑰叢實際上已經超出了它所在的先驅博物館的範圍。

body.en: The Rose Tree Museum in the famous wild west town of Tombstone, Arizona displays a fine collection of historic artifacts and materials, but the real attraction is the backyard rose bush which is the largest in the world.
body.zh: 玫瑰樹博物館位於亞利桑那州著名的狂野西部小鎮墓碑鎮，展示了一系列精美的歷史文物和材料，但真正吸引人的是後院的玫瑰叢，它是世界上最大的。

body.en: Planted in 1885 with cuttings from a"Lady Banksia Rose" that had been sent from Scotland, as the tree was first declared the "world's largest" in the late 1930's and has only continued to grow since then. The canopy of the bush-cum-tree now covers nearly 5,000 feet of space and is elevated from the ground by a series of wooden and steel supports. Each year, after the shed husks are cleaned out from around the base of the tree, the plant blossoms with clusters of small white roses. As weather permits, visitors are welcome to visit the museum and spend a lunch beneath the scenic green roof. More information can be found on the Rose Tree Museum's website http://tombstonerosetree.com
body.zh: 該樹於 1885 年種植，採用的是從蘇格蘭運來的“班克西亞玫瑰”的插條，該樹在 1930 年代末首次被宣佈為“世界上最大的”樹，此後一直在不斷生長。這棵灌木兼樹的樹冠現在覆蓋了近 5,000 英尺的空間，並透過一系列木製和鋼製支架從地面升起。每年，當樹根周圍的棚殼被清理乾淨後，植物就會開出一簇簇小白玫瑰。如果天氣允許，歡迎遊客參觀博物館並在風景優美的綠色屋頂下享用午餐。更多資訊請上玫瑰樹博物館網站 http://tombstonerosetree.com

body.en: Get more unusual and extraordinary places each week with the Atlas Obscura Places newsletter.
body.zh: 每週透過 Atlas Obscura Places 通訊了解更多不尋常和非凡的地方。

body.en: Your newsletter subscriptions with us are subject to Atlas Obscura's Privacy Policy and Terms of Use .
body.zh: 您向我們訂閱的電子報須遵守 Atlas Obscura 的隱私權政策和使用條款。

body.en: The best time to visit is in March and early April when the tree is in bloom.
body.zh: 最佳遊覽時間是三月和四月初，此時樹木盛開。

body.en: Gillian
body.zh: 阿嬌

address: Corner of 4th & Toughnut Street, Tombstone, Arizona, 85638

excerpt.en: This Arizona observatory is famous for investigations into Martian life, and as the place humans first spotted Pluto.
excerpt.zh: 這座亞利桑那州天文台因調查火星生命而聞名，也是人類首次發現冥王星的地方。

body.en: Percival Lowell, of the well-known Lowell family in Boston, was an early 20th century astronomer who popularized the belief that Mars was home to an advanced, highly technological civilization. Like most wealthy amateur scientists of his era, Lowell had many interests; he was a businessman, author, mathematician, and noted Japanophile who traveled extensively in Asia. In 1894, however, Lowell dedicated most of his efforts to studying astronomy and used his wealth to found an observatory in his name.
body.zh: 珀西瓦爾·洛威爾 (Percival Lowell) 出身於波士頓著名的洛威爾家族，是一位 20 世紀早期的天文學家，他讓人們普遍相信火星是先進、高科技文明的家園。像他那個時代大多數富有的業餘科學家一樣，洛威爾有很多興趣。他是一位商人、作家、數學家，也是一位遊歷亞洲各地的著名日本愛好者。然而，1894年，洛威爾將大部分精力投入天文學研究上，並以他的財富以他的名義建立了一座天文台。

body.en: Lowell's interest in astronomy and the potential for life on other worlds developed after the release of two influential works: The Planet Mars and Its Conditions of Habitability (1892), by French Spiritualist and science writer Camille Flammarion, and Life on Mars(1893), which documented the Martian observations of Italian astronomer Giovanni Schiaparelli. The latter book featured hand-drawn surface maps of the red planet, detailing a complex system of what Schiaparelli called canali , Italian for "channels." In English, however, the word was mistranslated as "canals," which implied that they had been artificially created. This mistake led some to conclude that Schiaparelli had observed the constructions of an advanced civilization (canals), rather than a natural feature of the landscape (channels). Though today the canali are known to be an optical illusion, Lowell was the strongest proponent of the view that they were artificial in nature. Consequently, he dedicated the next 15 years to studying Mars at his observatory in Flagstaff, Arizona.
body.zh: 洛厄爾對天文學和其他星球上存在生命的潛力的興趣在兩本有影響力的著作出版後得到了發展：法國招魂術家和科學作家卡米爾·弗拉馬里翁的《火星及其宜居條件》（1892年）和火星上的生命（1893年），該書記錄了意大利天文學家喬瓦尼·夏帕雷利對火星的觀測。後一本書以手繪的紅色星球表面地圖為特色，詳細介紹了夏帕雷利所謂的“canali”（意大利語中“渠道”的意思）的複雜系統。然而，在英語中，這個詞被誤譯為“運河”，這意味著它們是人工創造的。這個錯誤導致一些人得出這樣的結論：斯基亞帕雷利觀察到的是先進文明的建築（運河），而不是景觀的自然特徵（渠道）。儘管今天人們知道這條運河是一種視錯覺，但洛厄爾是運河本質上是人造的這一觀點的最有力支持者。因此，他在接下來的 15 年裡致力於在亞利桑那州弗拉格斯塔夫的天文台研究火星。

body.en: The site in Flagstaff was chosen for its high altitude (over 7,000 feet), few cloudy nights, and distance from city lights. These criteria, though now accepted as essential for optimal observing, were pioneered by Lowell. From Arizona, the astronomer presented his findings, along with illustrations of the surface features, in three books: Mars (1895), Mars and Its Canals (1906), and Mars As the Abode of Life (1908). In his publications, Lowell suggested that the canals were evidence of the desperate efforts of a technological society to siphon water from the polar ice caps of their drying planet.
body.zh: 選址位於弗拉格斯塔夫是因為其海拔較高（超過 7,000 英尺）、少有陰天且遠離城市燈光。這些標準雖然現在被認為是最佳觀測的必要條件，但它們是由洛威爾率先提出的。這位來自亞利桑那州的天文學家在三本書中介紹了他的發現以及表面特徵的插圖：《火星》（1895 年）、《火星及其運河》（1906 年）和《火星作為生命的居所》（1908 年）。洛威爾在他的出版品中提出，運河是科技社會拼命努力從乾燥星球的極地冰蓋中吸水的證據。

body.en: While Lowell's ideas generated much public excitement, the astronomer and his observatory were ostracized by the skeptical scientific community. Unfortunately for Lowell, his observations of Mars were not the only erroneous ones; he also sketched maps of Venus with spoke-like features emanating from a central dark spot. As the Venusian atmosphere is now known to be opaque, it was suggested that the astronomer was in fact observing an image of the blood vessels in his own eye.
body.zh: 雖然洛威爾的想法引起了公眾的廣泛關注，但這位天文學家和他的天文台卻遭到了懷疑的科學界的排斥。對洛威爾來說不幸的是，他對火星的觀察並不是唯一的錯誤。他也繪製了金星地圖，其中心暗點發出輻條狀特徵。由於現在已知金星大氣層是不透明的，因此有人認為天文學家實際上是在觀察自己眼睛中的血管圖像。

body.en: Despite the observer's mishaps, Lowell made significant contributions to astronomy and, in recognition of his efforts, craters on the Moon and Mars bear his name. Most notably, he began the search that culminated in Pluto's discovery. To explain apparent discrepancies in the orbits of Uranus and Neptune, Lowell proposed the Planet X hypothesis: an unseen ninth planet was perturbing the outer planets' orbits. Today we know that Pluto's gravitational influence on Uranus and Neptune is negligible, but Lowell was correct in suggesting another body resided beyond Neptune. Though Lowell would not live to see his theory affirmed, his observatory staff would. In 1930, Clyde Tombaugh , using the 13-inch astrograph, discovered the ninth "planet." Appropriately, Pluto's name and symbol were chosen in part due to Percival Lowell's initials, PL.
body.zh: 儘管觀察者遭遇了不幸，洛威爾還是對天文學做出了重大貢獻，為了表彰他的努力，月球和火星上的隕石坑都以他的名字命名。最值得注意的是，他開始了探索，最終發現了冥王星。為了解釋天王星和海王星軌道的明顯差異，洛威爾提出了 X 行星假說：一顆看不見的第九行星正在擾動外行星的軌道。今天我們知道冥王星對天王星和海王星的引力影響可以忽略不計，但洛威爾提出的另一個天體存在於海王星之外的說法是正確的。儘管洛厄爾無法活著看到他的理論得到證實，但他的天文台工作人員會。 1930年，克萊德·湯博（Clyde Tombaugh）使用13英寸占星儀發現了第九顆「行星」。冥王星的名字和符號的選擇部分是由於珀西瓦爾·洛厄爾的名字縮寫PL。

body.en: Today, the 24-inch Alvan Clark telescope, through which Lowell made his observations, is used for educational purposes. The telescope is housed in a dome designed by local bicycle mechanics and handymen, the Sykes brothers. The brothers constructed the "inverted bucket" shaped-dome out of local Ponderosa pine, and set the roof on a track so that it could rotate. Though construction was completed in only ten days, it has remained in good condition since, with the exception of the roof's rotation mechanism. When the original metal wheels of the track stopped functioning, the observatory staff attempted to rotate the wooden roof by floating it in a ring-shaped trough of salt water. This technique was abandoned however when the salt water proved a threat to the instruments. Today, the dome lid sits atop numerous 1954 Ford pickup tires, but it's not the only makeshift solution inside the dome: Mrs. Lowell's frying pan remains a suitable lens cap for the guide telescope mounted on the side of the Clark refractor!
body.zh: 如今，洛威爾進行觀測的 24 吋阿爾萬克拉克望遠鏡已用於教育目的。望遠鏡安裝在由當地自行車機械師和勤雜工賽克斯兄弟設計的圓頂內。兄弟倆用當地的黃鬆建造了“倒桶”形狀的圓頂，並將屋頂安裝在軌道上，以便它可以旋轉。雖然施工僅用了十天時間就完成了，但除了屋頂的旋轉機構外，自那以來一直保持良好狀態。當軌道原來的金屬輪停止運轉時，天文台工作人員試圖將木質屋頂漂浮在環形鹽水槽中來旋轉木質屋頂。然而，當鹽水對儀器構成威脅時，這項技術被放棄了。如今，圓頂蓋位於許多 1954 年福特皮卡輪胎的頂部，但這並不是圓頂內唯一的臨時解決方案：洛厄爾夫人的煎鍋仍然是安裝在克拉克折射鏡側面的引導望遠鏡的合適鏡頭蓋！

address: 1400 West Mars Hill Road, Flagstaff, Arizona, 86001

excerpt.en: The largest natural travertine bridge in the world is nestled in a small canyon in central Arizona.
excerpt.zh: 世界上最大的天然石灰華橋坐落在亞利桑那州中部的一個小峽谷中。

body.en: It isn't only humans and stomach-churning masses of swarming ants that are capable of building bridges. Mother Nature can build bridges, too — she just needs the right geological circumstances, and several million years.
body.zh: 不僅是人類和令人反胃的成群結隊的螞蟻有能力建造橋樑。大自然也可以建造橋樑——她只需要合適的地質環境和數百萬年的時間。

body.en: Tonto Natural Bridge is the result of one such combination of materials and slow, iterative natural forces. Lava flows created a base of rhyolite, which an ancient sea then covered in sand and mud. This sediment layer formed limestone that was again covered in lava, forming a basalt cap that was broken and shifted by erosion and tectonic activity, creating what is now known as Pine Creek Canyon. As water filtered down through the broken cap and into the underlying limestone, mineral-rich limestone aquifers were created. The water in these aquifers then returned to the surface in the form of springs, depositing travertine — a type of limestone specifically created by such springs — which over time formed a travertine dam across the canyon, which was bored through by the water flowing on the canyon floor. And bingo bango, you've got a bridge.
body.zh: Tonto 天然橋是材料與緩慢、迭代的自然力相結合的結果。熔岩流形成了流紋岩基底，然後古老的海洋被沙子和泥土覆蓋。該沉積層形成石灰岩，再次被熔岩覆蓋，形成玄武岩蓋，該玄武岩蓋因侵蝕和構造活動而破裂和移動，形成了現在的松溪峽谷。當水通過破碎的蓋子向下過濾並進入下面的石灰岩時，就形成了富含礦物質的石灰岩含水層。然後，這些含水層中的水以泉水的形式返回地表，沉積出石灰華（一種由此類泉水專門形成的石灰岩），隨著時間的推移，石灰華壩形成橫跨峽谷，並被峽谷底部流動的水所沖穿。宾果班戈，你有一座桥。

body.en: Tonto Natural Bridge is a geological wonder not only because it is believed to be the largest natural travertine bridge in the world, but also because the area contains a gap in the geological record, with some 225 million years (starting 300 million years ago and ending 75 million years ago) unaccounted for in the surrounding rock formations. In a similarly numerically-staggering manner, consider this: a person underneath the bridge can stand with their feet on the rhyolite and their hands on the travertine, thus spanning a period of millions of years with just the length of their body.
body.zh: 通托天然橋是一個地質奇觀，不僅因為它被認為是世界上最大的天然石灰華橋，還因為該地區在地質記錄中存在一個空白，周圍的岩層大約有 2.25 億年（開始於 3 億年前，結束於 7,500 萬年前）下落不明。以類似的數字驚人的方式，考慮一下：橋下的人可以腳踩流紋岩，手放在石灰華上站立，從而僅用身體的長度就跨越了數百萬年的時間。

body.en: Tonto Natural Bridge was discovered in 1877 by a Scottish prospector named David Gowan, who was being chased by Apaches and needed a place to hide. After hiding in the tunnel for three days and two nights, he laid claim to the bridge and canyon via squatter's rights and moved the rest of his family over from Scotland in 1898. The Gowan family lived in the area until 1948, and their lodge still stands as part of Tonto Natural Bridge State Park, which was formed in 1990 to preserve the area.
body.zh: 通托天然橋 (Tonto Natural Bridge) 於 1877 年由一位名叫大衛·高恩 (David Gowan) 的蘇格蘭探礦者發現，當時他正被阿帕奇直升機追趕，需要一個藏身之處。在隧道裡躲了三天兩夜後，他透過佔屋者的權利對橋樑和峽谷提出了所有權，並於 1898 年將家人從蘇格蘭搬了過來。高恩家族一直居住在該地區直到 1948 年，他們的小屋仍然是通托天然橋州立公園的一部分，該公園於 1990 年成立，旨在保護該地區。

body.en: This 183-foot high bridge is beautiful from every angle. The three hiking trails in the area bring you all the way down to the 400-foot long tunnel. If you are not afraid of slipping on some algae, you can make your way through the tunnel to one of the other trails. Tonto Natural Bridge will not disappoint any visitor. There are viewing points from above so those who are not in the hiking mood can still enjoy the beautiful scenery.
body.zh: 這座 183 英尺高的橋樑從各個角度看都很美麗。該地區的 3 條遠足小徑可帶您一路到達 400 英尺長的隧道。如果您不怕被藻類絆倒，可以穿過隧道前往其他小徑之一。通托天然桥不会让任何游客失望。上面有觀景點，所以沒有健行心情的人仍然可以欣賞美麗的風景。

body.en: Get more unusual and extraordinary places each week with the Atlas Obscura Places newsletter.
body.zh: 每週透過 Atlas Obscura Places 通訊了解更多不尋常和非凡的地方。

address: Nf-583A, Tonto Natural Bridge State Park, Pine, Arizona, 85544

title.en: Tonto National Monument Upper Cliff Dwelling
title.zh: 通托國家紀念碑上崖住宅

excerpt.en: This 40-room dwelling tucked within a cliff was built by the basin's prehistoric residents.
excerpt.zh: 這座隱藏在懸崖內的 40 個房間的住宅是由盆地的史前居民建造的。

body.en: You’ll find much more than cacti and desert critters at the Tonto National Monument. This sliver of central Arizona offers an exceptional example of prehistoric cliff dwellings built by members of the Salado culture.
body.zh: 在通托國家紀念碑，您會發現的不僅僅是仙人掌和沙漠生物。亞利桑那州中部的這片地區是薩拉多文化成員建造的史前懸崖住宅的典範。

body.en: A moderate 1.5-mile hike through the basin brings you to the Upper Cliff Dwelling, which features 40 rooms and boasts panoramic views of the Tonto Basin and Theodore Roosevelt Lake. The dwelling is built into a large, shallow cave near the crest of the mountain.
body.zh: 穿過盆地步行 1.5 英里即可抵達 Upper Cliff Dwelling，這裡設有 40 間客房，可欣賞到 Tonto 盆地和西奧多·羅斯福湖的全景。該住宅建在山頂附近的一個又大又淺的洞穴中。

body.en: This enormous architectural marvel was built in 1300 CE, with construction continuing until its residents abandoned the area sometime between 1400 and 1450 CE. While exploring the cave, you’ll find partially intact roofs, old door lintels, and even rooms that once stood three stories tall.
body.zh: 這座巨大的建築奇蹟建於西元 1300 年，施工一直持續到西元 1400 年至 1450 年期間居民放棄該地區為止。在探索洞穴時，您會發現部分完好的屋頂、古老的門楣，甚至曾經是三層樓高的房間。

body.en: You can’t explore this dwelling on your own, though. Access is only via guided tours offered through the National Park Service.
body.zh: 不過，您無法獨自探索這棟住宅。只能透過國家公園管理局提供的導遊服務進入。

body.en: If you can’t snag a spot on an Upper Cliff Dwelling tour, you can still check out another cliff dwelling within the national monument. The Lower Cliff Dwelling doesn’t require a tour to visit, allowing you to view its 20 rooms at your own pace. A paved trail leads to the site, making it more accessible and more visited than the Upper Cliff Dwelling.
body.zh: 如果您無法參加上懸崖住宅之旅，您仍然可以參觀國家紀念碑內的另一個懸崖住宅。下懸崖住宅不需要跟團參觀，您可以按照自己的步調參觀其 20 間房間。一條鋪好的小路通往該地點，比上懸崖住宅更容易到達，也更容易參觀。

body.en: Get more unusual and extraordinary places each week with the Atlas Obscura Places newsletter.
body.zh: 每週透過 Atlas Obscura Places 通訊了解更多不尋常和非凡的地方。

title.en: Mat Bevel's Museum of Kinetic Art & Surrealistic Pop Science Theater
title.zh: 馬特貝維爾的動能藝術博物館和超現實主義流行科學劇院

excerpt.en: A Tucson museum and performance space full of found-object movable sculptures.
excerpt.zh: 圖森博物館和表演空間，裡面擺滿了發現的可移動雕塑。

body.en: In an interview with the radio show Studio 360 , artist Ned Schaper said, "Trash is the great medium of our age." We're surrounded by it, he said, so why shouldn't we do something with it?
body.zh: 在接受廣播節目 Studio 360 採訪時，藝術家 Ned Schaper 表示：「垃圾是我們這個時代最偉大的媒介。」他說，我們被它包圍了，那麼為什麼我們不應該利用它做點什麼呢？

body.en: What he's decided to do with it is create sculptures. Over 100 sculptures created from salvaged items fill Schaper's Museum of Kinetic Art in Tucson, Arizona .
body.zh: 他決定用它來創作雕塑。亞利桑那州圖森市的沙佩爾動能藝術博物館 (Schaper's Museum of Kinetic Art) 陳列著 100 多件由回收物品製成的雕塑。

body.en: Old rocking horses. Discarded diving boards. An old drum machine. What used to be trash has been repurposed as art by Schaper, a sculptor, poet, and performance artist whose kinetic sculptures were first seen as part of his theater projects and in other exhibitions across the country before settling into their permanent home at the museum in 1983.
body.zh: 老搖馬。廢棄的跳水板。一台舊鼓機。沙佩爾是一位雕塑家、詩人和行為藝術家，他的動態雕塑最初是他的戲劇計畫和全國各地其他展覽的一部分，後來於 1983 年在博物館永久落腳。

body.en: Schaper says he doesn't necessarily have a plan when he begins assembling his found materials. Instead, he " look[s] at things that come to me and wait for things to fit together. " This results in moveable creations that are unpredictable and unique. The objects aren't just meant for observation, however. The pieces are transformed from sculpture into sets, props, costumes, and characters for Schaper's one-man theater. The story takes place in the magical world of Beveldom, a "lost land of found objects" where discarded relics from our consumer culture find new life under the guidance of General Belief System Technology Project Expert Mat Bevel.
body.zh: 沙珀說，當他開始組裝找到的材料時，他不一定有計劃。相反，他「看著出現在我面前的事物，然後等待它們組合在一起。」這導致了不可預測且獨特的可移動創作。然而，這些物體不僅僅用於觀察。這些作品從雕塑轉變為沙佩爾獨角戲的佈景、道具、服裝和角色。故事發生在 Beveldom 的魔法世界，這是一個“失落的失落之地”，消費文化中廢棄的文物在普遍信仰系統技術項目專家 Mat Bevel 的指導下找到了新的生命。

body.en: Update November 2018: Mat Bevel's Museum of Kinetic Art, the Surrealistic Pop Science Theater, and the School of Intuition are no longer available for private tours, special events, or educational classes. They have instead posted videos streaming content available on Facebook .
body.zh: 2018 年 11 月更新：Mat Bevel 的動能藝術博物館、超現實主義流行科學劇院和直覺學院不再提供私人導覽、特別活動或教育課程。相反，他們在 Facebook 上發布了視訊串流內容。

excerpt.en: Some of the tallest ancient American ruins continue to inspire awe and curiosity.
excerpt.zh: 一些最高的美國古代遺址繼續激發人們的敬畏和好奇。

body.en: Surrounded by a low, earthen wall and a number of agricultural canals, the Casa Grande Ruins in Arizona could have been a residence or a municipal hub, but whatever its original purpose, the four-story dirt pueblo has survived for centuries to give us a glimpse at America's prehistoric history.
body.zh: 亞利桑那州的卡薩格蘭德遺址周圍環繞著低矮的土牆和多條農業運河，它本可以成為住宅或市政中心，但無論其最初的目的是什麼，這座四層泥土村已經保存了幾個世紀，讓我們得以一睹美國的史前歷史。

body.en: In 1694, Padre Eusebio Francisco Kino, a Jesuit missionary, made his way across what is now the American Southwest. He may not have been the first European to encounter the Casa Grande ruins, but he was the first to make note of the ruins in a written account, unwittingly giving the ruins the name meaning "great house" that is still used today.
body.zh: 1694 年，耶穌會傳教士尤西比奧·弗朗西斯科·基諾 (Padre Eusebio Francisco Kino) 穿越了現在的美國西南部地區。他可能不是第一個遇到卡薩格蘭德遺址的歐洲人，但他是第一個在書面記錄中記錄下該遺址的人，無意中給該遺址起了一個名字，意思是“偉大的房子”，並沿用至今。

body.en: Built by the ancient Sonoran people around 1350, the structure was abandoned only a century afterward, and was already in ruins by the time Kino came upon it. Little is known about the people who built Casa Grande except for their agricultural practices, as they left no writing behind, but interest in the ruins increased as expansion in the West continued.
body.zh: 該建築由古代索諾蘭人於 1350 年左右建造，僅一個世紀後就被廢棄，當基諾到達時，它已成為廢墟。人們對建造卡薩格蘭德的人們知之甚少，除了他們的農業實踐之外，因為他們沒有留下任何文字，但隨著西方擴張的繼續，人們對這些廢墟的興趣與日俱增。

body.en: The Great House is only one of a complex of buildings within the site, and only one of a much larger culture that is spread throughout the valley from Tucson to Pheonix. A common feature in many of the sites in the area is a “ball court,” which the Casa Grande site has. It was used for a ball game that appears to have been standardized throughout the area and can be seen to the north of the monument’s parking lot.
body.zh: 大宅只是該遺址內的建築群之一，也是傳播從圖森到菲尼克斯整個山谷的更大文化之一。該地區許多遺址的一個共同特徵是“球場”，卡薩格蘭德遺址也有。它被用於一場球賽，該球賽似乎在整個地區都已標準化，並且可以在紀念碑停車場的北面看到。

body.en: Another feature that is widespread is a series of canals that moved water from the Gila River to fields used for agriculture. In some cases, modern canals like the Central Arizona Project use the same canal pathways.
body.zh: 另一個普遍存在的特徵是一系列運河，將希拉河的水輸送到農業田地。在某些情況下，像亞利桑那中心計畫這樣的現代運河使用相同的運河路徑。

body.en: Casa Grande has elements that allowed for observing the summer solstice, the equinoxes, and for measuring the lunar standstill, a phenomenon that occurs every 18.6 years. These can be seen in the upper corners of the building on the west side.
body.zh: 卡薩格蘭德擁有觀測夏至、春分以及測量月球靜止（每 18.6 年發生一次）的元素。這些可以在西側建築物的上角看到。

excerpt.en: What is the Thing?
excerpt.zh: 那是什麼東西？

body.en: You may not want to drive hundreds of miles out of your way to see The Thing?, but if you ever find yourself traveling along I-10 in southeastern Arizona, you would be remiss not to stop and take a look. This is roadside America at its kitschy best. It would spoil the fun to know ahead of time what The Thing is, but suffice to say the museum features some antique Americana at its best.
body.zh: 您可能不想繞道數百英里去看看“怪形”？但如果您發現自己正沿著亞利桑那州東南部的 10 號州際公路行駛，那麼您不停下來看看就太失職了。這是路邊美國最俗氣的一面。提前知道“The Thing”是什麼會破壞樂趣，但足以說明博物館展示了一些最好的美國古董。

body.en: Don't worry about finding "The Thing?" There are scores of billboards pointing the way. You really CAN'T miss it. There is a very small admission charge and plenty of free parking.
body.zh: 不用擔心找「那個東西」？有許多廣告牌指路。你真的不能錯過它。入場費非常低，並且有充足的免費停車位。

excerpt.en: A motel dedicated to Southwestern nostalgia.
excerpt.zh: 致力於西南懷舊的汽車旅館。

body.en: Traveling across the American Southwest always seems to evoke feelings of nostalgia. It’s hard not to think of cowboys riding along the desert terrain or a family road trip with the car windows lowered and the highway stretching ahead. The Wigwam Motel in Holbrook, Arizona, prides itself on celebrating the motel traditions that gained popularity in the 1950s—a clean, safe, and affordable roadside accommodation.
body.zh: 穿越美國西南部似乎總是會喚起懷舊之情。很難不讓人想起牛仔沿著沙漠騎行，或是家庭公路旅行，車窗降下，高速公路在前方延伸。位於亞利桑那州霍爾布魯克的 Wigwam 汽車旅館以弘揚 20 世紀 50 年代流行的汽車旅館傳統而自豪，即乾淨、安全且價格實惠的路邊住宿。

body.en: Chester E. Lewis first opened the motel in 1950 and his family has run it ever since. There are a few other Wigwam Motels or "villages" still in operation including Wigwam Village #7 in San Bernardino, California, and Wigwam Village #2 in Cave City, Kentucky. There are 15 private "wigwams" at this motel. Despite the name, the structures don't actually resemble wigwams, which are round, domed shelters used by a number of northeastern Native American tribes. They are modeled after tipis, which are tall conical tents that are traditionally used by Indigenous people of the Great Plains.
body.zh: 切斯特·E·劉易斯 (Chester E. Lewis) 於 1950 年首次開設這家汽車旅館，此後一直由其家族經營。還有一些其他 Wigwam 汽車旅館或「村莊」仍在運營，包括加州聖貝納迪諾的 Wigwam Village #7 和肯塔基州凱夫城的 Wigwam Village #2。這家汽車旅館設有 15 間私人「棚屋」。儘管有這個名字，但這些結構實際上並不像棚屋，棚屋是一些美國東北部原住民部落使用的圓形圓頂庇護所。它們以圓錐形帳篷為藍本，圓錐形帳篷是大平原原住民傳統上使用的高大圓錐形帳篷。

body.en: They are a popular, and sometimes co-opted, symbol of Native identity. The original developers thought that "wigwam motel" had a better ring to it than "tipi motel" and the name stuck. There’s also a museum and two smaller tipis that were originally used as restrooms for a former Texaco station. It’s clear that the Wigwam Motel truly embraces many of the iconic associations of the American Southwest: road trips, exploration and the aesthetic virtues and functionality of the tipis of the Plains Indians.
body.zh: 他們是流行的、有時甚至是被選為原住民身分的象徵。最初的開發者認為「wigwam motel」比「tipi motel」聽起來更好，於是這個名字就被保留了下來。這裡還有一座博物館和兩座較小的圓錐形帳篷，原本是用作前德士古車站的衛生間。顯然，威格瓦姆汽車旅館真正融入了美國西南部的許多標誌性元素：公路旅行、探索以及平原印第安人圓錐形帳篷的美學優點和功能性。

body.en: Nestled between the highway and train tracks, this roadside motel comes with all the sounds you might expect. Each vintage "wigwam" comes with its own tiny bathroom, wall heater/fan and creaky bed or two.
body.zh: 這家路邊汽車旅館坐落在高速公路和火車軌道之間，擁有您可能期望的所有聲音。每個老式「棚屋」都配有自己的小浴室、壁式加熱器/風扇和吱吱作響的一兩張床。

excerpt.en: This Route 66 classic sports a giant fiberglass rabbit that you can ride.
excerpt.zh: 這款 66 號公路經典車配備了一隻可以騎乘的巨型玻璃纖維兔子。

body.en: Jack Rabbit Trading Post is a souvenir shop along I-40 in Arizona, just west of Joseph City. The shop is the first of five Route 66 attractions to survive the creation of the interstate with its own, named exit.
body.zh: Jack Rabbit Trading Post 是亞利桑那州 40 號州際公路沿線的紀念品商店，位於約瑟夫城以西。該商店是 66 號公路上五個景點中第一個在州際公路建成後倖存下來並擁有自己的出口的。

body.en: First opened in the 1940s, Jack Rabbit Trading Post is still in operation today, surviving the rise and fall of Route 66, as well as several different owners. Much of this prosperity owes to clever marketing: the original owner, James Taylor – no relation to the folk singer – put up billboards all along the Mother Road, from Arizona to Missouri, a tactic since copied by many a tourist trap. The hand-painted signs depicted the store’s iconic jackrabbit logo, culminating in a final HERE IT IS billboard beside the trading post. Few, if any, of the billboards remain, except for the (now legendary) HERE IT IS sign, which is repainted every few years. Jack Rabbit Trading Post was also parodied in Disney-Pixar’s Cars in 2006. The HERE IT IS sign was shown with a Ford Model T instead of the jackrabbit logo.
body.zh: 傑克兔貿易站於 1940 年代首次開業，至今仍在運營，經歷了 66 號公路的興衰以及幾位不同業主的考驗。這種繁榮很大程度上歸功於巧妙的營銷：原始所有者詹姆斯·泰勒（與這位民謠歌手沒有任何關係）在從亞利桑那州到密蘇裡州的母親之路沿線豎起了廣告牌，這種策略後來被許多旅遊陷阱效仿。手繪標誌描繪了商店標誌性的長耳大野兔標誌，最終形成了貿易站旁的「這裡是」廣告看板。除了每隔幾年重新粉刷一次的「這裡是」標誌（現在已成為傳奇），廣告看板幾乎沒有保留下來。 2006 年，迪士尼-皮克斯的《汽車總動員》中也模仿了傑克兔貿易站。此處的標誌是用福特 T 型車代替傑克兔標誌來顯示的。

excerpt.en: In Tucson a giant metal snake helps pedestrians cross a busy highway.
excerpt.zh: 在圖森，一條巨大的金屬蛇幫助行人穿越繁忙的高速公路。

body.en: Tucson, Arizona, is a city with a devotion to public art, having spent millions on various projects around the city over the past couple of decades, but possibly the most monumental of these projects is the Diamondback Bridge which was constructed in the surprisingly accurate image of a giant rattlesnake.
body.zh: 亞利桑那州圖森市是一座熱衷於公共藝術的城市，在過去的幾十年裡，該市在城市周圍的各種項目上花費了數百萬美元，但這些項目中最具紀念意義的可能是響尾蛇橋，它是按照令人驚訝的精確巨型響尾蛇的形象建造的。

body.en: Built in 2002, the bridge was designed by a local artist who wanted to incorporate the local wildlife into his city project. The bridge, while abstract, is also quite biologically accurate. On one end the entrance to the bridge is shaped like the snake's gaping maw, the long fangs presented as support beams below sinister reptilian eyes. The bridge itself is covered by a metal mesh which forms the snake's body which is painted in the exact hues and gradient of a real rattlesnake. In addition, cars passing beneath the span can see the accurately spaced segments of the beast displayed on the belly. Coming out the... other... end of the snake, there is a tall statue shaped like a tail rattle that juts 30 feet out of the ground, also sculpted and painted biologically correct. Finally (as if this particular serpentine lily needed any gilding), if you walk in just the right place when exiting the bridge, you'll receive a loud and startling "goodbye" rattle from hidden speakers.
body.zh: 這座橋建於 2002 年，由一位當地藝術家設計，他希望將當地野生動物融入他的城市計畫中。這座橋雖然抽象，但在生物學上也相當準確。橋的一端的入口形狀像蛇張開的嘴巴，長長的獠牙在險惡的爬行動物眼睛下方呈現為支撐梁。橋本身覆蓋著金屬網，形成蛇的身體，並以真實響尾蛇的精確色調和梯度繪製。此外，從橋下駛過的汽車還可以看到這頭野獸腹部精確排列的各個部分。從蛇的……另一端出來，有一座高大的雕像，形狀像尾巴撥浪鼓，伸出地面 30 英尺，同樣按照生物學原理進行雕刻和繪製。最後（好像這朵特殊的蛇紋百合需要鍍金一樣），如果你在離開橋時走在正確的地方，你會從隱藏的揚聲器中聽到響亮而令人震驚的“再見”嘎嘎聲。

body.en: When the bridge was first built it was met with a certain amount of backlash from locals who felt it was garish and cheesy, but the artist's vision won out and the bridge remains to this day. Unfortunately, the maintenance budget for the bridge is not quite what it should be and the snake looks like it may need to grow a new skin, peeling paint and cracked concrete signaling its age. Regardless of its wear, though, there is still something novel about strolling cavalierly into the belly of a metal monster.
body.zh: 這座橋剛建成時，遭到了當地人的強烈反對，他們認為這座橋花哨又俗氣，但藝術家的願景最終獲勝，這座橋至今仍保留著。不幸的是，這座橋的維護預算並不完全是它應有的水平，而且這條蛇看起來可能需要長出新的皮膚，剝落的油漆和開裂的混凝土表明它的年齡。不過，不管它的磨損程度如何，漫不經心地走進金屬怪物的肚子裡仍然有一些新奇的感覺。
