excerpt.en: All of the 20 occupied houses in this mostly abandoned town feature some curious display of junk art.
excerpt.zh: 在這座幾乎廢棄的小鎮裡，所有 20 棟有人居住的房屋都展示著一些奇怪的垃圾藝術品。

body.en: Located just a short drive from the deteriorating town of Santa Claus , Chloride seems to resemble any kitschy Wild West village turned tourist trap. But if you look a little deeper, you’ll find something that makes this ghost town stand out: a wonderfully bizarre collection of junk art and a display of giant murals.
body.zh: 克洛賴德距離日益惡化的聖誕老人鎮只有很短的車程，看起來就像任何俗氣的狂野西部村莊變成的旅遊陷阱。但如果你看得更深入一些，你會發現一些讓這座鬼城脫穎而出的東西：奇特的垃圾藝術品收藏和巨型壁畫的展示。

body.en: In science, chloride is an ion used to desalinate seawater into drinking water. Which is ironic, because the Arizona town of the same name is incredibly dry. Founded in 1862 as a silver mining town, Chloride was once home to some 75 mines and 5,000 residents. The local miners excavated minerals like silver, gold, and turquoise for over six decades, until in the late 1920s when the town was burnt to the ground in its (near) entirety. By the 1940s, it had practically become a ghost town.
body.zh: 在科學中，氯離子是一種用來將海水淡化成飲用水的離子。這很諷刺，因為亞利桑那州的同名小鎮非常乾燥。克洛賴德成立於 1862 年，當時是一個銀礦小鎮，曾經擁有約 75 個礦場和 5,000 名居民。當地礦工六十多年來一直在開採銀、金和綠松石等礦物，直到 1920 年代末，該鎮（幾乎）全部被燒毀。到了 20 世紀 40 年代，它幾乎變成了一座鬼城。

body.en: Now Chloride is making a comeback, thanks to tourism. With new attractions like mock gunfights, Arizona’s oldest post office, and “The World’s Only All-Female Gun Fighting Troupe”, the town is a chance to walk through an original Wild West town. Yet amid all this, the two most unique characteristics of Chloride often go unnoticed.
body.zh: 現在，由於旅遊業，氯化物正在捲土重來。該鎮擁有模擬槍戰、亞利桑那州最古老的郵局和“世界上唯一的全女性槍戰團”等新景點，讓您有機會漫步在原始的狂野西部小鎮。然而，在這一切之中，Chloride 的兩個最獨特的特性常常被忽略。

body.en: The bizarre junk art of Chloride can easily be seen along the roadside of the non-historic part of town. Drivers can admire a flamingo made of a gas tank, a tin man with a blue hat, and a junk tree with rusty items hanging from the branches. The graves in the town cemetery are even topped with old telephones. In fact, of the 20 currently-inhabited residences of Chloride, each of them features some display of junk art. One house, for example, features an elaborate bottle tree; another displays a metallic spider next to a caterpillar made of bowling balls.
body.zh: 在城鎮非歷史區的路邊很容易就能看到 Chloride 奇特的垃圾藝術。司機們可以欣賞到由油箱製成的火烈鳥、戴著藍色帽子的鐵皮人，以及樹枝上掛著生鏽物品的垃圾樹。鎮上墓園的墳墓上甚至還放著舊電話。事實上，在 Chloride 目前居住的 20 棟住宅中，每棟都展示了一些垃圾藝術品。例如，一棟房子有一棵精緻的瓶子樹；另一個展示了一隻金屬蜘蛛，旁邊是一條由保齡球製成的毛毛蟲。

body.en: Harder to reach, yet equally worth the visit, are the Murals of Chloride. A 1.3-mile, 4-wheel-drive-only road past abandoned mines and ancient Native American petroglyphs will take you up the hill to the murals of Roy Purcell, who, in 1966, was a local prospector with some extra time on his hands. Not yet showing the signs of weathering, Purcell’s “The Journey” covers 2,000 square feet of cliffside granite and is dense in symbolism, featuring a yin yang, a giant red snake spanning multiple rocks, and a fertility goddess.
body.zh: 氯化物壁畫較難到達，但同樣值得一遊。一條全長 1.3 英里的四輪驅動道路，經過廢棄礦井和古老的美洲原住民岩畫，將帶您上山，欣賞羅伊·珀塞爾 (Roy Purcell) 的壁畫。 1966 年，羅伊·珀塞爾 (Roy Purcell) 是當地的探礦者，有一些空閒時間。珀塞爾的「旅程」尚未顯示出風化的跡象，它覆蓋了 2,000 平方英尺的懸崖邊花崗岩，具有濃鬱的象徵意義，包括陰陽、橫跨多塊岩石的巨大紅蛇和生育女神。

body.en: Get more unusual and extraordinary places each week with the Atlas Obscura Places newsletter.
body.zh: 每週透過 Atlas Obscura Places 通訊了解更多不尋常和非凡的地方。

excerpt.en: These free-roaming horses were once destined to disappear from the land.
excerpt.zh: 這些自由馳騁的馬匹曾經注定要從這片土地上消失。

body.en: Wild horses running freely beneath a great, open sky is an iconic symbol of the American West, though seeing the powerful animals in person isn’t always a guarantee. Catching a glimpse of these particular horses feels like an extra special treat, as they were once destined to disappear from the land.
body.zh: 野馬在廣闊的天空下自由奔跑是美國西部的標誌性象徵，儘管並不總是保證親眼目睹這些強大的動物。瞥見這些特殊的馬感覺像是一種特別的享受，因為它們曾經註定要從這片土地上消失。

body.en: The hundreds of horses that live within the Tonto National Forest and roam along the banks of the Salt River are technically feral, as they’re the descendants of horses the Spanish re-introduced to North America during their conquests of the New World. However, as with most of the feral horses in the United States , they’re referred to as “wild.”
body.zh: 生活在通托國家森林內並沿著鹽河沿岸漫步的數百匹馬嚴格意義上來說是野生的，因為它們是西班牙人在征服新世界期間重新引入北美的馬的後代。然而，與美國的大多數野馬一樣，它們被稱為“野馬”。

body.en: According to state records, the Salt River herd has been roaming the land freely since before the Tonto National Forest was designated in 1902. But though they’d been living on the land for at least a century, the horses’ fates were uncertain in the early 21st century. In 2015, the United States Forest Service issued a notice declaring the herd as “unauthorized livestock” and announced a plan to capture, remove, and auction off any unclaimed horses.
body.zh: 根據國家記錄，自 1902 年指定通托國家森林之前，鹽河馬群就一直在這片土地上自由漫步。儘管它們已經在這片土地上生活了至少一個世紀，但在 21 世紀初，這些馬的命運仍不確定。 2015年，美國林務局發布通知，宣布該馬群為“未經授權的牲畜”，並宣布計劃捕獲、移除和拍賣任何無人認領的馬匹。

body.en: The apparent end of the Salt River horses spurred local advocates into action. The Salt River Wild Horse Management Group was formed and successfully reached an agreement with the Arizona Department of Agriculture. Now, the nonprofit group manages the horses and attempts to control the population by darting the animals with a birth control vaccine.
body.zh: 鹽河馬的明顯終結促使當地倡議者採取行動。鹽河野馬管理集團成立，並成功與亞利桑那州農業部達成協議。現在，這個非營利組織負責管理這些馬匹，並試圖透過給動物注射避孕疫苗來控制馬匹數量。

body.en: It’s possible to rent kayaks near the start of the river and paddle through their territory, which creates a high likelihood of seeing the horses in or along the river. (Please be careful not to disturb them, and take only pictures from a safe distance.)
body.zh: 可以在河源附近租用皮划艇並劃過它們的領地，這樣就很有可能在河中或沿河看到馬匹。 （請注意不要打擾它們，並僅在安全距離內拍照。）

body.en: Even if you don’t catch a glimpse of any elusive equines, the river itself is beautiful, particularly early in the morning. Many other animals including blue heron, bald eagles, and river otters frequent its banks. It is for the most part a gentle river, although there are some class 1 rapids in sections.
body.zh: 即使您看不到任何難以捉摸的馬匹，河流本身也很美麗，尤其是在清晨。許多其他動物，包括藍鷺、禿鷹和水獺，經常出現在河岸上。儘管部分河段有一些一級急流，但它大部分是一條平緩的河流。

excerpt.en: For those going through a life transition, a place to leave behind a piece of your former self.
excerpt.zh: 對於那些正在經歷人生轉變的人來說，這是一個可以留下一些以前的自我的地方。

body.en: In 2020, to honor outgoing Atlas Obscura CEO David Plotz and his five years of service to the company, his colleagues purchased 1.18 acres of land in the middle of the Arizona desert on eBay. Located a mile from Arizona's Petrified Forest National Park , and 2,500 feet from historic Route 66, the Plotz Plot is the first place in the Atlas Obscura database created by Atlas Obscura itself.
body.zh: 2020 年，為了紀念即將離任的 Atlas Obscura 執行長 David Plotz 及其對該公司五年的服務，他的同事在 eBay 上購買了位於亞利桑那州沙漠中部的 1.18 英畝土地。 Plotz 地塊距離亞利桑那州石化森林國家公園 1 英里，距離歷史悠久的 66 號公路 2,500 英尺，是 Atlas Obscura 自己創建的 Atlas Obscura 資料庫中的第一個位置。

body.en: Visitors to the Plotz Plot will discover an orange metal shed with a sign that reads: “For those experiencing a life transition: This is a place to leave behind a piece of your former self.”
body.zh: 參觀 Plotz Plot 的遊客會發現一個橙色的金屬棚，上面寫著：“對於那些正在經歷人生轉變的人來說：這是一個可以留下你以前的自我的地方。”

body.en: Inside, shelves hold objects donated by members of the Atlas Obscura community who find themselves in the midst of personal transformation, and who wish to cast off a bit of their old lives. The first contribution to the Plotz Plot came from David Plotz himself. Its tag reads:
body.zh: 裡面的架子上擺滿了 Atlas Obscura 社區成員捐贈的物品，他們發現自己正處於個人轉變之中，並希望擺脫一些舊的生活。 Plotz Plot 的第一個貢獻來自 David Plotz 本人。它的標籤寫著：

body.en: This Deuter Giga Bike Backpack represents the time I spent as CEO of Atlas Obscura. For more than five years, I commuted from my home in Washington to our headquarters in Brooklyn . I would say goodbye to family early Monday morning, board an Amtrak train, and return home late each Wednesday night. This backpack was my constant companion during those years. Now, I am leaving Atlas Obscura—and this backpack—behind to take my next adventure. —David Plotz, February 2020
body.zh: 這款 Deuter Giga 自行車背包代表了我擔任 Atlas Obscura 執行長的時光。五年多來，我從華盛頓的家到布魯克林的總部。我會在周一早上與家人告別，登上美鐵列車，然後在每週三深夜回家。那些年，這個背包是我不變的伴侶。現在，我將離開 Atlas Obscura 和這個背包，開始我的下一次冒險。 ——大衛‧普洛茨，2020 年 2 月

body.en: The Plotz Plot is a pilgrimage site for people navigating major life transitions of all kinds. We invite those who find themselves in the midst of a personal transformation to cast off a symbol of their old lives, and leave it behind as a memento inside this growing museum. All are welcome to contribute.
body.zh: Plotz Plot 是人們經歷各種重大人生轉變的朝聖地。我們邀請那些發現自己正處於個人轉變的人拋棄他們過去生活的象徵，並將其作為紀念品留在這個不斷發展的博物館中。歡迎大家踴躍投稿。

body.en: We ask that any contributions be appropriately tagged. The code for the combination lock is “4444.” Please re-lock the door upon leaving.
body.zh: 我們要求任何貢獻都被適當標記。密碼鎖的密碼是「4444」。離開時請重新鎖門。

excerpt.en: Come for the pizza, stay for a performance on the world's largest theater pipe organ.
excerpt.zh: 來吃披薩，留下來欣賞世界上最大的劇院管風琴的表演。

body.en: Rather than a pizza shop with an organ in it, Organ Stop Pizza is an organ show that serves pizza. Each night in Mesa, Arizona, the largest theater pipe organ ever created rises on an 8,000-pound rotating hydraulic elevator to sit 10 feet above the nearly always at-capacity 700-seat dining room, brought to roaring life by virtuoso theater organists while patrons sup on pizza, pasta, and sandwiches under disco balls and spotlights. The 276-key organ is linked to a mind-boggling series of xylophones, glockenspiels, gongs, and cymbals. Marionette cats dance in unison within a recessed “stage” perched above the behemoth instrument. Co-owner Jack Barz recalls tourists who compared their experience at Organ Stop to the one they had at the Grand Canyon the day prior . One YouTuber called it “American eccentricism at its finest.”
body.zh: Organ Stop Pizza不是裡面有風琴的披薩店，而是一個供應披薩的風琴表演。每天晚上，在亞利桑那州梅薩，有史以來最大的劇院管風琴會在 8,000 磅重的旋轉液壓電梯上升起，位於幾乎始終容納 700 個座位的餐廳上方 10 英尺處，藝術大師的劇院管風琴演奏家將這裡演繹得栩栩如生，而顧客則在迪斯科披薩和聚光燈下享用、意大利面和三明治。這個 276 鍵的風琴與一系列令人難以置信的木琴、鐘琴、鑼和鈸相連。木偶貓在巨型樂器上方的凹進「舞台」內齊聲跳舞。合夥人傑克·巴茲 (Jack Barz) 回憶起遊客們將他們在風琴站的經歷與前一天在大峽谷的經歷進行了比較。一位 YouTuber 稱其為“美國最古怪的行為”。

body.en: The landmark attraction was the brainchild of the late William P. Brown, a veteran of both World War II and Wharton Business School. The real-estate developer, pizza enthusiast, and accomplished theater organist found ample time to pursue these varying interests and in fact saw no reason he couldn’t combine them. The original Organ Stop Pizza, opened in Phoenix in 1972, was such a success that it led to a second, larger franchise in Mesa three years later. Brown retired from the restaurant industry in 1984, selling the Mesa location to a longtime employee and manager, Mike Everitt, who carried Brown’s charge to continuously acquire rare parts and expand the organ—so much so that Organ Stop had to change locations in 1995 to accommodate its new dimensions.
body.zh: 這個具有里程碑意義的景點是已故的威廉·P·布朗 (William P. Brown) 的創意，他是二戰老兵和沃頓商學院的退伍軍人。這位房地產開發商、披薩愛好者和出色的劇院風琴師有充足的時間來追求這些不同的興趣，事實上，他沒有理由不能將它們結合起來。最初的 Organ Stop Pizza 於 1972 年在鳳凰城開業，取得了巨大成功，三年後在梅薩開設了第二家更大的特許經營店。 1984 年，布朗從餐飲業退休，將梅薩店賣給了一位長期僱員兼經理邁克·埃弗里特 (Mike Everitt)，邁克·埃弗里特 (Mike Everitt) 負責不斷獲取稀有零件並擴建風琴，以至於風琴站不得不在 1995 年更換地點以適應新的規模。

body.en: Today, 42-foot-tall ceilings accommodate balcony seating for viewing the record-holding 1927 Wurlitzer console (insured for up to $5 million ). Four industrial blowers pump pressurized air through the organ’s 6,000 pipes, allowing the Pizza Stop’s 300,000 annual dinner patrons to enjoy timeless compositions such as “The Flight of the Bumblebee,” “The Hills Are Alive” from The Sound of Music, “The Circle of Life” from The Lion King, the Star Wars opening theme, and of course, “God Bless America.”
body.zh: 如今，42 英尺高的天花板設有陽台座位，可觀賞 1927 年創下紀錄的 Wurlitzer 混音器（保險金額高達 500 萬美元）。四台工業鼓風機透過管風琴的 6,000 根管道泵送壓縮空氣，讓 Pizza Stop 的 300,000 名年度晚餐顧客能夠欣賞到永恆的作品，如《大黃蜂的飛翔》、《音樂之聲》中的《山丘生機》、《王者王輪》中的《大黃蜂的飛翔》、《音樂之聲》中的《山丘生機》、《王者王》中的《星際大戰》中的《生命之輪》，當然還有《星際星球大戰》。

body.en: Your newsletter subscriptions with us are subject to Atlas Obscura's Privacy Policy and Terms of Use .
body.zh: 您向我們訂閱的電子報須遵守 Atlas Obscura 的隱私權政策和使用條款。

body.en: Hours are seasonal, so check in advance. The organist begins playing 30 minutes after opening and the kitchen shuts down 30 minutes before closing time, so plan accordingly.
body.zh: 營業時間是季節性的，因此請提前檢查。風琴師在開放後 30 分鐘開始演奏，廚房在關門前 30 分鐘關閉，因此請做好相應計劃。

body.en: lukefater
body.zh: 路克法特

excerpt.en: A mysterious spirit totem at the edge of Navajo lands.
excerpt.zh: 納瓦荷土地邊緣的神秘精神圖騰。

body.en: No one seems to know the origin of the spirit totem nor exactly how long it's been present on "Deadman Flats" and the edge of Navajo lands. Locals will tell you the totem has been around "a very long time" or "for as long as I remember."
body.zh: 似乎沒有人知道精神圖騰的起源，也不知道它在「亡靈平地」和納瓦荷土地邊緣存在了多久。當地人會告訴您，圖騰已經存在「很長一段時間」或「從我記事起就存在」。

body.en: Wupatki National Monument, a place of ancient pueblos, is just east of the totem, as is the Navajo sacred place, Chezzhin Deez'd, Black Point or Black-Rock Point, an ancient basalt lava flow where the founders of the Western Water Clans journeyed eastward from the point of their creation on the shore of the Pacific Ocean, crossed the Little Colorado on their way from the San Francisco Peaks.
body.zh: 伍帕特基國家紀念碑（Wupatki National Monument）是古代普韋布洛人的聚集地，就在圖騰的東邊，還有納瓦霍人的聖地 Chezzhin Deez'd、Black Point 或 Black-Rock Point，這是一條古老的玄武岩熔岩流，西部水族的創始人從他們在太平洋沿岸的創造點向東航行，從舊金山山峰穿越小山。

body.en: Travelers often leave gifts and tokens in the totems. Possibly it is for safe travels, maybe it is in respect to the ancients who travelled past years ago.
body.zh: 旅行者經常在圖騰中留下禮物和信物。也許是為了安全出行，也許是為了致敬多年前遠行的古人。

body.en: Get more unusual and extraordinary places each week with the Atlas Obscura Places newsletter.
body.zh: 每週透過 Atlas Obscura Places 通訊了解更多不尋常和非凡的地方。

body.en: Your newsletter subscriptions with us are subject to Atlas Obscura's Privacy Policy and Terms of Use .
body.zh: 您向我們訂閱的電子報須遵守 Atlas Obscura 的隱私權政策和使用條款。

body.en: Located on the East side of US Hwy 89, about 100 yards. north of mile post 443. It’s about 1.5 miles south of the Wupatki National Monument. One can pull well off the highway onto a dirt pullout.
body.zh: 位於美國89號高速公路東側，約100碼。 443 英里後以北。位於 Wupatki 國家紀念碑以南約 1.5 英里處。人們可以把車從高速公路開到泥土路上。

excerpt.en: An old saloon in the West filled with history, and according to some, a few dozen ghosts.
excerpt.zh: 西方的一家老酒館充滿了歷史，據一些人說，有幾十個鬼魂。

body.en: Tombstone, Arizona is home to many Wild West legends, and the Bird Cage Theater is no exception. Open from 1881-1889, the Theater was a saloon, a bar, a theater, and a brothel, with the ladies hung from the ceiling in crib style rooms named "bird cages."
body.zh: 亞利桑那州墓碑鎮是許多狂野西部傳奇的故鄉，鳥籠劇院也不例外。劇院於 1881 年至 1889 年間開放，曾是一家沙龍、一家酒吧、一家劇院和一家妓院，女士們被懸掛在名為“鳥籠”的嬰兒床式房間的天花板上。

body.en: Wyatt Earp and Doc Holiday drank and played cards there, and many were murdered there as well. Bullet holes still show in parts of the stage and the walls.
body.zh: 懷亞特·厄普（Wyatt Earp）和霍樂迪醫生（Doc Holiday）在那裡喝酒、打牌，許多人也在那裡被謀殺。舞台和牆壁的部分地方仍可見彈孔。

body.en: According to the operators of the saloon 26 ghosts apparently still love to party at this historic brothel/saloon in Southern Arizona, and it is a frequent stop for ghost hunters from all over the world. Supposedly shouting and loud music is sometimes heard at night, and some tourists have claimed smelling cigar smoke and whiskey in the air.
body.zh: 據該酒吧的經營者稱，26 個鬼魂顯然仍然喜歡在亞利桑那州南部這家歷史悠久的妓院/酒吧舉行派對，這裡也是來自世界各地的捉鬼者經常光顧的地方。據稱，夜間有時會聽到喊叫聲和響亮的音樂，一些遊客聲稱在空氣中聞到了雪茄煙霧和威士忌的味道。

body.en: After years of being closed, the Bird Cage was reopened for tourists in 1934. The night tour is probably best to experience a spooky time, but perhaps even more interesting then the "paranormal phenomena" are all the wonderful original historical artifacts perfectly preserved since 1889.
body.zh: 關閉多年後，鳥籠於 1934 年重新向遊客開放。夜間遊覽可能是體驗恐怖時光的最佳選擇，但也許比「超自然現象」更有趣的是自 1889 年以來完美保存的所有精彩的原始歷史文物。

body.en: Your newsletter subscriptions with us are subject to Atlas Obscura's Privacy Policy and Terms of Use .
body.zh: 您向我們訂閱的電子報須遵守 Atlas Obscura 的隱私權政策和使用條款。

body.en: I-10 to Benson, take Hwy 80 South. Plenty of parking away from Allen Street. Admission is $14 for adults. They have military and senior discounts as well.Small dogs are permitted in the museum if they can be carried. Very well-behaved bigger dogs are allowed as well, if you ask nicely.
body.zh: 搭乘 I-10 州際公路前往本森 (Benson)，沿著 80 號高速公路向南行駛。遠離艾倫街有充足的停車位。成人入場費為 14 美元。他們還提供軍人和老年人折扣。如果可以攜帶小狗，則可以進入博物館。如果您提出好意的話，也可以飼養行為良好的大型犬。

address: 533 East Allen St., P.O. Box 248, Tombstone, Arizona, 85638

excerpt.en: Over 100,000 items, ranging from the skeletons of vampire bats and baby pigs to meteorites and the skull of a Roman gladiator.
excerpt.zh: 超過 10 萬件物品，從吸血蝙蝠和小豬的骨頭到隕石和羅馬角鬥士的頭骨。

body.en: Not far from Old Tucson, a studio town built in the 1950s for filming westerns, a large canvas teepee and a bright red tyrannosaurus rex flank an old wooden storefront that looks like it could be in a classic Western movie.
body.zh: 距離老圖森不遠，這是一個建於 20 世紀 50 年代為拍攝西部片而建的工作室小鎮，一個巨大的帆布圓錐形帳篷和一隻鮮紅色的霸王龍位於一個古老的木製店面旁邊，看起來就像是經典西部片中的場景。

body.en: Tucson Mineral and Gem World has been around since 1968. The place is a cabinet of wonder in the middle of the desert. The Arizona rock shop/museum combo touts over 100,000 items, ranging from the skeletons of vampire bats and baby pigs to meteorites.
body.zh: 圖森礦物和寶石世界 (Tucson Mineral and Gem World) 始建於 1968 年。這個地方就像是沙漠中央的一個奇蹟櫃。亞利桑那州的搖滾商店/博物館組合出售超過 100,000 件物品，從吸血蝙蝠和小豬的骨骼到隕石，應有盡有。

body.en: Alongside a tall filing cabinet filled with alphabetized minerals like copper and quartz, the shop keeps meteorites, fossils, and a dried rattlesnake head. Visitors are encouraged to explore the old building, but preferably pay for anything you want to leave with.
body.zh: 除了一個高大的文件櫃，裡面裝滿了銅和石英等按字母順序排列的礦物，這家商店還存放著隕石、化石和乾響尾蛇頭。我們鼓勵遊客探索這座古老的建築，但最好為想要離開的任何東西付費。

body.en: In April 2016, someone got away with three skulls: a Roman gladiator, a Spanish conquistador (from 1541), and a Mexican soldier (from the battle of the Alamo). They were among the shop’s most prized possessions, and have been featured in plenty of selfies taken in the old desert store.
body.zh: 2016 年 4 月，有人偷走了三個頭骨：一名羅馬角鬥士、一名西班牙征服者（來自 1541 年）和一名墨西哥士兵（來自阿拉莫戰役）。它們是這家商店最珍貴的財產之一，並出現在這家古老的沙漠商店中拍攝的大量自拍照中。

excerpt.en: Collection of vintage trailers double as hotel rooms.
excerpt.zh: 老式拖車的集合兼作飯店房間。

body.en: Begun in 1927 as trailer and camping spaces for weary travelers it has transformed into a kind of vintage monument and remembrance of times gone by.
body.zh: 它始建於 1927 年，最初是為疲憊的旅行者提供拖車和露營地，現已轉變為一種老式紀念碑和對過去時光的紀念。

body.en: Situated a mile high up the Mule Mountains, in Bisbee, Arizona, (a historic copper mining town) the Shady Dell is home to nine vintage travel trailers. Among them are a 1949 Airstream, a 1950 Spartan Manor and a 33-foot Royal Mansion built in 1951 complete with "leopard carpet, martini glasses, diner-style breakfast booth and phonograph with a collection of 78rpm records." A particularly popular trailer is the "1947 Tiki Bus Polynesian Palace, complete with hand-carved outrigger bar and your own tiki god."
body.zh: 謝迪戴爾 (Shady Dell) 位於亞利桑那州比斯比（歷史悠久的銅礦小鎮）穆爾山脈 (Mule Mountains) 一英里高處，擁有九輛老式旅行拖車。其中包括一輛 1949 年的 Airstream、一座 1950 年的斯巴達莊園和一座建於 1951 年的 33 英尺皇家宅邸，配有“豹紋地毯、馬提尼酒杯、餐廳風格的早餐攤和收藏有 78 轉唱片的留聲機”。一款特別受歡迎的預告片是「1947 年 Tiki 巴士波利尼西亞宮殿，配有手工雕刻的支腿桿和您自己的 Tiki 神」。

body.en: Perfect in every vintage detail, the "vintage radios play era-appropriate radio programs, televisions only broadcast in two colors, period books and magazines allow for even more mental time travel and big-band, early rhythm-and-blues and original rock-and-roll are available for your listening entertainment."
body.zh: 每個復古細節都很完美，“老式收音機播放適合時代的廣播節目，電視僅以兩種顏色播放，時代書籍和雜誌允許更多的精神時間旅行，大樂隊、早期節奏藍調和原創搖滾樂可供您聆聽娛樂。”

body.en: All the trailers are available for overnight stays, but book well in advance as the trailers fill up many months ahead of time. The trailers range in price from $87 to $145 a night.
body.zh: 所有拖車都可以過夜，但請提前預訂，因為拖車會提前幾個月裝滿。拖車的價格從每晚 87 美元到 145 美元不等。

excerpt.en: Don't blink or you'll miss it.
excerpt.zh: 不要眨眼，否則你會錯過它。

body.en: The longest continuous stretch of the Old Route 66 that still remains today is the path from Seligman to Kingman in Arizona, which, at 86 miles, passes by both Delgadillo’s Snow Cap Drive In and the Grand Canyon Caverns . But in the western half of this segment, seemingly unannounced, lies one of the kitschiest stops on the Mother Road.
body.zh: 至今仍保留的老 66 號公路中最長的連續路段是從亞利桑那州的塞利格曼到金曼的道路，全長 86 英里，途經德爾加迪略的雪帽駕車道 (Snow Cap Drive In) 和大峽谷洞穴 (Grand Canyon Caverns)。但在這段路段的西半部，似乎沒有事先通知，坐落著母親路上最俗氣的車站之一。

body.en: Hackberry General Store, located in the former mining town of Hackberry, Arizona, is bypassed by many Route 66 travelers, oftentimes because they simply blink and miss it. Unannounced by signage and isolated in the middle of desert, this hidden gem may be driven by countless times, but those who have decided to pull in know it to be a must stop for all Route 66 travelers.
body.zh: 樸樹雜貨店 (Hackberry General Store) 位於亞利桑那州樸樹鎮 (Hackberry) 的前礦業小鎮，許多 66 號公路旅行者都會繞過樸樹雜貨店 (Hackberry General Store)，通常是因為他們只是眨眼就錯過了。這顆隱藏的瑰寶沒有任何指示牌，而且與世隔絕，可能已經被駕駛過無數次，但那些決定停車的人都知道，它是所有 66 號公路旅行者的必經之地。

body.en: Nicknamed the “Mother Lode of Mother Road Memorabilia”, the Hackberry General Store is packed wall to wall with historic signs and artifacts. It also features a root beer bar and an internationally recognized shelter dog (best known for its spot on Harley Davidson and United Airlines commercials). The exterior of the general store is just as quirky. Historic Pegasus gas pumps, rusted-over Model As from the early 20th century, and a red ‘57 Corvette are scattered across the general store's facade. A walk around will take you to animal head skeletons, a yellow “jack rabbit crossing" sign, and five original Burma Shave signs.
body.zh: 樸樹百貨商店 (Hackberry General Store) 被稱為“母親之路紀念品的母親礦脈”，牆上掛滿了歷史標誌和文物。它還設有根汁啤酒吧和國際公認的收容所狗（以其在哈雷戴維森和聯合航空廣告中的位置而聞名）。雜貨店的外觀也同樣奇特。歷史悠久的 Pegasus 加油泵、生鏽的 20 世紀初的 Model As 以及一輛紅色的 57 款 Corvette 散落在雜貨店的正面。繞一圈走一圈，您會看到動物頭骨、黃色的「傑克兔十字路口」標誌和五個原始的緬甸剃須標誌。

body.en: Hackberry General Store was once a lifeline for a few dozen people. In 1874, when silver was discovered in the area, the town of Hackberry was founded, home of “shooting, fighting, and faro.” The town grew in 1882, when a railroad was built through Hackberry, allowing ranchers and miners to export their products further than ever before. Unfortunately, the nearest place to find groceries, gas, and other needs was Kingman, a full day’s drive in a Model A. Although it only served a small community of workers, the Hackberry General Store was a vital resource for the town.
body.zh: 樸樹雜貨店曾經是幾十個人的生命線。 1874 年，當該地區發現銀礦時，樸樹鎮成立，成為「射擊、格鬥和法羅」的故鄉。 1882 年，一條穿過樸樹的鐵路建成，使牧場主和礦工能夠將產品出口到比以往更遠的地方，該鎮隨之發展。不幸的是，最近的購買雜貨、汽油和其他必需品的地方是金曼，乘坐 A 型車需要一整天的車程。雖然它只為一小部分工人提供服務，但樸樹雜貨店卻是鎮上的重要資源。

body.en: Unfortunately, Hackberry lost its main draw and nearly became a ghost town in 1919, when the Hackberry Silver Mine was closed down. However, it was revitalized a few decades later, when Route 66’s path crossed directly through town.
body.zh: 不幸的是，1919 年樸樹銀礦被關閉，樸樹失去了它的主要吸引力，幾乎成為鬼城。然而，幾十年後，當 66 號公路直接穿過城鎮時，它又重新煥發了活力。

body.en: As of now, Hackberry has a population of 68 and is a unique must-stop for those who get their kicks on Route 66.
body.zh: 截至目前，Hackberry 人口已達 68 人，對於那些喜歡 66 號公路的人來說，這是一個獨特的必經之地。

title.en: Coit Museum of Pharmacy and Health Sciences
title.zh: 科伊特藥學與健康科學博物館

excerpt.en: An Arizona museum with a collection of pharmaceutical oddities, including a jar of a gangster's chewed gum.
excerpt.zh: 亞利桑那州的一家博物館，收藏了一些奇怪的藥品，其中包括一罐黑幫口香糖。

body.en: Renamed the Coit Museum of Pharmacy and Health Sciences in 2022, the museum has been a well-kept secret at the University of Arizona. Its unique collection documents the pharmacy profession from the 19th and 20th centuries, complete with thousands of medical curiosities.
body.zh: 該博物館於 2022 年更名為科伊特藥房和健康科學博物館，一直是亞利桑那大學保守的秘密。其獨特的收藏記錄了 19 世紀和 20 世紀的藥學行業，其中包括數以千計的醫學珍品。

body.en: In 1966, the museum opened in the UA College of Pharmacy, which was less than 20 years old at the time. Former State Board Inspector Jesse Hurlbut had amassed a collection of thousands of items from drugstores all over Arizona. After he retired, he donated them to the school to found a small museum. For the last half-century, the museum has continued to grow as it celebrates and preserves the rich history of the practice of pharmacy.
body.zh: 1966年，博物館在當時成立不到20年的UA藥學院開幕。前州委員會檢查員傑西·赫爾布特從亞利桑那州各地的藥局收集了數千件物品。退休後，他將它們捐贈給學校，建立了一個小型博物館。在過去的半個世紀中，博物館不斷發展壯大，慶祝並保存了豐富的藥學實踐歷史。

body.en: The museum features a fascinating collection from the Upjohn Pharmacy in Disneyland, a full-scale replica of an old-time drugstore, and a jar of gangster John Dillinger's chewed gum. In addition to its new dedicated space in room 260 of the Skaggs Pharmaceutical Sciences building, its exhibits extend throughout the College of Pharmacy, in both the Skaggs and Drachman Hall buildings.
body.zh: 博物館擁有來自迪士尼樂園 Upjohn 藥房的迷人藏品、一家老式藥房的全尺寸複製品，以及一罐黑幫約翰·迪林格的口香糖。除了位於 Skaggs 製藥科學大樓 260 室的新專用空間外，其展品還延伸到整個藥學院的 Skaggs 和 Drachman Hall 大樓。

excerpt.en: An urban laboratory.
excerpt.zh: 一個城市實驗室。

body.en: Using a concept he calls arcology, architect Paolo Soleri began construction on Arcosanti in 1970. This experimental city was constructed in order to demonstrate how urban conditions could be improved while minimizing the destructive impact on the earth. A lack of funding has somewhat crippled the town-site, originally intended to house over 5000 people. The current population varies between 50-150 persons, based on the number of students and volunteers on the site.
body.zh: 建築師保羅·索萊裡 (Paolo Soleri) 運用他稱之為「生態學」的概念，於 1970 年開始建造阿爾科桑蒂。建造這座實驗城市的目的是為了展示如何改善城市條件，同時最大限度地減少對地球的破壞性影響。由於缺乏資金，這座原本可容納 5,000 多人的城鎮受到了一定程度的破壞。根據現場學生和志工的數量，目前的人數在 50 至 150 人之間。

body.en: The layout of the buildings is intricate and organic, rather than a typical city grid. The current structures include a five-story visitors' center/cafe/gift shop, a bronze-casting apse, a ceramics apse, an outdoor amphitheater, a community swimming pool, an office complex, as well as a ring of apartment residences and storefronts. Arcosanti also maintains greenhouses, gardens, and agricultural fields.
body.zh: 建築物的佈局錯綜複雜且有機，而不是典型的城市網格。目前的建築包括一個五層樓的遊客中心/咖啡館/禮品店、一個青銅鑄造後殿、一個陶瓷後殿、一個室外圓形劇場、一個社區游泳池、一個辦公大樓以及一圈公寓住宅和店面。 Arcosanti 也維護溫室、花園和農田。

body.en: Construction continues as students from around the world visit in order to attend workshops and classes. Funding is aided by the sale of artistic bells, crafted onsite, and the 50,000 tourists that visit each year.
body.zh: 隨著來自世界各地的學生前來參加研討會和課程，施工仍在繼續。現場製作的藝術編鐘的銷售以及每年 50,000 名遊客的到來為資金提供了幫助。

body.en: Soleri, who was from Italy, enrolled in Frank Lloyd Wright's school of architecture, one of which was located just outside of Scottsdale, Arizona. The two architects had a falling out due to inflated egos and Soleri went off to build Arcosanti, a notable example of Brutalism architecture.
body.zh: 索萊裡來自義大利，就讀於弗蘭克·勞埃德·賴特的建築學院，其中一所學校位於亞利桑那州斯科茨代爾郊外。兩位建築師因自負而爭吵，索萊裡開始建造阿爾科桑蒂，這是粗野主義建築的一個著名例子。

excerpt.en: An artificial crater field that trained astronauts for lunar exploration.
excerpt.zh: 訓練太空人進行月球探索的人造隕石坑場。

body.en: Before the first astronauts ever made it to the moon, they had to have somewhere to practice, and thus the Cinder Lake Crater Field was constructed.
body.zh: 在第一批太空人登上月球之前，他們必須有一個地方進行練習，因此建造了煤渣湖火山口場。

body.en: Chosen for its porous volcanic gravel, the former volcano provided a more than suitable analogue for moon rock. However to accurately simulate the surface of the moon, scientists mapped a portion of the satellite's craters and proceeded to create an exact replica of the pothole field in Cinder Lake. Using hundreds of pounds of dynamite, NASA scientists created an identical field of craters in a carefully ordered series of blasts. Once the simulated moon field was constructed, the astronauts were free to try out their lunar rovers and other equipment from the safety of Earth's gravity.
body.zh: 這座前火山因其多孔的火山礫石而被選中，它為月球岩石提供了非常合適的模擬。然而，為了準確模擬月球表面，科學家們繪製了衛星隕石坑的一部分，並繼續創建了煤渣湖坑坑洼窪的精確複製品。美國太空總署科學家使用數百磅炸藥，在一系列精心安排的爆炸中創造了一個相同的隕石坑區域。一旦模擬月球場建成，太空人就可以在不受地球引力影響的情況下自由測試月球車和其他設備。

body.en: Remnants of the craters still remain today, although many of them have been been filled in and softened into divots by natural erosion and weathering. In addition to the natural deterioration, it now is a portion of a popular designated off-highway vehicle recreation area in the Coconino National Forest, which contributes to the destruction of this historically significant area.
body.zh: 隕石坑的遺跡至今仍然存在，儘管其中許多已被自然侵蝕和風化所填充並軟化成凹痕。除了自然惡化之外，它現在是科科尼諾國家森林中一個受歡迎的指定非公路車輛休閒區的一部分，這導致了這個具有重要歷史意義的地區的破壞。

body.en: From Interstate 40/Purple Heart Trail, take exit 201 (US 89 N to Page), turn north on Country Club Drive, then turn right (northeast) onto Route 89 for about 8 miles. From US-89, turn right (east) onto the unpaved Forest Service Rd 776, and continue about 1.5 miles to the Cinder Hills Off-Highway Vehicle Area. Turn right and head south-southwest through this area about half a mile to reach the crater field.Forest Service Rd 776 may be closed seasonally or due to poor conditions, and may only accessible by 4-wheel-drive vehicles in other conditions. Although all motor vehicles are technically permitted in the Cinder Hills OHV area, vehicles other than ATV's or high-clearance 4-wheel-drive vehicles may get stuck. Road conditions and closures, detailed maps including the boundaries of the Cinder Hills OHV area, fire danger level, and other information is available on the Coconino National Forest website.
body.zh: 從 40 號州際公路/紫心山步道出發，從 201 號出口（US 89 N 至佩奇）出發，沿著鄉村俱樂部大道 (Country Club Drive) 向左轉，然後右轉（向東北）駛入 89 號公路，行駛約 8 英里。從 US-89 出發，右轉（向東）駛入未鋪砌的 Forest Service Rd 776，然後繼續行駛約 1.5 英里到達 Cinder Hills 非公路車輛區。右轉，向西南偏南方向穿過該區域約半英里即可到達火山口場。 Forest Service Rd 776 可能會因季節性或惡劣條件而關閉，在其他情況下只能由四輪驅動車輛通行。儘管技術上允許所有機動車輛進入 Cinder Hills OHV 區域，但除 ATV 或高間隙四輪驅動車輛以外的車輛可能會被卡住。道路狀況和封閉情況、詳細地圖（包括 Cinder Hills OHV 區域的邊界、火災危險等級以及其他資訊）可在可科尼諾國家森林網站上取得。

excerpt.en: A mysterious "wedding cake" castle in the middle of the urban desert.
excerpt.zh: 城市沙漠中一座神秘的「婚禮蛋糕」城堡。

body.en: They say the desert attracts dreamers, schemers, and prophets. A mysterious, fanciful structure that tops a knoll in the Airport Gateway District of Phoenix looks like the work of at least two out of three.
body.zh: 他們說沙漠吸引夢想家、陰謀家和先知。鳳凰城機場門戶區一座小丘頂上有一座神秘而奇特的建築，看起來至少是三分之二的作品。

body.en: Italian immigrant Alessio Carraro dreamed of building a resort hotel as the centerpiece of his high-end subdivision, Carrarro Heights. He and his son constructed the hotel over just fourteen months, between 1928 and 1930. The building was a thing of beauty, based on Italian architecture and tiered like a wedding cake.
body.zh: 義大利移民阿萊西奧·卡拉羅 (Alessio Carraro) 夢想建造一家度假酒店，作為他的高端住宅區卡拉羅高地 (Carrarro Heights) 的核心。 1928 年至 1930 年間，他和兒子僅用了 14 個月的時間就建造了這家酒店。這座建築非常美麗，以義大利建築風格為基礎，層次分明，就像婚禮蛋糕一樣。

body.en: However, perhaps because of the stench from the nearby Tovrea meatpacking stockyards, or because of the Great Depression, it never opened. Carraro sold his castle and its 42 acres to Edward Ambrose Tovrea, magnate of the stockyards, who transformed the massive hotel into a private residence. Tovrea died after less than a year living in the castle, and is memorialized by a giant steel pyramid on the property. His widow Della lived there until her death in 1969.
body.zh: 然而，也許是因為附近托夫雷亞肉類加工堆場的惡臭，或者是因為大蕭條，它從未開業。卡拉羅將他的城堡及其 42 英畝土地賣給了牲畜飼養場大亨愛德華·安布羅斯·托夫雷亞 (Edward Ambrose Tovrea)，後者將這座大型酒店改造成私人住宅。托夫雷亞在城堡裡生活不到一年後就去世了，城堡裡有一座巨大的鋼製金字塔要紀念。他的遺孀德拉一直住在那裡，直到 1969 年去世。

body.en: Over the years Tovrea Castle developed an air of mystery. As Phoenix grew outward and the land surrounding the castle developed into a metropolitan area, the isolated mansion and its acres of desert attracted a lot of attention. After Della's death, the land (which had fallen into ruin) was purchased by the City of Phoenix. The structure was restored, its cactus garden replanted, and the grounds were opened for tours.
body.zh: 多年來，托夫雷亞城堡逐漸散發出神秘的氣息。隨著菲尼克斯向外發展，城堡周圍的土地發展成為大都市區，這座孤立的宅邸及其數英畝的沙漠吸引了許多人的注意。德拉去世後，這片土地（已成為廢墟）被鳳凰城購買。建築結構已修復，仙人掌花園重新種植，場地也開放供遊客參觀。

body.en: Visitors on the rare tours (they occur intermittently every couple of months and usually sell out) get to wander across the Tovreas' desert with its 5,000 plants. Then they are led inside, where they get to peek in the basement and the ground floor of this 1930s palace.
body.zh: 參加罕見旅遊的遊客（每隔幾個月間歇性進行一次，通常門票已售罄）可以漫步穿越托夫雷斯沙漠，那裡有 5,000 種植物。然後他們被帶入內部，參觀這座 1930 年代宮殿的地下室和底層。

address: 5025 E Van Buren Street, Phoenix, Arizona

title.zh: 伊利街，歷史悠久的洛厄爾

excerpt.en: A living snapshot of a different time in America is preserved and maintained by a community of volunteers.
excerpt.zh: 美國不同時期的生動快照由志工社區保存和維護。

body.en: Visiting Erie Street is like walking into a 1950s post-apocalyptic landscape. From all that is immediately apparent, it could have been abandoned in a hurry and forgotten for half a century. Rusting cars, trucks, and an old Greyhound bus sit deserted along the street as if their passengers had suddenly vanished (or worse).
body.zh: 遊覽伊利街就像走進 20 世紀 50 年代的後世界末日景觀。從所有顯而易見的情況來看，它可能會被匆忙拋棄並被遺忘半個世紀。生鏽的汽車、卡車和一輛舊灰狗巴士空蕩蕩地停在街邊，就好像乘客突然消失了（或者更糟）。

body.en: Erie Street is most of what is left of Lowell, Arizona, a mining town incorporated into Bisbee in the early 1900s. Much of the town's residential area was demolished to widen an open-pit copper mine. Losing most of its residents caused the commercial district to struggle, and many businesses failed as a result. Today, the street's special curiosities include a Harley Davidson repair shop with a now-defunct gas pump and Sprouse Reitz Co., a department store that is nearly empty except for a few appliances and a whole pile of mannequin parts.
body.zh: 伊利街 (Erie Street) 是亞利桑那州洛威爾 (Lowell) 的大部分遺跡，洛威爾是一個採礦小鎮，於 1900 年代初期併入比斯比 (Bisbee)。該鎮的大部分住宅區被拆除，以擴大露天銅礦。失去大部分居民導致商業區陷入困境，許多企業因此倒閉。如今，這條街上最令人好奇的地方包括哈雷戴維森 (Harley Davidson) 修理店，其加油站現已廢棄，還有 Sprouse Reitz Co.，這是一家百貨商店，除了一些電器和一大堆人體模型零件外，幾乎空無一人。

body.en: Despite appearing untouched since its decline, further investigation reveals that Erie Street is continually restored by a vibrant and passionate community of residents and volunteers who want to remember a different America. So although you can no longer see a show at Lowell's movie theater or pay $0.22 for gasoline, the Lowell Americana Project has made it possible to experience the street as a living snapshot of another time. And not everything on Erie Street is purely decorative—visit the Bisbee Breakfast Club for an excellent Huevos Rancheros.
body.zh: 儘管自衰落以來，伊利街似乎沒有受到任何影響，但進一步的調查顯示，伊利街不斷被充滿活力和熱情的居民和志願者社區所修復，他們想要記住一個不同的美國。因此，儘管您無法再在洛厄爾電影院觀看演出，也無法再支付 0.22 美元的汽油費，但洛厄爾美國項目卻讓您能夠以另一個時代的生動快照來體驗這條街道。伊利街 (Erie Street) 上的一切並非純粹是裝飾性的，您可以前往 Bisbee Breakfast Club 品嚐美味的 Huevos Rancheros。

body.en: cassidyac
body.zh: 卡西迪亞克

excerpt.en: Walk through the actual strap iron cells and solitary chambers of Arizona Territory’s first prison.
excerpt.zh: 穿過亞利桑那領地第一座監獄的鐵牢牢房和單間牢房。

body.en: On July 1, 1876, the first seven inmates entered the Territorial Prison at Yuma and were locked into the new cells they had built themselves.
body.zh: 1876 年 7 月 1 日，首批七名囚犯進入尤馬地區監獄，並被鎖在他們自己建造的新牢房裡。

body.en: A total of 3,069 prisoners, including 29 women, lived within these walls during the prison's thirty-three years of operation. Among the 29 women sentenced to Yuma was 16-year-old Maria Moreno, who shot her brother after he complained about the way she was dancing. There was also Pearl Hart. Pearl and her partner, Joe Boot, committed the last stagecoach robbery in Arizona. They robbed the Globe stage, and were caught very quickly. Joe Boot was sentenced to 30 years, and would later escape. Pearl Hart, after being tried twice, was given five years.
body.zh: 在監獄運作三十三年期間，共有 3,069 名囚犯，其中包括 29 名女性，居住在這些圍牆內。被判入尤馬監獄的 29 名女性中有 16 歲的瑪麗亞·莫雷諾 (Maria Moreno)，她在哥哥抱怨她跳舞的方式後開槍射殺了她。還有珀爾·哈特。珀爾和她的搭檔喬·布特在亞利桑那州實施了最後一起驛站馬車搶劫案。他們搶劫了環球舞台，很快就被抓獲。喬布特被判處 30 年徒刑，後來越獄。珀爾·哈特在接受兩次審判後被判處五年徒刑。

body.en: The prison was known for its strict rules; weapons, gambling, and fighting were prohibited, as was littering and failing to bathe. Those who broke the rules could be forced to wear the ball and chain and more serious offenders would be sent to the dark cell. The dark cell was basically an excavation in the hillside measuring 15' by 15', with a cage in the center.
body.zh: 該監獄以其嚴格的規則而聞名。武器、賭博和打架都是被禁止的，亂丟垃圾和不洗澡也是被禁止的。那些違反規則的人可能會被強迫戴上球和鍊子，更嚴重的違規者將被送到黑暗的牢房。黑暗牢房基本上是在山坡上挖出的一個 15 英尺乘 15 英尺的坑，中間有一個籠子。

body.en: Now a museum, the building houses photographs and colorful exhibits of those who once stayed there and the prison life they had to endure. Visitors can walk through the many cells and view the infamous dark cell.
body.zh: 該建築現在是一座博物館，裡面陳列著那些曾經住在那裡的人以及他們不得不忍受的監獄生活的照片和豐富多彩的展品。遊客可以穿過許多牢房並參觀臭名昭著的黑暗牢房。

label.en: Felicity, California: Center of the World
label.zh: 加州費利西蒂：世界中心

excerpt.en: Once the product of an inexplicable gold strike, this ghost town is now home to one man and his love of classic machines.
excerpt.zh: 這座鬼城曾經是一次莫名其妙的金礦開採的產物，現在成了一個人和他對經典機器的熱愛的家園。

body.en: In 1890, the Haynes Copper Company sunk a 1200-foot shaft into the middle of one of the richest copper deposits ever discovered. Much to their chagrin, they found no copper. Luckily, they struck gold instead, creating the small boom town of Haynes, the remnants of which are today an intriguing mix of ghost town and mechanical hobbyist's paradise.
body.zh: 1890 年，海恩斯銅礦公司 (Haynes Copper Company) 在有史以來發現的最豐富的銅礦床之一的中部挖了一個 1200 英尺長的豎井。令他們懊惱的是，他們沒有找到銅。幸運的是，他們卻挖到了金子，創造了海恩斯這個新興小鎮，如今，它的遺跡已成為鬼城和機械愛好者天堂的迷人組合。

body.en: While the Gold King Mine Ghost Town boasts a disused mine shaft and antiquated buildings, owner/proprietor Don Robertson is both the source of and a large part of the main attraction. A tinkerer with a knack and an enthusiasm for all things mechanical, Don purchased the site of the abandoned town of Haynes and has turned it into his own gearhead paradise.
body.zh: 雖然金王礦鬼城擁有廢棄的礦井和陳舊的建築，但業主/業主唐羅伯遜 (Don Robertson) 既是主要景點的來源，也是主要景點的重要組成部分。唐是一位擁有訣竅和對所有機械事物充滿熱情的修補匠，他購買了廢棄小鎮海恩斯的場地，並將其變成了自己的齒輪箱天堂。

body.en: The attractions assembled and lovingly cared for by Don Robertson include antique mine equipment still cranking away, as well as a turn-of-the-century sawmill still actively filling orders, a circa 1901 blacksmith shop, classic gas engines, and a wide array of restored antique cars, including vintage trucks and race cars. The open-air museum also features resident animals—including donkeys, rabbits, goats, and chickens—looking for treats and scratches from visitors.
body.zh: 由唐·羅伯遜 (Don Robertson) 組裝和精心維護的景點包括仍在運轉的古董採礦設備、仍在積極履行訂單的世紀之交鋸木廠、大約 1901 年的鐵匠鋪、經典燃氣發動機以及各種經過修復的古董車，包括老式卡車和賽車。露天博物館也飼養一些常駐動物，包括驢子、兔子、山羊和雞，它們正在尋找遊客的零食和抓痕。

body.en: Keep right past the Fire Station; becomes a dirt road pretty quickly.
body.zh: 靠右行駛經過消防局；很快就會變成土路。

excerpt.en: A wild west cemetery in Tombstone, Arizona, provides a window into the Old West.
excerpt.zh: 亞利桑那州墓碑鎮的狂野西部墓地提供了一個了解舊西部的窗口。

body.en: In these modern times, death is portrayed as uncommon and tragic, often hidden from daily life. Contrast that to the rollicking days of the Wild West, where gunfights and hangings were common occurrences in the town square, and it's easy to see how a place like Boothill Graveyard would seem curious now.
body.zh: 在當今時代，死亡被描繪成不尋常和悲劇性的，並且常常隱藏在日常生活中。與狂野西部的熱鬧日子相比，槍戰和絞刑在城鎮廣場上很常見，很容易看出像布特希爾墓地這樣的地方現在會顯得多麼好奇。

body.en: A rocky burying grounds atop a hill in the historic Old West town of Tombstone, Arizona, Boothill Graveyard is a looking glass through which we can see a time and place where death came casually, and even humorously. Weathered wooden signs mark the graves of about 250 men, women, and children who passed, literally, through Tombstone, mostly between 1879-1884.
body.zh: 布特希爾墓園是亞利桑那州歷史悠久的西部小鎮墓碑鎮山頂上的一塊岩石墓地，它就像一面鏡子，透過它，我們可以看到死亡隨意、甚至幽默地降臨的時間和地點。飽經風霜的木牌上刻著約 250 名男女老少的墳墓，幾乎都是在 1879 年至 1884 年間走過墓碑鎮的。

body.en: Although this cemetery and the town that surrounds it are now known as tourist attractions due to their authentic Old West appeal, and because the town was the site of the infamous Gunfight at the O.K. Corral, an interesting aspect of the town's history that isn't discussed as much is the cemetery's integregation of a variety of races and stations in life represented in the same cemetery. Cowboys, Vaqueros, Chinese immigrants, South American immigrants, miners, former slaves, business folk, soldiers, mothers, children, soiled doves, drunks, cattle ranchers, lawmen, and outlaws are all buried, side by side, in Boothill.
body.zh: 儘管這個墓地和它周圍的小鎮現在因其真正的老西部魅力而被稱為旅遊景點，而且因為該鎮是 O.K. 臭名昭著的槍戰地點。科拉爾是該鎮歷史上一個有趣的方面，但沒有被太多討論，那就是該墓地將不同種族和生活地位融合在同一個墓地中。牛仔、牛仔、中國移民、南美洲移民、礦工、前奴隸、商人、士兵、母親、兒童、骯髒的鴿子、酒鬼、牧場主、執法者和亡命之徒都並排埋葬在布特希爾。

body.en: One of the most attended funerals in Boothill's history was actually held for "China Mary", Sing Choy. A competent businesswoman and well liked by the community.
body.zh: 布特希爾歷史上參加人數最多的葬禮之一實際上是為「中國瑪麗」蔡星舉行的。一位有能力的女商人，深受社會的喜愛。

body.en: There is also the Jewish Memorial on site that was set aside especially for Jewish Pioneers. This is interesting, because most western cemeteries of that date range will be absent of Jewish internments alltogether.
body.zh: 現場還有專為猶太拓荒者設立的猶太紀念碑。這很有趣，因為該日期範圍內的大多數西方墓地都不會拘留猶太人。

body.en: Many of the graves are marked as "unknown". Miners and drifters who's names have been lost to time. Graves that are marked mostly tell a blunt tale of how a person came to be deceased. "MURDERED," reads one in outraged capital letters, while another says "Found dead in his cabin with bullet wounds," solemnly giving more detail. It's up to the visitor to examine the distinction between terms like "Hanged" and "Legally Hanged."
body.zh: 許多墳墓被標記為“未知”。礦工和漂流者的名字已被時間遺忘。有標記的墳墓大多講述了一個人如何死亡的直白故事。其中一人用憤怒的大寫字母寫著“被謀殺”，而另一人則嚴肅地提供了更多細節，“被發現死在他的小屋裡，身上有槍傷”。由訪客來檢查「絞刑」和「合法絞刑」等術語之間的區別。

address: Boothill Graveyard, 408 Arizona Hwy 80, Tombstone, Arizona, 85638

excerpt.en: A secret fresh water spring for animals and humans alike hidden along the most famous road in the United States.
excerpt.zh: 隱藏在美國最著名的道路上的一處供動物和人類使用的秘密淡水泉。

body.en: While driving this arid stretch of Route 66, keep your eyes peeled for a staircase built into one of the cliffs. It leads to a secret spring bubbling with life, tucked out of sight along the most famous road in the United States .
body.zh: 在 66 號公路這段乾旱的路段上行駛時，請密切注意懸崖上建有的樓梯。它通往一個充滿活力的秘密泉水，隱藏在美國最著名的道路上看不見的地方。

body.en: A man named Shaffer created this hidden roadside wonder in the 1930s under the Works Progress Administration. While constructing the “Gold Road Section” that weaves between Gold Road Mine and Kingman, Arizona, he noticed water cascading down the cliff walls. To take advantage of the precious resource, he built a basin of stones at its base to allow the water to pool.
body.zh: 1930 年代，一位名叫謝弗 (Shaffer) 的男子在工程振興署 (Works Progress Administration) 的領導下創造了這個隱藏的路邊奇蹟。在建造金路礦和亞利桑那州金曼之間的「黃金路段」時，他注意到水從懸崖壁上傾瀉而下。為了利用這寶貴的資源，他在底部建造了一個石頭盆，以便讓水匯集。

body.en: This minute, secluded oasis soon became a welcome refuge for the weary travelers and parched animals passing through. Because the water stems from a consistent natural source, the bowl remains full year-round. Locals frequently keep it stocked with goldfish (leading some to call it the "fish bowl spring"), and the snails clinging to its walls help keep the algae at bay so the water stays fresh.
body.zh: 這一刻，僻靜的綠洲很快就成為疲憊的旅人和路過的飢餓的動物歡迎的避難所。由於水來自一致的天然水源，因此碗全年保持滿水。當地人經常在其中飼養金魚（因此有些人稱之為“魚碗泉”），而附著在其牆壁上的蝸牛有助於阻止藻類生長，使水保持新鮮。

body.en: Desert-dwelling animals like bees and burros still frequent the site to quench their thirsts. Humans, however, are less common. Only travelers who already know of its existence or those who happen to spot the stairs will ever stumble upon this secret spring.
body.zh: 蜜蜂和驢子等生活在沙漠中的動物仍然經常光顧這裡解渴。然而，人類卻不太常見。只有已經知道它的存在或碰巧發現樓梯的旅行者才會偶然發現這個秘密泉水。

label.zh: 唐勞克林老爺車博物館

excerpt.en: This southwestern historic site was designed and built by an artist who wanted his work to "feel at home."
excerpt.zh: 這座西南歷史遺址是由一位藝術家設計和建造的，他希望他的作品「有賓至如歸的感覺」。

body.en: Starting in the early 1950s, artist Ettore “Ted” DeGrazia decided that he would build a complex that was in itself a devotional work to his beloved southwestern climes, but also as a place where his unique works of art and construction could find a space where they were comfortable.
body.zh: 從 20 世紀 50 年代初開始，藝術家 Ettore “Ted” DeGrazia 決定建造一座綜合體，這座綜合體本身就是對他熱愛的西南氣候的奉獻，同時也是他獨特的藝術和建築作品能夠找到一個舒適空間的地方。

body.en: DeGrazia's family immigrated from Italy in the early 1900s. Ted would purchase 10 acres of land in the foothills of Tucson, Arizona in order to escape the growing population of downtown Tucson. Instead of simply building a new house for he and his wife, the artist set to work designing and building a Spanish mission-style complex where he could both work on his art and integrate it into the space.
body.zh: DeGrazia 的家人於 1900 年代初從義大利移民。特德將在亞利桑那州圖森山麓購買 10 英畝土地，以逃離圖森市中心不斷增長的人口。這位藝術家並沒有簡單地為他和妻子建造一座新房子，而是開始設計和建造一座西班牙傳教式建築群，在那裡他既可以創作自己的藝術作品，又可以將其融入空間中。

body.en: Along with a group of friends, DeGrazia built the original "Mission in the Sun" using adobe bricks that they made themselves on-site. He dedicated the space to the Virgin of Guadalupe and his uniquely southwestern vision began coming to fruition. Once his naturally inspired constructions were complete, the gallery and mission were opened to the public in 1965. After completing the mission, DeGrazia built a gallery space nearby in the same style in which he could his display his steady stream of paintings among the traditional adobe style that so inspired him. Once his naturally inspired constructions were complete, the gallery and mission were opened to the public in 1965.
body.zh: 德格拉齊亞與一群朋友一起，用他們在現場製作的土坯磚建造了最初的“陽光下的使命”。他將這個空間獻給瓜達露佩聖母，他獨特的西南願景開始實現。當他的自然靈感建築完成後，畫廊和使命於 1965 年向公眾開放。完成使命後，德格拉齊亞在附近以相同的風格建造了一個畫廊空間，他可以在其中展示他源源不斷的傳統土坯風格的繪畫作品，這給他帶來了靈感。當他的自然靈感建築完成後，畫廊和教堂於 1965 年向公眾開放。

body.en: Today the site remains as one of the most quintessentially southwestern locations in the American desert and is now a protected historic site, preserving not only countless of DeGrazia's works, but also his dream of a bygone desert culture.
body.zh: 如今，該遺址仍然是美國沙漠中最典型的西南地點之一，現在是受保護的歷史遺址，不僅保存了德格拉齊亞的無數作品，還保存了他對過去沙漠文化的夢想。

excerpt.en: The eroded core of an ancient volcano is now accessible by a short hike.
excerpt.zh: 現在只需短途健行即可到達一座古老火山被侵蝕的核心。

body.en: Approximately 740,000 years ago, a volcanic eruption blasted out the side of a cinder cone volcano in what is now northern Arizona. The volcano is part of the San Francisco Volcanic Field, an 1,800-square-mile area that is crowded with evidence of volcanic activity as recent as 1,000 years ago.
body.zh: 大約 74 萬年前，一場火山爆發了一座火山渣錐火山的側面，該火山位於現在的亞利桑那州北部。該火山是舊金山火山場的一部分，該火山場佔地 1,800 平方英里，充滿了 1,000 年前火山活動的證據。

body.en: There are over 600 volcanoes in the area between Flagstaff, Arizona, and the Grand Canyon. What makes Red Mountain unique is that its eruption blew out the side of the mountain, leaving it as an odd U-shape and presenting an impressive amphitheater of otherworldly pillars of stone and volcanic materials.
body.zh: 亞利桑那州弗拉格斯塔夫和大峽谷之間的地區有 600 多座火山。紅山的獨特之處在於，它的噴發炸毀了山的一側，使其成為一個奇怪的 U 形，並呈現出一個令人印象深刻的圓形劇場，由超凡脫俗的石柱和火山材料組成。

body.en: Passed by unnoticed by most tourists en route to the Grand Canyon, the trail up to the core of Red Mountain gently climbs up 300 feet in elevation and presents hikers with views of the transition in ecosystems from pinyon and juniper desert scrubland to high-elevation ponderosa pine forests.
body.zh: 大多數遊客在前往大峽谷的途中都會經過，這條通往紅山核心的小路緩緩上升 300 英尺的海拔，為徒步旅行者提供了從松林和杜松沙漠灌叢到高海拔黃松林的生態系統轉變的景觀。

body.en: The trail between the parking area and the amphitheater of Red Mountain is an easy 3-mile hike roundtrip. Near the end of the trail there is a small ladder built into a rise that goes up 6 feet. If hiking during the summer, be sure to bring plenty of water.
body.zh: 停車場和紅山露天劇場之間的步道是 3 英里的輕鬆徒步往返路線。在步道盡頭附近有一個小梯子，建在 6 英尺高的高地上。如果在夏季健行，一定要帶足水。

excerpt.en: A small canyon with petroglyphs and a seasonal waterfall, only a short hike from the remnants of old Route 66.
excerpt.zh: 這是一座小峽谷，擁有岩畫和季節性瀑布，距離舊 66 號公路遺跡僅幾步之遙。

body.en: For centuries, the canyon and pool now known as Keyhole Sink was a place where the Cohonina people hunted and conducted religious ceremonies. Petroglyphs at the site dating to around 1,000 years ago indicate that hunters used the natural dead-end to corner prey that gathered at the watering hole. Curiously, despite the area being a rare source of fresh water in the arid region, archaeological evidence doesn't indicate that people settled permanently at the site.
body.zh: 幾個世紀以來，現在被稱為鑰匙孔水槽的峽谷和水池是科霍尼納人狩獵和舉行宗教儀式的地方。該遺址的岩畫可以追溯到大約 1000 年前，獵人利用大自然的死胡同將聚集在水坑的獵物逼入絕境。奇怪的是，儘管該地區是乾旱地區稀有的淡水來源，但考古證據並未顯示人們在此永久定居。

body.en: The images marked onto the volcanic basalt rock mostly show animals that were probably encountered at the watering hole—deer, snakes, frogs, and lizards. One image depicts a herd of deer entering the canyon. These pictures were made by the Cohonina, who lived in the area from around 700 to 1100. Anthropologists believe that the Cohonina are the ancestors of today's Navajo, Hopi, and Zuni tribes, among others.
body.zh: 火山玄武岩上標記的圖像主要顯示了可能在水坑中遇到的動物——鹿、蛇、青蛙和蜥蜴。一張圖片描繪了一群鹿進入峽谷。這些照片是由科霍尼納人拍攝的，他們在 700 年至 1100 年間居住在該地區。人類學家認為，科霍尼納人是當今納瓦霍人、霍皮人和祖尼部落等的祖先。

body.en: In 2010 the petroglyphs were heavily damaged by vandals who drew on the wall of the canyon with aluminum roofing cement. The vandalism made national news and an expert from Atlanta , Georgia, was recruited to help restore the site. They were able to remove almost all evidence of the vandalism from the petroglyph panels, and today hidden cameras monitor the site.
body.zh: 2010 年，破壞者用鋁製屋頂水泥在峽谷壁上塗鴉，導致岩畫嚴重受損。這次破壞行為成為全國新聞，來自喬治亞州亞特蘭大的一位專家被聘請來幫助修復該遺址。他們能夠從岩畫板上清除幾乎所有破壞行為的證據，如今隱藏的攝影機監視著該地點。

body.en: The trailhead is on the shoulder of the historic Route 66, a few miles west of Parks, Arizona. Parking for the trailhead is on the other side of the highway, in the Oak Hill Snow Play area. The trail is easy, and goes about a mile from the highway.
body.zh: 步道起點位於歷史悠久的 66 號公路的路肩上，位於亞利桑那州帕克斯以西幾英里處。步道起點的停車場位於高速公路的另一側，橡樹山雪地遊樂區。這條路很容易，距離高速公路大約一英里。

excerpt.en: This rustic cabin, outfitted with gun slits, was once home to John D. Tewksbury, patriarch of the bloodiest family feud in American history.
excerpt.zh: This rustic cabin, outfitted with gun slits, was once home to John D. Tewksbury, patriarch of the bloodiest family feud in American history.

body.en: Even the architecture of this small, humble structure hints at violence. This Flying “V” Cabin, built in 1880 seems to lack windows, but on closer inspection you see that there are small slits throughout the cabin. These were not designed to let sunlight in but to let gunfire out. In place of windows there are gun ports.
body.zh: Even the architecture of this small, humble structure hints at violence. This Flying “V” Cabin, built in 1880 seems to lack windows, but on closer inspection you see that there are small slits throughout the cabin. These were not designed to let sunlight in but to let gunfire out. In place of windows there are gun ports.

body.en: The Flying V Cabin has since been moved to the Pioneer Living History Museum in Pioneer Arizona, but it was originally located in Pleasant Valley and was home to John Tewksbury, Sr. Whether you call it the Pleasant Valley War or the Tewksbury-Graham Feud the resident of that small cabin was at the center of a family war that lasted six years and had the largest death toll of any family feud in US history. By the end of the battle nearly every male in both families was dead.

By the end of the battle nearly every male in both families was dead.

body.en: John Tewksbury, Sr., the resident of the Flying V Cabin, was part Indian and was the patriarch of the Tewksbury clan. However it would be his sons who undertook the battles in the Tewksbury-Graham Feud.
body.zh: John Tewksbury, Sr., the resident of the Flying V Cabin, was part Indian and was the patriarch of the Tewksbury clan. However it would be his sons who undertook the battles in the Tewksbury-Graham Feud.

body.en: The family feud started like so many others before it. Two neighbors, friends at first, slowly fall into a dispute. It was John Tewksbury, Sr himself who invited Tom Graham out to Arizona to begin ranching. Soon however, even the vast expanse of the Southwest began to feel cramped. Both families started accusing the others of stealing horses and cattle. Egged on by a third rancher named James Stinson, the arguments and accusations turned to arrest warrants.
body.zh: The family feud started like so many others before it. Two neighbors, friends at first, slowly fall into a dispute. It was John Tewksbury, Sr himself who invited Tom Graham out to Arizona to begin ranching. Soon however, even the vast expanse of the Southwest began to feel cramped. Both families started accusing the others of stealing horses and cattle. Egged on by a third rancher named James Stinson, the arguments and accusations turned to arrest warrants.

body.en: An attempt to settle some of the issues in person quickly turned into a shoot out. In 1885 a Basque sheepherder was killed and robbed by a member of the Graham clan, and suddenly the entire valley took sides. For the next three years it was all out war.
body.zh: An attempt to settle some of the issues in person quickly turned into a shoot out. In 1885 a Basque sheepherder was killed and robbed by a member of the Graham clan, and suddenly the entire valley took sides. For the next three years it was all out war.

body.en: The Tewksbury-Graham Feud became wildly complicated, involving multiple other ranchers, hired hands, and the investors of both rancher families. In one incident a 19-year-old scout, who was attempting to rally support for the Graham side was captured by a bounty hunter hiding in a cave, who was then killed by an Apache who was stalking the bounty hunter, at which point the Apache was immediately shot by the 19-year-old scout. A group of cowboys called the Hashknife outfit got involved and quickly gained a reputation as the "thievinist, fightinest bunch of cowboys” in the U.S. People were beheaded, ranches were burned to the ground, an assassin was hired, and lynchings, murders, and shootouts became commonplace. The Tewksbury-Graham Feud played like a super-cut of spaghetti Westerns climaxes.

excerpt.en: Colossal Cave's human history is as intriguing as its geology.
excerpt.zh: Colossal Cave's human history is as intriguing as its geology.

body.en: Just outside of Vail, Arizona , is what is believed to be the largest known dry cave in the United States . Its human history is just as fascinating as its geology.
body.zh: Just outside of Vail, Arizona , is what is believed to be the largest known dry cave in the United States . Its human history is just as fascinating as its geology.

body.en: The mummified bodies of two members of the Hohokam Nation were discovered in Colossal Cave. Local folklore and historic sources also indicate it has been used at least once as a hideout by train robbers, who allegedly stashed gold within its depths.
body.zh: The mummified bodies of two members of the Hohokam Nation were discovered in Colossal Cave. Local folklore and historic sources also indicate it has been used at least once as a hideout by train robbers, who allegedly stashed gold within its depths.

body.en: It would’ve made a great hideout spot, too, as Colossal Cave extends approximately 600 feet into the mountain. It’s considered a dry or dead cave because the water source is no longer active, and as a result, the cave’s geological features are no longer growing.
body.zh: It would’ve made a great hideout spot, too, as Colossal Cave extends approximately 600 feet into the mountain. It’s considered a dry or dead cave because the water source is no longer active, and as a result, the cave’s geological features are no longer growing.

body.en: The geological formations within the cave are quite impressive, though some have been damaged by relic seekers in the past. It’s is also quite comfortable, as the interior temperature remains at a nearly uniform 71 degrees Fahrenheit throughout the year. The fact that Colossal Cave is “fixed in time” and no longer living makes it quite a unique place to visit and tour.
body.zh: The geological formations within the cave are quite impressive, though some have been damaged by relic seekers in the past. It’s is also quite comfortable, as the interior temperature remains at a nearly uniform 71 degrees Fahrenheit throughout the year. The fact that Colossal Cave is “fixed in time” and no longer living makes it quite a unique place to visit and tour.

body.en: Though previously known to Native Americans, Colossal Cave didn’t gain attention from the colonial settlers until a man named Solomon Lick stumbled upon it in 1879. Prior to 1912, the cave was known by several names, including Five Mile Cave, Arizona Catacombs, and Mountain Springs Cave.
body.zh: Though previously known to Native Americans, Colossal Cave didn’t gain attention from the colonial settlers until a man named Solomon Lick stumbled upon it in 1879. Prior to 1912, the cave was known by several names, including Five Mile Cave, Arizona Catacombs, and Mountain Springs Cave.

body.en: During the Depression Era, the Civilian Conservation Corps made improvements to the cave so that it was easier to provide tours. The cave has also been used as the backdrop for a number of low budget films.

excerpt.zh: This small, unassuming street is now a canvas for color and creativity.

body.en: Wander around the outskirts of Phoenix , Arizona , and you'll come across an alley flanked by wonderful, elaborate murals created by local artists.
body.zh: Wander around the outskirts of Phoenix , Arizona , and you'll come across an alley flanked by wonderful, elaborate murals created by local artists.

body.en: Some of the images showcase scenes from the city, its history, and its people. Others reference popular culture or reflect the artists' own unique designs.
body.zh: Some of the images showcase scenes from the city, its history, and its people. Others reference popular culture or reflect the artists' own unique designs.

body.en: Every year, a festival is held to celebrate this street, where artists add new murals to the existing collection. Dozens of artists descend upon the alley, which continues to serve as a canvas for their creativity. It's a way for the people of Phoenix to bring quite a few splashes of color to their concrete desert oasis.

excerpt.en: A former department store turned into a quirky restaurant.
excerpt.zh: A former department store turned into a quirky restaurant.

body.en: In a restaurant with a name like “Hanny’s”, one would usually expect Hanny to be the owner, or perhaps the chef. But that's not the case here—the restaurant draws its name from Vic Hanny, a department store proprietor who built the store decades ago. Looking closely, you'll see the walls of the restaurant are covered in original Hanny’s logos and advertisements for menswear.
body.zh: In a restaurant with a name like “Hanny’s”, one would usually expect Hanny to be the owner, or perhaps the chef. But that's not the case here—the restaurant draws its name from Vic Hanny, a department store proprietor who built the store decades ago. Looking closely, you'll see the walls of the restaurant are covered in original Hanny’s logos and advertisements for menswear.

body.en: The building was constructed in 1947 by architects Royal Lescher and Leslie Mahoney, as a late example of the “International Style” of architecture. Upon its completion, the Arizona Times praised it for bringing a “new look” to the city as a modern department store. After its closing in 1986, Hanny’s was purchased by the city of Phoenix and used to train firefighters.
body.zh: The building was constructed in 1947 by architects Royal Lescher and Leslie Mahoney, as a late example of the “International Style” of architecture. Upon its completion, the Arizona Times praised it for bringing a “new look” to the city as a modern department store. After its closing in 1986, Hanny’s was purchased by the city of Phoenix and used to train firefighters.

body.en: The old Hanny’s building was purchased by Karl Kopp in 2005. Kopp understood the appeal in giving his restaurants an unconventional style. So, instead of concealing its past as a department store, he kept much of the original, fading decor, as well as an original elevator shaft with a glass bottom.
body.zh: The old Hanny’s building was purchased by Karl Kopp in 2005. Kopp understood the appeal in giving his restaurants an unconventional style. So, instead of concealing its past as a department store, he kept much of the original, fading decor, as well as an original elevator shaft with a glass bottom.

body.en: Kopp also added some new features: weird bathrooms, and an unnamed horned mannequin covered in a mosaic of colorful objects. If you’re looking for something unsettling, head on down to the basement, with its collection of creepy dolls. Legend says that these dolls move from time to time—whether this is simply a trick of artistry or actual paranormal activity is up for debate.

excerpt.en: This collection of neon icons is preserving Arizona's history, one sign at a time.
excerpt.zh: This collection of neon icons is preserving Arizona's history, one sign at a time.

body.en: Signs, signs, everywhere are signs—at the Ignite Sign Art Museum in Tucson's Arroyo Chico neighborhood. What's so special about this collection is the sheer variety of signs on display. There's neon, electric, hand-painted, aluminum, and LED. They run the gamut from historic neon signs to a rescued 76 gas station ball. There are signs from local mom-and-pop grocery stores displayed next to an enormous Arby's hat. It's an eclectic and unexpected assortment, just like Tucson itself.
body.zh: Signs, signs, everywhere are signs—at the Ignite Sign Art Museum in Tucson's Arroyo Chico neighborhood. What's so special about this collection is the sheer variety of signs on display. There's neon, electric, hand-painted, aluminum, and LED. They run the gamut from historic neon signs to a rescued 76 gas station ball. There are signs from local mom-and-pop grocery stores displayed next to an enormous Arby's hat. It's an eclectic and unexpected assortment, just like Tucson itself.

body.en: The Ignite museum started as the personal collection of Jude Cook, who has spent his life in the design and sign industry. His work is familiar to any Tucsonan; his company built the city's iconic neon saguaro at Main Street and Drachman, and restored beloved historic signs including the Tropicana, the Picarretta-Davis diving girl, and the Canyon State Motor Lodge.
body.zh: The Ignite museum started as the personal collection of Jude Cook, who has spent his life in the design and sign industry. His work is familiar to any Tucsonan; his company built the city's iconic neon saguaro at Main Street and Drachman, and restored beloved historic signs including the Tropicana, the Picarretta-Davis diving girl, and the Canyon State Motor Lodge.

body.en: Over the course of 40 years, Cook collected signs from across Arizona and the U.S., and acquired a reputation as the person to call when you needed an old sign hauled off quick. After his collection grew too large to store, he decided to put it on display for everyone to enjoy. Ignite Sign Art Museum opened to the public in 2018.

body.en: Visit Ignite on a typical day and you'll see signs in various states of repair and refurbishment. It's a rare opportunity to see what goes into bringing these iconic (and fragile) American icons back to life.

excerpt.zh: This collection of Wild West movie memorabilia also claims to hold some secrets of the Lost Dutchman's mine.

body.en: At the foot of the Superstition Mountains, the Superstition Mountain Museum is a tourist trap in the middle of the Arizona desert that remembers the filming of a number of Western films as well as exploring the legend of the Lost Dutchman's mine. Also, Elvis weddings.
body.zh: At the foot of the Superstition Mountains, the Superstition Mountain Museum is a tourist trap in the middle of the Arizona desert that remembers the filming of a number of Western films as well as exploring the legend of the Lost Dutchman's mine. Also, Elvis weddings.

body.en: Most of the old movie sets that once made up an extensive open-air museum known as "Apacheland" burned up in a fire in 2004, however two of the original buildings from the Apacheland attraction were moved to the Superstitions mountains site.
body.zh: Most of the old movie sets that once made up an extensive open-air museum known as "Apacheland" burned up in a fire in 2004, however two of the original buildings from the Apacheland attraction were moved to the Superstitions mountains site.

body.en: The Audie Murphy Apacheland Barn houses a number of horse-drawn buggies and carts used in the 17 television series, 29 full-length feature films, and hundreds of commercials filmed on the site. Scattered around the grounds are a few kitschy Old West scenes and full-size dioramas, complete with plenty creepy old mannequins. If you have a little change in your pocket, you can even try to toss a coin or two into the open mouth of the barber/dentist’s patient, posed with his plastic mouth wide open.

If you have a little change in your pocket, you can even try to toss a coin or two into the open mouth of the barber/dentist’s patient, posed with his plastic mouth wide open.

body.en: Just a stone’s throw away is the Elvis Chapel, a mini-museum and wedding chapel dedicated to “the King” and his unique western movie “Charro!” also filmed on site.
body.zh: Just a stone’s throw away is the Elvis Chapel, a mini-museum and wedding chapel dedicated to “the King” and his unique western movie “Charro!” also filmed on site.

body.en: The museum devoted to the area itself is tucked behind the gift shop through an indoor iron gate and for a $5 fee you can go in and see a taxidermy display of native wildlife in action poses and a number of displays about life in the region.
body.zh: The museum devoted to the area itself is tucked behind the gift shop through an indoor iron gate and for a $5 fee you can go in and see a taxidermy display of native wildlife in action poses and a number of displays about life in the region.

body.en: Of special note are the crudely engraved local sandstone blocks. These are known as the Peralta Stones, widely believed to be key pieces in the search for the Lost Dutchman Mine. This legendary mine’s location has been unknown since the death of its most famous owner, a Dutchman who lived in the 1800's. He allegedly stumbled on the mine, shot the owners, and died late in life after giving only a list of cryptic clues as to the location of his incredibly lucrative gold mine. Generations of searchers have scoured the Superstitions and several have died in the search, with at least five deaths confirmed over the past 150 years. excerpt.en: One of the world's largest telescopes, stares into the night sky with two huge mirrors.
excerpt.zh: One of the world's largest telescopes, stares into the night sky with two huge mirrors.

body.en: Binocular vision, binocular being Latin for double eye, is an amazing trait. So valuable is having double eye vision that all animals have two eyes or more. The first reason being that if you lose one eye you have a spare, the second being that it greatly expands your field of vision. In humans, among many other animals, this binocular vision is taken a step further by having our two eyes both point forward. While this gives us a narrower field of vision than say, a bird, it also gives us a special ability, stereopsis or the ability to see one image with depth perception.

In humans, among many other animals, this binocular vision is taken a step further by having our two eyes both point forward. While this gives us a narrower field of vision than say, a bird, it also gives us a special ability, stereopsis or the ability to see one image with depth perception.

body.en: In the world of telescopes, having two eyes has just as many advantages. The LBT or large binocular telescope is currently considered the largest telescope in the world, and while it does not have the largest single mirror, what it does have is two very large -- each 27ft across and weighing 17.7 metric tons each -- mirrors positioned next to each other like giant eyes. Together the mirrors allow for the combined resolution of a 75ft telescope, the light gathering surface of a single 39ft mirror and a better clarity, than the Hubble Space Telescope, which is of course located IN space.

body.en: Situated in the Arizona Pinaleno Mountains, (Arizona is the location a disproportionate number of telescopes, presumably in part because of the geography and weather) the huge LBT, which cost over $120 million to build, had its massive mirrors crafted in the University of Arizona's nearby Steward Observatory Mirror Lab one of the few places in the world where over 20 tons of glass can be heated red hot and spun into a perfect parabola at roughly 2,130 degrees. They then polish the glass to a level of accuracy that is "3,000 times thinner than a human hair."

body.en: Though there was some controversy during the building, involving both the local Native American San Carlos Apache tribe and environmentalists who were concerned about a species of endangered squirrel, by the time the telescope got to work with both mirrors in (known in the telescope as "seeing first light") January 2008 most of the concerns had died down or been resolved.

excerpt.en: From working out of his garage to the James Beard semifinals, one Tucson baker has kept his fan base—and his grains—local.
excerpt.zh: From working out of his garage to the James Beard semifinals, one Tucson baker has kept his fan base—and his grains—local.

body.en: In 2009, Don Guerra was a grade-school teacher with a yearning for bread. He had previously given up the baking life for grad school. But almost a decade into his teaching career, Guerra found himself longing for the feeling of dough in his hands. So he did what many a fledgling founder does: He set up shop in his garage.
body.zh: In 2009, Don Guerra was a grade-school teacher with a yearning for bread. He had previously given up the baking life for grad school. But almost a decade into his teaching career, Guerra found himself longing for the feeling of dough in his hands. So he did what many a fledgling founder does: He set up shop in his garage.

body.en: His first customers and supporters were his neighbors. It's this rootedness in community that motivated Guerra to name his bakery Barrio , after the Spanish word for "neighborhood." Like the bakery's origins, Guerra's ingredients are literally rooted in the community. While his lineup includes traditional European loaves familiar to Great British Bake Off fans, such as olive fougasse , the grains he uses are largely local, either wheats that have learned to thrive in the arid Arizona desert after centuries of adaptation, or native plants.
body.zh: His first customers and supporters were his neighbors. It's this rootedness in community that motivated Guerra to name his bakery Barrio , after the Spanish word for "neighborhood." Like the bakery's origins, Guerra's ingredients are literally rooted in the community. While his lineup includes traditional European loaves familiar to Great British Bake Off fans, such as olive fougasse , the grains he uses are largely local, either wheats that have learned to thrive in the arid Arizona desert after centuries of adaptation, or native plants.

body.en: Guerra's most famous loaves are evidence of this fusion. His Saturday morning Barrio Mesquite loaf, made with wheat and mesquite flour, bears the spicy taste of the desert. His Pan de Kino , meanwhile, is made with White Sonora, a desert-adapted heritage wheat introduced to southern Arizona in the late 1600s by a Spanish missionary, which is grown especially for Barrio by a local farm. Most iconic among his offerings is the Heritage loaf, distinguished by its blend of native desert grains and the signature stenciled-in saguaro that decorates it. The local environment even plays a key role in the baking process, literally causing Barrio's breads to rise: They are made not from commercial yeast, but from "natural leavening," or a sourdough starter, whose fermentation incorporates ambient yeast and bacteria.

The local environment even plays a key role in the baking process, literally causing Barrio's breads to rise: They are made not from commercial yeast, but from "natural leavening," or a sourdough starter, whose fermentation incorporates ambient yeast and bacteria.

body.en: Guerra's commitment to all things local hasn't stopped him from receiving national recognition, however. In 2019, he was a semifinalist for the Outstanding Baker James Beard award , the Oscar of bread. But more than any award, the proof is in the pudding—or in the Desert Durum loaf. Venture to Barrio Bread on a weekend morning, and you'll see a line of locals snaking around the corner of his shop, each hungry aspirant waiting for a crusty, earthy slice of Tucson.

excerpt.zh: This public square capitalized on a single Eagles reference to bring some life back to an Arizona town.

body.en: Winslow, Arizona was once the largest town in the northern part of the state, but after the traffic from Route 66 dried up the town fell into a depression that only an Eagles song could fix.
body.zh: Winslow, Arizona was once the largest town in the northern part of the state, but after the traffic from Route 66 dried up the town fell into a depression that only an Eagles song could fix.

body.en: During the heyday of tourism along America's historic Route 66, Winslow was a well known spot among the arid Arizona expanse. So well known in fact that the band dads love, and everyone else loves to hate, the Eagles, mentioned the town in their classic rock staple, Take It Easy . Unfortunately things weren't easy for very much longer in Winslow as the trans-national I-40 highway finally opened and their stretch of Route 66 was no longer the necessary thoroughfare it once was. Once the road closed, so did a number of businesses in the town, making the future look bleak.
body.zh: During the heyday of tourism along America's historic Route 66, Winslow was a well known spot among the arid Arizona expanse. So well known in fact that the band dads love, and everyone else loves to hate, the Eagles, mentioned the town in their classic rock staple, Take It Easy . Unfortunately things weren't easy for very much longer in Winslow as the trans-national I-40 highway finally opened and their stretch of Route 66 was no longer the necessary thoroughfare it once was. Once the road closed, so did a number of businesses in the town, making the future look bleak.

body.en: Luckily a local group looking to reinvigorate the town remembered the reference in the Eagles song and had the idea to capitalize on it. Thus Standin' On the Corner Park was born. Bringing the scene from the song to life, a bronze statue of a musician in 70's garb stands on the corner with his instrument on his toe. Painted on the brick wall behind him is a tromp l'oeil mural of a woman in a pickup truck reflected in a storefront window. The entire effect is to bring the song's easy breezy story to life.

body.en: The plan worked and Standin' On the Corner Park is now a popular roadside attraction along the now historic Route 66 road, bringing new tourism to the area and allowing a number of local businesses to reopen. Winslow can once again, take it easy.

excerpt.en: Bootleggers ran booze beneath this building before (and after) Route 66 appeared beside it.
excerpt.zh: Bootleggers ran booze beneath this building before (and after) Route 66 appeared beside it.

body.en: A contoured neon martini, sandwiched by the words "Package Goods," beckons travelers along Route 66 in Williams, Arizona. Below the glow, the Sultana Bar—situated in a town best known as the gateway to the Grand Canyon—touts itself as "World Famous." In terms of longevity, they've got a point: This dive opened in 1912, 14 years before the historic highway on which it stands.
body.zh: A contoured neon martini, sandwiched by the words "Package Goods," beckons travelers along Route 66 in Williams, Arizona. Below the glow, the Sultana Bar—situated in a town best known as the gateway to the Grand Canyon—touts itself as "World Famous." In terms of longevity, they've got a point: This dive opened in 1912, 14 years before the historic highway on which it stands.

body.en: As an article from the Phoenix New Times elaborates, the Sultana "traces its roots to a time when ranching, logging, and the Santa Fe Railroad were the big games in town." Desperados originally designed tunnels underneath the bar for drug-running—namely, opium—but were called upon with new purpose when Prohibition created a sudden demand for clandestine booze stockpiles across the United States. Above-ground, guests wandered a less harrowing passageway, which brought them to a theater that screened silent films prior to World War I.

Above-ground, guests wandered a less harrowing passageway, which brought them to a theater that screened silent films prior to World War I.

body.en: Though visitors can (and should) still access the theater through this passage, the space now operates as a special events hall. Pool tables occupy the center of the main bar, and a modern jukebox sits backed against the wall. Beside the flat screens, a stuffed cougar gazes past the massive American flag hanging from the ceiling. Beer is the overarching theme of all lighting, signage, taps, bottles, and cans. Even the term "package goods" (alcohol sealed and labeled in its original container, as distributed by the manufacturer) refers to the bygone practice of bartenders selling booze for the road.

excerpt.en: One of the oldest Mexican restaurants in the United States air-dries its trademark beef in a dangling outdoor cage.
excerpt.zh: One of the oldest Mexican restaurants in the United States air-dries its trademark beef in a dangling outdoor cage.

body.en: Tradition is important at El Charro Cafe. Founded in 1922, it claims to be the oldest Mexican restaurant in the United States that's been continually operated by the same family. In that time, generations of chefs have passed down and perfected some seriously delicious recipes. The most important of these menu items can be seen drying in a dangling cage outside the restaurant every day.
body.zh: Tradition is important at El Charro Cafe. Founded in 1922, it claims to be the oldest Mexican restaurant in the United States that's been continually operated by the same family. In that time, generations of chefs have passed down and perfected some seriously delicious recipes. The most important of these menu items can be seen drying in a dangling cage outside the restaurant every day.

body.en: The dangling delicacy is El Charro’s carne seca . The jerky-like product starts as thinly sliced beef that gets marinated in garlic and lemon juice, then hoisted in the metal cage for a day’s worth of drying in the hot Sonoran sun. After baking further in an oven, the hard beef is then shredded into pillowy mounds of meat that adorn dishes ranging from tacos to enchiladas to cheese crisps.
